x: The Bay Weekender San Francisco & the Bay Area Edition of Monday, October 26, 2026 Coverage: October 26 to November 29 59 events In this edition At a Glance Pick of the Month The Map The Calendar Music, Arts & Nightlife Food, Drink & Festivals Outdoors, Sports & Active On the Horizon At a Glance Five weeks, three holidays, and one deadline this Saturday This is a long window and it has a clear shape. It opens with Halloween landing on a Saturday, which has pushed almost every good party indoors and spread the rest across both Friday and Saturday night. Then comes the real centre of the edition: November 2, when the Mission builds several hundred altars in a park and walks 24th Street by candlelight, and Oakland closes nine blocks of Fruitvale the day before. There are seven separate Day of the Dead observances here across four counties, and six of the seven are free. After that the window turns athletic. The Warriors come home 0-3 for the longest homestand of their season, nine Chase Center dates in all. The Earthquakes play two final home matches with playoff seeding still live, and Bay FC says goodbye to a hard year on November 1. Then the holiday machinery starts: a coffee festival, a tea festival, a chocolate salon, Dickens Fair, Lightscape, and four turkey trots in four counties on Thanksgiving morning. One thing needs deciding this week rather than later. Dickens Fair's Early Bird pricing, which covers the opening weekends and saves ten dollars a head, is only on sale through October 31. Weekend weather Cool, grey, and a real chance of rain on Halloween The National Weather Service's Bay Area forecast, issued Monday morning, puts San Francisco in the upper 50s on Saturday with a chance of rain, and the lower 60s on Sunday with a slight chance. Inland bay shoreline runs a few degrees warmer. There is also a coastal flood advisory in effect through Thursday afternoon, which matters for anything near the Embarcadero or Aquatic Park at high tide. Costumes on Saturday want a coat over them. Act now Four clocks running By Saturday October 31. Dickens Fair Early Bird tickets, $40 adult rather than $50, valid only on the opening weekends. Sold out already. Brandi Carlile and Jessie Reyez at the Fox, Tuba Skinny and Haley Heynderickx at the Freight, Weston Estate at The Independent. Closing. SOMArts' Day of the Dead exhibition ends November 20. The Iturbide retrospective at SFMOMA ends November 29. Book ahead. Free Saturday museum entry for Bay Area residents needs an advance timed ticket, and the slots do run out. Pick of the Month Day of the Dead in the Mission Festival of Altars and the Ritual Procession, Monday November 2 Two events, one evening, and they are designed to be done together. From ten in the morning the community builds altars in Potrero del Sol Park, with a ceremony at sunset and a performance at eight. At seven the procession gathers at Bryant and 22nd and walks toward 24th Street with drums, Aztec dancers and several thousand people moving mostly in silence. Food vendors line the procession route rather than the park. Both are free. Why this one Most of what fills a five-week calendar can be caught again next year, or next month, or in another city. This cannot. The Marigold Project has run the Festival of Altars for more than three decades and it only works on November 2, only in that neighbourhood, and only because a few thousand people show up and build it themselves. It costs nothing, it asks something of you, and it is the single most San Francisco thing happening between now and December. Bring a photograph of someone you have lost. Indoor options are doing well. Cold Cave solo, with SRSQ Fri Oct 30 · $22 to $90 Wesley Eisold plays stripped-down darkwave on the best bill of Halloween weekend. A five-act night of Bay and Texas darkwave: Cold Cave in solo configuration, SRSQ, Houses of Heaven, False Figure and a.cold.era. The early door is the thing to notice here, with the show starting at 6:30pm rather than the usual nine, so the whole bill is done in time to go elsewhere. The Great American's balcony is the move if you want to actually see the stage. The museum's after-dark series goes full costume for Halloween Eve, with DJs in Wilsey Court and gallery access included. It is the rare SF party where you can see Treasures of the Pharaohs and then dance in front of it. VIP adds early entry and a separate bar, which matters because the main bar lines get long by ten. Friday brings Mindex in support, Saturday brings Supersillyus, and the Halloween-night crowd dresses for it in a way few other shows in the Bay can match. The Fox is a 2,800-capacity former movie palace with a standing floor, so arrive early if you want the rail. Dia de Muertos Celebracion at La Pena Sun Nov 1 · Free, donations encouraged Son jarocho, an ofrenda and Latin American home cooking in Berkeley. Free entry. La Pena has been the Bay Area's Latin American cultural center since 1975, and its Day of the Dead night is small, warm and entirely unhurried. The ceremony is around 5:30pm, with son jarocho music after. Admission is free with donations encouraged; food and drink are sold inside, and the kitchen is the real draw. Event and ticket details Day of the Dead Festival of Altars ★ Mon Nov 2 · Free, donations welcomed Hundreds of candlelit ofrendas fill a Mission park. Free, and the best night of the window. The Marigold Project has run this for more than three decades: the community builds altars for its dead through the day, a ceremony happens at sunset, and the park turns into a field of candles and marigolds after dark. It is not a street fair and it is not a parade. Come quietly, bring a photograph of someone if you want to add to an altar, and eat from the vendors along the procession route rather than in the park itself. When Monday November 2 Time Altar building from 10:00am, sunset ceremony 5:00pm, performance 8:00pm Where Potrero del Sol Park , Mission 2650 25th Street, San Francisco, CA 94110 Price Free, donations welcomed Times per KQED's 2026 guide, not the organizer's own page If it rains. Outdoors and goes ahead in light rain. Candles struggle in wind, so the ceremony can shift inside the park's sheltered corners. Event and ticket details Day of the Dead Ritual Procession Mon Nov 2 · Free The Mission's candlelit procession gathers at Bryant and 22nd and walks 24th Street. The procession is the moving half of November 2 in the Mission: Aztec dancers, drums, painted faces and several thousand people walking in silence or close to it. Food vendors line 24th Street rather than the park, so this is where you eat. It ends at the Festival of Altars, so do both in one evening. When Monday November 2 Time 7:00pm Where Bryant Street at 22nd Street , Mission Bryant Street at 22nd Street, San Francisco, CA 94110 Price Free If it rains. Goes ahead wet. Event and ticket details Redwood City Dia de los Muertos Festival Sun Nov 8 · Free Free Peninsula festival in Courthouse Square, altars and food from three until half past eight. k: Jose Mourinho takes Real Madrid back to the Camp Nou on Sunday six points adrift of an unbeaten Barcelona and without Vinicius Junior.
x: World football, every Wednesday · Arsenal covered separately The Weekly Soccer Digest Wednesday Edition · October 21, 2026 · Vol. 1 In this edition The Lead · Como's Night · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Mourinho Walks Back Into the Camp Nou Thirteen years after he left Spain, Jose Mourinho returns to Barcelona as Real Madrid's manager, six points adrift of a side that had won eleven straight until Tuesday, and without the two wingers who were supposed to win him the game. T here is no gentle way to walk into the Spotify Camp Nou, and Jose Mourinho has never looked for one. On Sunday evening, at 1 p.m. Pacific, he takes Real Madrid back to the ground where he spent three seasons in open warfare with the institution he is about to visit, and he does it as the underdog. Barcelona have won nine from nine in La Liga. They have 27 points. Real Madrid have 21, and are third, behind Atletico Madrid as well. A Barcelona win on Sunday makes the gap nine points before Halloween. What makes the fixture genuinely hard to call is that both sides arrive bruised in different places. Barcelona's winning run, eleven matches across all competitions, ended on Tuesday night at the Parc des Princes, where Paris Saint-Germain beat them 4-2 in the best game of the Champions League season so far. It was not a collapse. It was something more worrying for Hansi Flick : two individual errors, one from Lamine Yamal inside his own half for Desire Doue 's opener, one from Warren Zaire-Emery 's opponent under a high ball, and a midfield that could not hold the ball when Vitinha decided to take the game. Barcelona equalised twice, through Xavi Espart and then Yamal himself, and still lost by two. Real Madrid, meanwhile, will play the biggest match of their season so far without Vinicius Junior , who is suspended, and without Rodrygo , who has a cruciate ligament injury. That is a Clasico without either of the wingers who have carried Madrid's transitions for the better part of five years. Kylian Mbappe has nine La Liga goals and will almost certainly start centrally. Beyond him, Mourinho is short of the specific thing his teams have always been built to do, which is run at a high line with pace in the wide areas. Ferland Mendy is back in training. Raul Asencio is not available. Madrid at least arrive in form: they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 at the Bernabeu on Wednesday night, Mbappe and Arda Guler among the scorers, a third straight Champions League win. El Clasico: Key Facts Kickoff Sunday October 25, 1:00 p.m. Pacific (9:00 p.m. in Barcelona) Venue Spotify Camp Nou, La Liga matchday 10 Managers Hansi Flick (Barcelona), Jose Mourinho (Real Madrid) League Barcelona 1st, 27 pts from 9. Real Madrid 3rd, 21 pts from 9 Barcelona out Olmo, Christensen, Eric Garcia, Kounde, Bardghji, de Jong Real Madrid out Vinicius Junior (suspended), Rodrygo, Asencio. Mendy back in training Head to head Barcelona 29 wins, Real Madrid 21, 10 draws Which leaves the tactical question of the week: does Mourinho try to win this game, or does he try to stop Barcelona winning it? His record at the Camp Nou in his first spell suggests he is perfectly willing to do the latter and absorb the criticism, and there is a reasonable argument that 21 points from nine games is not a platform from which to gamble. Barcelona's shape under Flick is still the most aggressive in Europe's top five leagues, a high line that invites exactly the ball in behind that Mbappe has spent his career running onto. PSG hurt Barcelona by playing through them rather than over them. Madrid, without Vinicius and Rodrygo , may not have that option. Barcelona's own absentee list is longer. Dani Olmo came off injured in Paris. Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia have thigh problems, Jules Kounde a sprained ankle. Roony Bardghji ruptured a cruciate ligament in training in August and Frenkie de Jong has been out since tearing the medial collateral ligament in his right knee at the World Cup. The absence that matters most tactically is at centre back: with Christensen out, Ronald Araujo on loan at Liverpool and Kounde injured, Gerard Martin is Flick 's only natural left-sided option. Catalan reporting this month names a left-footed centre back as Barcelona's clearest squad need, and the club cannot address it in January without selling first. More on that below. The two squads were rebuilt around each other over the summer, which gives Sunday an extra edge. Barcelona spent roughly 174 million euros on seven players, headlined by Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United for 70 million plus up to 10 million in variables and Rodri from Manchester City for 60 million plus up to 15 million, with Karim Adeyemi arriving from Borussia Dortmund and Joao Cancelo back on a free. Robert Lewandowski left at the end of his contract. Ferran Torres was sold to PSG for 48.5 million euros, which is why he was on the pitch in Paris on Tuesday in the other shirt, and why he hit the post against the club that made him. "I don't care about [the favourites tag] because I don't see PSG as the favourite. This match isn't decisive. The decisive month will be in April." Luis Enrique, after PSG 4-2 Barcelona The individual duel to watch is Raphinha against whichever full back Mourinho trusts. Raphinha leads the Pichichi race with twelve goals, three clear of Mbappe , and is the one Barcelona attacker whose form has not wobbled. Yamal has eight in La Liga and nine goals with ten assists across eleven appearances in all competitions, and Joan Laporta chose the week of the PSG tie to tell L'Equipe that he is going nowhere. "He's a Barca fan and came through La Masia," Laporta said, in beIN Sports' English rendering of the French interview. "All of that helps when it comes to renewing a contract. We're not worried." The Pichichi Race La Liga top scorers after matchday 9. Raphinha Barcelona 12 Kylian Mbappe Real Madrid 9 Lamine Yamal Barcelona 8 Sergio Camello Rayo Vallecano 7 Ante Budimir Osasuna 7 The head-to-head record in the fixture's modern run reads 29 wins to Barcelona, 21 to Real Madrid, ten draws. None of that will matter much by Sunday evening. What will matter is whether Mourinho , who built his reputation on exactly this kind of night, can produce one more of them with half his attack missing, and whether a Barcelona side that has not lost a league game all season can absorb the first real test of its nerve. The tie is at 1 p.m. Pacific, 9 p.m. in Barcelona. Spain's clocks go back that morning, so the local time reads the same as it did in September while the Pacific conversion shifts. Como's Night Como 4, Manchester United 1 A club playing its first Champions League campaign took Manchester United apart on the shore of Lake Como, and the questions about Michael Carrick are now the loudest in English football. Nico Paz scored inside two minutes. By the time Anastasios Douvikas made it two early in the second half, Manchester United had managed no shots on target at all in the first half, had committed nine fouls to Como 's two, and had seen 62 per cent of the ball go the other way. Michael Carrick made two substitutions at the interval, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos . It did not help. Como finished 4-1 winners, with Paz scoring twice and assisting another, and Douvikas and Ramon also on the scoresheet, according to Corriere dello Sport . It was Como's first home match in the competition. Como are fifth in Serie A on 14 points, have won four of seven, and beat Fiorentina 3-1 away on Sunday. Cesc Fabregas , whose contract runs to June 2028, has built something that now has to be taken seriously rather than enjoyed as a curiosity. His line after the match, to Gianluca Di Marzio , was about the next one rather than this one: "Crediamo tanto in Baturina. Vogliamo diventare una realta solida." We believe a great deal in Baturina. We want to become a solid reality. United's position is harder to describe charitably. They are 13th in the Premier League on seven points from seven games, with one win, and drew 1-1 at Leeds United on Sunday. They have now lost to Atletico Madrid and Como in successive Champions League matchdays after opening with a 4-0 win over Sabah . Carrick used his press conference last weekend to talk about January, telling Sky Sports : "When the next transfer window comes, you want to plan and you want to make the best of it. Whatever that looks like at this stage, we don't quite know. But without doubt, there's opportunity because the transfer window is open." Sky reported centre back and left back as the priorities. With Luke Shaw injured, United currently have no senior left back. The commercial irony is sharp. In late September the club reported record revenue of 677 million pounds achieved without European football. It now has European football and a 4-1 defeat to a club that was in Serie B three years ago. Across the rest of matchday 3 on Wednesday night, nine matches produced 34 goals and exactly one draw. Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1, Aston Villa made it three wins from three by seeing off Viking 3-1, Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0 and Inter Milan edged Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 with ten men after Alessandro Bastoni was sent off. Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0 through an Isco penalty, Galatasaray came from 2-1 down to win 4-2 at Lille with Victor Osimhen scoring, and Bayern Munich were held 2-2 at home by Arsenal. The shock was in Lisbon, where LASK , pointless after two matchdays, won 3-2 at Sporting CP . Transfer News Europe's summer window closed on September 1, so nothing below is a completed transfer. What is moving instead is the thing that always moves in late October: the January pre-contract clock, which starts on New Year's Day and turns every player whose deal expires in June 2027 into either an asset to be sold now or a free agent to be lost later. Certainty tiers are stated for every item. The January 1 Clock Is Already Driving the Market Every contract expiring in June 2027 becomes a pre-contract target on New Year's Day. That single date explains most of this week's reporting. Under FIFA rules a player inside the final six months of a contract can agree a pre-contract with a club in another country. From January 1 that applies to the whole June 2027 cohort, and clubs with sellable players and no signatures are suddenly motivated. The cleanest illustration is at Bournemouth , where Rob Dorsett and Mark McAdam of Sky Sports News reported on October 16 that the club will consider offers in excess of 80 million pounds plus add-ons in January for Alex Scott , who has refused a new contract reported to be the best the club has ever offered. Status: concrete interest with a club valuation set, no bid on the table. Fabrizio Romano corroborated it four days later, saying Chelsea are "definitely there" and have had several contacts with Scott's representatives after a rejected summer bid, and that Liverpool made calls in late June and early July without ever bidding. Scott is 23, an England international, currently injured, and has a little over 18 months left. Marco Rose was blunt when asked: "I told you that Alex Scott was going to stay in the summer. He's a player of our club and now he's injured. If he is back, he's playing for Bournemouth." The same mechanism is producing stories everywhere. Jean-Philippe Mateta is out of contract in June 2027 at Crystal Palace and, per talkSPORT material carried in Sky's Paper Talk on October 20, is showing no inclination to extend, with Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur both linked. Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk reported in late September that United's director of football Jason Wilcox rates his Premier League goals record. Status: concrete interest plus reported player willingness, no talks between clubs. Mateta has made two appearances this season with a hamstring problem, which is the obvious complication. In Spain the same clock is ticking loudest at Sevilla . Javier Merino of JaviSFC reported on October 21 that centre back Andres Castrin , out of contract on June 30 2027, agreed terms in early October on a three-year extension with a significant rise and a 50 million euro release clause, and that the club is still waiting for a formal response from his agency. From January 1 he can sign elsewhere for nothing. Bayer Leverkusen are following closely; Valencia , Real Sociedad , Leeds United and Espanyol are named as interested. This is a Sevilla-specialist outlet rather than a national one, so treat the detail as single-sourced, though the structural facts are not in dispute. Garcia Plaza said in late September: "Ojala renueve, ojala." Liverpool Have Three Midfielders on One List Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Adam Wharton are all live Liverpool links inside ten days. Romano says the intent is explicit. The most useful kind of transfer signal is not a single report but a cluster, and Liverpool have produced one. Fabrizio Romano said on October 20 that "Liverpool are planning to do something important in midfield in 2027," and inside the same ten-day window three separate midfielders have been reported as targets. Lamine Camara is the one with the most history. Romano reported, in material written up by James Marshment at TEAMtalk , that Chelsea had agreed a 47 million pound fee for the 22-year-old Senegal international with Monaco on deadline day before the deal collapsed, that Chelsea were "furious" and are "no longer in talks," and that Liverpool are now frontrunners at a price closer to 59 million pounds. Status: concrete interest and long-term tracking, no bid. Single-origin to Romano, carried by two outlets. There is a separate Liverpool thread worth tracking. Romano said on October 21 that there are "active conversations ongoing between Rio Ngumoha and Liverpool over a new, long-term contract," that the club "absolutely want to keep Rio," and then hedged carefully: "Let's see what's gonna happen in the future, but his contract talks are taking place." Rio Ngumoha is 18 and under contract to 2028. Status: active talks, no agreement. Separately, The Telegraph reported on October 21 that Liverpool have not yet opened renewal talks with Alexis Mac Allister , whose deal runs to 2028, and that Chelsea are watching. Single-sourced. Kane Agrees Terms to 2029, and Dortmund Tie Down Kovac Bayern got the shorter deal they wanted. Dortmund extended their manager a week before the doubts came back. Michael Bridge of Sky Sports News reported on October 16 that Harry Kane has agreed a new Bayern Munich contract in principle through the summer of 2029. Sky Sport Germany and Bild had the same line the previous day. Kane reportedly wanted 2030, so Bayern got their preferred term. The Times put the terms at roughly 474,000 euros a week, just under 25 million a year, which is his existing salary unchanged. Status: personal terms agreed, not signed and not announced. Bridge: "There are just a few things to iron out before confirmation." President Herbert Hainer called the talks "hervorragend." No release clause has been reported. At Borussia Dortmund , the extension is done and official. Niko Kovac signed to 2029 on October 13, along with assistants Robert Kovac and Filip Tapalovic , per the club and Get German Football News . Lars Ricken , managing director for sport, said: "With Niko Kovac, we've been on a very good path since he took office a little over a year and a half ago." Kovac inherited an 11th-placed team in February 2025 and finished second on 73 points last season. Barcelona Have About One Million Euros of Room A detailed look at the club's fair-play position concludes that any January signing must be preceded by a sale. The renewals are eating the margin. Artur Lopez published the single hardest number in this week's European reporting. Writing for Cronica Global on October 11, he set out Barcelona 's position under La Liga's salary rules: the club's limit has risen from 432 million euros to 582 million, and its sporting costs have risen 115 million to 581 million. That is a margin of roughly one million euros. His conclusion is unambiguous: "Todo fichaje en enero de 2027 tendra que pasar primero por ventas." Every January signing will have to come after a sale. At Real Madrid the renewal board is busier and the money less constrained. Jose Felix Diaz of Diario AS reported on October 16 that Jude Bellingham has agreed an extension to June 2031, two years beyond his current deal, with a rise and no figure published. Status: agreement reached, official announcement still expected, and effectively single-sourced to AS. Thibaut Courtois has verbally agreed a one-year extension to 2028, per both Romano and MARCA on October 13, unsigned. Arda Guler 's extension to 2031 is reported closed and awaiting announcement. Antonio Rudiger , out of contract in 2027, has no deal and no talks, which makes him Madrid's only senior expiry inside twelve months. Eduardo Camavinga , to 2029, has no extension conversations at all. Vinicius Junior 's file is closed: he signed to June 2032 in the summer, and his terms set the ceiling every other negotiation at the club is measured against. Nico Paz, Chelsea, and Real Madrid's 80 Million Euro Button Como own him outright. Madrid can buy him back next summer for a fixed price. Chelsea have been watching, and Como's number starts with a one. The most interesting contractual object in European football right now sits on the shore of Lake Como. Marco Conterio of TUTTOmercatoWEB reported on October 21 that Chelsea staff have watched Nico Paz in recent Serie A and Champions League matches and are not deterred by the price. Como own 100 per cent of his registration after paying around 60 million euros in June 2026. Real Madrid hold an exclusive buy-back at 80 million euros, exercisable in the summer of 2027, and take a percentage of any onward sale if they decline it. Guido Lorenzelli of CalcioComo added the same day that Como would only entertain 100 to 120 million euros, and attributed the Chelsea line to unnamed market whispers. On the Spanish side, Diego Vargas at Defensa Central reported the identical 60 and 80 million structure and said Madrid have not decided. Status: concrete interest at scouting level, no bid. The sequencing is the story: if Madrid press the button at 80 million, they buy a 22-year-old playmaker for less than Como could get on the open market, and Como's upside evaporates. The Rumour Mill The Rumour Mill The sagas still simmering, with the certainty of each stated plainly. Where something is single-sourced or rests on an aggregator, it says so. Lewis Hall, Newcastle to Manchester United Rumour, plus reported player willingness. No bid, no talks. The i Paper reported on October 20 that Hall was interested in Old Trafford a few months ago and has not changed his stance; Dean Jones at FlashScore reported on October 14 that Newcastle could value him above 100 million euros and that the finances are the major obstacle. Hall signed a new Newcastle deal in September running to 2031, which is the club's shield. Framed for 2027 rather than January. Two independent reporters. Lisandro Martinez, Manchester United Club planning, and the sources conflict. MailSport reported on October 21 that United will trigger their 12-month option to 2028 and then transfer-list him. Romano said on October 5 that United "have a clause to extend the contract till 2028, so they feel calm, they feel in control," that they still believe in him as a leader, and that he "is not in advanced negotiations with any other side." The Mail line is single-sourced and contradicts Romano. Treat with caution. Emiliano Buendia, new Aston Villa deal Advanced talks, offer on the table. Graeme Bailey at TEAMtalk and The Athletic both reported on October 20 that Aston Villa have offered Buendia, whose deal expires this season, a two-and-a-half-year extension to summer 2029, and that talks with Victor Lindelof and George Hemmings are also progressing. Two independent outlets on the same day, the best-sourced contract story of the week. A renewal ends Leeds United , Galatasaray and Fenerbahce interest. Markus Krosche, Eintracht Frankfurt to AC Milan Departure done, appointment in advanced talks. Kicker broke it on October 18: Krosche asked Eintracht Frankfurt to release him from his sporting-director duties, saying he needed a change, and the club agreed. He was contracted to 2028, so AC Milan must buy him out. Calciomercato.com put the penalty at around 3 million euros; Corriere dello Sport and Eurosport at 4 to 5 million, and the figures conflict. Milan reportedly want him in post by the end of October so he can run their January, with a centre back the stated priority. Frankfurt's shortlist is Johannes Spors , Marcel Schafer and Christoph Spycher , with Sportschau calling Spycher the front-runner. Fabian Hurzeler to Manchester United Knocked down. Romano , on October 16, on the reports linking Brighton 's manager to Old Trafford: "There have been no contacts. Secondly, there have been no direct talks." Ez Abde, Real Betis Concrete interest, with a rejected bid on the record. Flavio Pace of El Gol Digital reported on October 16 that Real Betis fear losing the Morocco international, whose contract runs to 2029 with a 60 million euro release clause the club treats as a floor. Mundo Deportivo reported on September 3 that Everton 's deadline-day package of 35 million euros fixed plus 8 million in variables was rejected. Barcelona hold 20 per cent of his rights. Wider club lists circulating this week run through aggregators and are not stood up. Hansi Flick , before facing him: "Estoy impresionado por Ez Abde." Around the Leagues Premier League Seven from seven, a regulator, and a reckoning Manchester City have won all seven of their Premier League matches under Enzo Maresca , who was appointed on June 29 on a three-year deal after Chelsea received more than 17 million pounds in compensation and after Pep Guardiola stepped down in May following a decade at the club. City beat Ipswich Town 3-2 on Saturday, lead by three points on 21, and have a goal difference of plus 12. Erling Haaland leads the division with eight goals. All of which is happening against a backdrop that nobody at the club can control: an independent Premier League commission upheld 114 of the 115 charges relating to financial rule breaches across 2009-10 to 2017-18, with the decision issued on September 29 and first reported by David Ornstein of The Athletic on September 25. The case moved again this week, and in a direction nobody had flagged. On October 21 Insider Sport reported that the UK Financial Reporting Council has opened inquiries into City's accounting, disclosed in a letter to the House of Commons. It is not yet a formal investigation, and the FRC can sanction individuals rather than the club. The commission's findings said City inflated sponsorship revenue by up to 830 million pounds using undisclosed owner funding, while also concluding that the auditors were unaware. Two days earlier the same outlet set out City's appeal grounds. Chief executive Ferran Soriano said the League's case rests on "a single false accusation, that the owner's personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club," that "this is just not true," and that the club has supplied "bank statements, money transfers, witnesses, and everything necessary." City appealed on October 1, and a ruling is not expected before late January. Unlike the 2020 UEFA case City won, the Court of Arbitration for Sport is not available: Premier League disputes run as private arbitration and an appeal board's decision is final. No sanction has been decided, and no credible outlet has reported a specific one. The points-deduction figures circulating trace to tabloid sourcing. Underneath City, the division is stranger than the table suggests. Brighton are third on 16 points with a goal difference of plus 18, the best in the league, after dismantling Crystal Palace 5-0 on Sunday; Fabian Hurzeler was September's manager of the month. Chelsea under Xabi Alonso are fourth on 13 after winning 2-0 at Everton , and Liverpool , in Andoni Iraola 's first season, fifth on 12 after a 2-1 win at Brentford , with Alexander Isak on five goals. Then the oddity: Manchester United are 13th on seven points after a 1-1 draw at Leeds United and Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como , with Michael Carrick under more pressure than any manager in the league. Newcastle United , now managed by Matthias Jaissle after Eddie Howe resigned in August, are 11th and lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa . Tottenham Hotspur beat Coventry City 3-1 on Monday. Sunderland are bottom on four. And at Everton , David Moyes said on October 16 that his own contract talks have hit "a bit of a lull," linking it to the Friedkin Group putting the club up for sale: "It's not the most important thing to me. I just want to keep driving Everton on." La Liga Nine from nine, and a Clasico without wingers Barcelona have won all nine, scored 30 more than they have conceded and sit on 27 points. Atletico Madrid are second on 22 after a 1-0 win at Espanyol , and Real Madrid third on 21 after beating Sevilla 4-1 at the Bernabeu on Sunday. Barcelona won 5-2 at Real Betis the day before. Raphinha leads the Pichichi on twelve, three ahead of Kylian Mbappe . The two Real Madrid league defeats came at Atletico Madrid , 1-2, and the pattern of their season is a side that wins handsomely and then loses the big one, which is precisely the pattern Jose Mourinho was hired to break. Elsewhere Villarreal drew 0-0 with Elche and Valencia drew 0-0 with Athletic Club , which tells you most of what you need to know about the division's middle. Real Betis are fourth on 19, Real Sociedad fifth on 16. At the bottom, Malaga are the only side yet to win, on four points from nine with four draws, and Valencia are 19th on six. Promoted Racing Santander and Deportivo de A Coruna are both still in the fight, with Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang on five goals for Depor. Bundesliga Four points cover the top four, and Gladbach have none Six matchdays in, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund lead on 14 points, with SC Freiburg and Bayer Leverkusen on 13. Bayern announced themselves on Saturday with a 6-1 destruction of RB Leipzig , which remains the result of the German season. Leverkusen beat Freiburg 2-1 to join the group. Dortmund have not won in three weeks, drawing 0-0 at Union Berlin after a 2-2 with Werder Bremen , which is why Niko Kovac spent his press conference pointing at the table rather than the performances. Patrik Schick of Leverkusen leads the scoring charts on five. The defining story, though, is at the other end. Borussia Monchengladbach have lost all six and have zero points, with eight goals scored and twenty conceded. Per Felix Kunkel of SPORT1 , losing the first six is only the fourth time it has happened in Bundesliga history, after Fortuna Dusseldorf in 1991-92, Mainz 05 in 2020-21 and Bochum in 2022-23, and only Dusseldorf were relegated. A seventh straight defeat, at VfB Stuttgart on Friday, would make them the first club ever to be pointless after seven matchdays. The previous floor is one point. Sporting director Rouven Schroder is not pretending. "Bei aller Kritik und allem, was wir haben, werden wir den Laden morgen nicht zusperren," he told 90min . For all the criticism, we are not shutting up shop tomorrow. He added that seven or eight players planned for the first eleven are unavailable "aber das ist kein Alibi," but that is no alibi, and that the remedy is psychological rather than financial: "Man muss in die Kopfe reinkommen und Selbstvertrauen einflossen." Alexander Blessin , appointed on September 22, was franker still after the 1-2 home defeat by TSG Hoffenheim : "Wo soll ich anfangen? Wir haben teilweise Angsthasen-Fussball gespielt." Where should I start? We played scared-rabbit football at times. Sport Bild has reported a broken dressing room, cliques and senior players doubting teammates. Notably, reporting this week says a Stuttgart defeat is not expected to cost Blessin his job, and that sacking the sporting leadership is ruled out for now. Serie A Lazio level at the top, Juventus in open revolt Inter Milan and Lazio lead on 19 points apiece after seven games, both unbeaten, with Roma on 17 and AC Milan on 15. Inter won 3-1 at Bologna ; Roma beat Genoa 2-0; Milan edged Atalanta 3-2; Como won 3-1 at Fiorentina and are fifth on 14. The two results that mattered most, though, went against the league's biggest names. Venezia beat Napoli 1-0, and Lazio won 3-0 at Juventus through Oliver Provstgaard Nielsen , Gustav Isaksen and a late Fisayo Dele-Bashiru goal. Juventus are eighth on eleven points, and the fallout has been extraordinary. Asked afterwards whether his squad still follows him, Luciano Spalletti said: "Se la squadra mi segue ancora? Fino a ieri avrei detto di si, oggi non lo so." Until yesterday I would have said yes. Today I don't know. His captain Bremer had already told reporters "non punto il dito, ma c'e qualcuno che davanti ai fischi ha paura," I'm not pointing the finger, but there is someone who is afraid when the whistles come. Spalletti's reply: "Le sconfitte non salvano nessuno, c'e dentro fino al collo anche lui." Defeats save nobody, he is in it up to his neck as well. Reporting says Bremer will be fined over the row. By Wednesday Spalletti had changed tack, telling his pre-Rennes press conference: "Questa volta li ho fatti parlare tutti, io son stato zitto." This time I let them all speak and I kept quiet. Maurizio De Santis of Fanpage reported on October 20 that Juventus have put Spalletti on pause with a short-term vote of confidence covering four league games and two Europa League ties before the November break, with Stefano Pioli as stopgap and Antonio Conte a future rather than immediate option. La Gazzetta dello Sport added Simone Inzaghi , now at Al-Hilal . Cost is the brake: Spalletti's contract runs to 2028 at around 5 million euros net a year. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every front, every Tuesday No. 10 · Season 2026/27 Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Read this edition on the web In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Back to Munich, Carrying a Different Kind of Problem Arsenal arrive at the Allianz Arena as champions of England, unbeaten in Europe and yet to concede a Champions League goal. They have also scored eleven times in seven league games. Wednesday night asks the question this season keeps asking: can a team this good at not losing find a way to actually win something bigger? T here is a version of this week that writes itself. Arsenal go to Bayern Munich on Wednesday with fourteen consecutive Champions League league-phase wins behind them, two clean sheets from two this season, a Premier League title in the cabinet for the first time since 2004 and a manager who has just signed on until 2030. They are second in the table, three points behind Manchester City , and they have lost once all season. By any ordinary accounting, this is a club in rude health walking into the most glamorous fixture on its calendar. Then you look at Sunday afternoon. Arsenal went to the City Ground, held seventy-four per cent of the ball, played 629 passes at ninety per cent accuracy, and registered precisely one shot on target. It went in, because Noni Madueke drove inside from the left on eighty minutes and the ball glanced off Jair Cunha and past Matz Sels . Without that deflection this is a goalless afternoon against a side that had not scored at home in the league all season, and the conversation this morning is very different. That is the real story of Arsenal 's autumn, and it is the thing Mikel Arteta will be turning over on the flight to Bavaria. His team have won 1-0 thirteen times in the last 366 days. They have conceded five goals in seven league matches. They have also scored eleven, which is fewer than Brentford , fewer than Chelsea , and barely half of Brighton 's twenty-three. A title defence built on a back four and a goalkeeper is a legitimate way to win a league. It is a far harder way to win in Munich. Key facts: Bayern Munich v Arsenal The tie Champions League league phase, matchday three, Allianz Arena, Wednesday Kick-off 12:00pm Pacific (8:00pm in London, 9:00pm in Munich) Bayern at home Unbeaten in a Champions League group or league-phase match at the Allianz since December 2013 Harry Kane 15 goals in 22 appearances against Arsenal Last meeting Arsenal 3-1 Bayern, Emirates Stadium, November 26, 2025 Out Arsenal: Saliba, Hincapie, Tzolis. Bayern: Musiala, Olise (suspended), with Kompany and Neuer both doubtful The shape of the night The tactical shape of the evening is unusually legible, because both teams are missing the player who would normally bend it. Bayern are without Jamal Musiala , who has a thigh problem, and without Michael Olise , suspended after his red card against Viking on matchday two. Vincent Kompany is recovering from a viral infection, missed training and did not take Tuesday's press conference, which assistant Aaron Danks fronted instead. Manuel Neuer has fluid on his foot. For a club that beat RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday, this is still a formidable team, but it is a reshuffled one, and Serge Gnabry is the likeliest man to take Olise's place against the club where he began. Arsenal 's own absence is the one that matters most. William Saliba is still out with the back problem that has cost him most of the autumn, and is only now back in individual training with a return targeted for next month. In his place Ezri Konsa , the £55m arrival from Aston Villa , has formed a partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes that has produced five clean sheets in nine appearances. Arteta was unambiguous about them after Sunday, saying the win "was not possible without them." Konsa also happens to have a good personal record against Kane, who had a thin evening at the Emirates last November. "We reached a mountain, but not the highest one or the one that I certainly visualise." Mikel Arteta, on winning the Premier League That quote, given to HBO Max's Inside the Game , is the key to why this fixture carries more freight than a matchday-three away trip ought to. Last season Arsenal were on for a quadruple and finished with one trophy. They lost the EFL Cup final to Manchester City , went out of the FA Cup to Southampton in the quarter-finals, and lost the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. The league title ended a twenty-two-year wait and it genuinely changed the club. It also left the one trophy Arteta talks about in those terms still unwon, and the shortest route to it runs through nights exactly like Wednesday. Arteta's choices The selection questions are real. Jurrien Timber is expected at right-back, sharing the load with Ben White . Martin Zubimendi is back from a minor hamstring issue but has played so little this season that a start would be a surprise, which leaves Declan Rice as the fixed point and a genuine choice between Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes alongside him. The midfield triangle against Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic is where Danks expects the match to be settled, and he is probably right. Up front, the arithmetic is awkward. Kai Havertz has three goals in nine appearances and has been below his level since the international break, but Arteta picks him for big games and went out of his way last week to argue that Havertz can become a twenty-five-goal striker. Viktor Gyokeres has started both Champions League matches and has not scored for the club this season. Bukayo Saka has four goals in all competitions and was quiet at Forest. The one man in form is Madueke, who scored the winner from the bench on Sunday after being hauled on for Eberechi Eze at half-time, and who is the obvious candidate to start on the left. Arteta's framing of the whole thing has been notably unhedged. He said he wants Bayern at full strength, expects "96 minutes of man-to-man," and intends to "confront that and go for it." He will not get Bayern at full strength, and he arrives without his best defender. A draw in Munich would keep Arsenal comfortably inside the top eight and would be a perfectly good night's work. A win would be the first proper statement of the defence of a title and of a continental ambition that last May came down to a shootout. Either way, the number that will tell us most is not the scoreline. It is the shot count. One on target at the City Ground was enough on Sunday. It will not be enough on Wednesday. The Vacancy on the Left Gabriel Martinelli is in Saudi Arabia, Christos Tzolis is injured, Eberechi Eze keeps drifting inside and Noni Madueke has just won a match from the bench. Arsenal's left wing has become the most open job at the club. When Gabriel Martinelli left for Al Hilal for £60m in early September, Arsenal accepted a reality that had been building for a while: the left flank was no longer a settled position. The summer replacement was Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge at £34m, who is a useful footballer rather than a transformative one, and who is currently out with a hamstring problem until roughly the start of November. Into the gap stepped Eberechi Eze , the £69m signing from Crystal Palace , who scored against Lille by drifting inside from the touchline, which is both his great strength and the reason he keeps being described as a stopgap out wide. At Forest he was anonymous and came off at half-time. Arteta did not name him in his post-match remarks. He did not need to. The man who has taken the chance is Madueke , and the story of how is worth knowing. Not called up by England over the October break, he stayed at the training ground and worked with Arteta, who afterwards said he had created more chances and taken more touches in the opposition box than anyone there. He started against Leeds United , crossed for Riccardo Calafiori 's equaliser in the 2-1 win, and then won the Forest game off the bench. Arteta's verdict was blunt: Madueke "gave me no option," and had been the best player in training for ten days. It is a left-footer on the left, which is unusual for this manager, and the wider question remains open. Arteta has floated Max Dowman there. Myles Lewis-Skelly can cover it. None of that is the same as an elite option, which is precisely why the January conversation below exists. Transfer News The January Attacker, and the Line Arsenal Cannot Cross David Ornstein's assessment is the one to trust: Arsenal know they are short in attack, they wanted to fix it in the summer and did not, and the constraint is financial rather than philosophical. Nothing has moved publicly on this thread in the last seven days, which is itself worth reporting, because the volume of speculation around it has gone up considerably while the sourcing has stayed exactly where it was. The best account remains David Ornstein 's reader Q&A for The Athletic in mid-September, and it is unusually candid. Arsenal lost Leandro Trossard , Gabriel Jesus and Martinelli in one window, loaned out Ethan Nwaneri , and did not "go beyond the signing of Christos Tzolis," who was in effect the Trossard replacement. Jesus was not replaced at all. On whether they will act in January, Ornstein's words were: "I could see something happening because they wanted to, and I thought they needed to, in the summer and they didn't." He paired that with a warning. He also said plainly that he did not know of anything brewing. Who they actually chased What makes the thread credible rather than idle is the record of who the club actually chased. The Lead The champions of Europe walk into the one place nobody is losing Paris Saint-Germain have won the last two Champions Leagues. Manchester City have won all eight games of Enzo Maresca’s reign. Wednesday night at the Etihad is the first evening this season that asks one of those sentences to give way. T here is a particular kind of fixture that the league phase was invented to produce, and this is it. Manchester City against Paris Saint-Germain , in the middle of October, with nothing eliminated and everything implied. The Etihad is sold out. The visitors are the holders of the European Cup, and the holders of the one before that. The hosts have not lost a match since the summer, under a manager who was appointed on the last Monday of June and has not yet found out what a bad week feels like. Start with Enzo Maresca , because his start is the statistical story of the European autumn. Six Premier League games, six wins, sixteen goals scored and five conceded, eighteen points and a three-point cushion at the top. City’s own records department notes that this equals the best opening run by a new manager in Premier League history, matching Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea in 2009/10 and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer ’s caretaker spell at Manchester United in December 2018. Win at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday and it becomes a record outright. Add the Champions League and the domestic cup and the number is eight from eight, per the club . The win that changed the temperature was Sunday’s. City went to Anfield and won 3-0, a scoreline that flatters nobody and settles nothing, because it arrived on the back of a red card. Liverpool were level and comfortable when Ryan Gravenberch collected a second yellow on 62 minutes; Erling Haaland scored two minutes and 37 seconds later, Jeremy Doku followed on 68 and Rayan Cherki finished it on 78. Jamie Carragher called the first booking “a shocking decision” and Gary Neville called the second “very soft”. Andoni Iraola , whose side had not lost all season, said the first foul “should never have been a yellow”. None of that changes the ladder. Liverpool are ninth and nine points back. Beat Porto 2-0 away on matchday one. PSG’s season Champions League holders, and winners in 2025 and 2026, having beaten Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in Budapest on 30 May. Sixth in Ligue 1 on 11 points. Beat Slovan Bratislava 6-1 on matchday one. The benches Enzo Maresca, appointed 29 June 2026, succeeding Pep Guardiola. PSG are not the team that beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest at the end of May, because three of that night’s forwards have gone. In their place Luis Enrique has Ferran Torres , bought from Barcelona for a reported fee around 41.5m pounds eleven days after he scored the goal that won Spain the World Cup, and Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco for around 43m, and Mika Godts from Ajax for around 39m. That reconstruction has shown in the league. PSG are sixth in Ligue 1 on eleven points, three behind Monaco, having drawn their first two matches, lost at home to Monaco in early September and lost the Trophee des Champions to Lens in August. Luis Enrique called the afternoon “an almost perfect result” and then conceded the obvious qualifier: “We conceded a goal, and it was tough.” “As a football fan, I like to watch City play.” Luis Enrique , speaking before travelling to Manchester In Europe, though, the machine still looks like the machine. A club that has historically let contracts run until the player’s leverage has evaporated is dealing with a 33-year-old centre-forward who is the only reason several of those results were not worse. Expect this one to be settled quietly and in Bayern’s favour, and expect the Premier League clubs who have been waiting for the clause to become usable to read the word “decreased” several more times. Manchester United keep answering a different question The club insists Michael Carrick is safe. Everyone briefing about January is briefing about a left-back. Neither of those is the problem. Six points from six league games is Manchester United ’s worst start since 1986/87. On Tuesday they lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid , conceding inside a minute to Pablo Barrios and finishing with ten men after Leny Yoro was dismissed. Fabrizio Romano reported on 13 October that the club is “still giving time and confidence” to Michael Carrick , that the players remain with him, and that the results are “not acceptable”. A day later he added that no last-minute change is expected and that United have not contacted any other manager. Where it stands Carrick is backed, for now. Two tier-one reporters arrive at the same answer from opposite directions, and no successor has been approached. David Ornstein landed in the same place from the other direction: he knows of no desire to remove Carrick, but said the manager “needs to improve things” and pointed the rest of the blame at recruitment, executives and owners. He singled out Sunday’s trip to Leeds United as “massive”. Nicolo Schira has gone further, naming Leeds, Como and Bournemouth as the decisive run. Reports linking Eddie Howe and Fabian Hurzeler to the job trace back to unnamed accounts and should be treated as speculation. Antonio Conte is a different case: Romano says he would be open to a mid-season move to a historical club and would not want the Middle East, while explicitly refuting a claim that he was reaching an agreement with INEOS. On the squad, Romano says January is “too early to say” and depends on conditions he did not specify, but that a left-back would not be “crazy money”. The name that keeps recurring is Adrien Truffert of Bournemouth , whom Ornstein valued at around 60m pounds last month while suggesting a deal was more likely in the summer of 2027. Bournemouth are expected to reject January offers. United wanted Newcastle United ’s Lewis Hall in August; Hall has since signed a new contract there. Milan and Inter spend the autumn protecting what they have Two clubs with no money to spend in January are doing the next best thing, which is making sure nobody can take anything for free in June. Inter have opened renewal talks with Federico Dimarco aimed at a contract to 2030, Gazzetta dello Sport reported on 12 October. The club holds a unilateral option to 2028, so there is no cliff edge, and no agreement has been reached. At Milan , Gazzetta reported in late September that Adrien Rabiot is close to a renewal through 2030 with an option year. Nothing is official on either. Where it stands Talks opened at Inter , reported progress at Milan . Neither club has announced anything, and both reports originate with Gazzetta dello Sport. Milan’s more pressing problem is structural. Matteo Gabbia tore a left hamstring with partial tendon involvement at Sassuolo on Sunday and is out for months, with a specialist deciding between surgery and conservative treatment. A club that drew 1-1 that afternoon and sits fifth now has a January window in which a centre-back is close to compulsory. Links to specific names have circulated without attribution and are not worth printing yet. Juventus , meanwhile, are reported by Tuttosport to be considering a striker in January to support Randal Kolo Muani , whose 81st-minute header at Cagliari rescued a point and was his first Serie A goal of the season. They have the balance sheet to think about it: the board approved accounts carrying a forecast 66m euro loss on 29 September and proposed a delegation for a capital increase of up to 250m euros, with Exor confirming an advance. The Rumour Mill Everything else that is moving, and how much of it is real Everything simmering, with the reliability stated plainly. Several of this week’s loudest stories are the thinnest. Advanced, or close to it Marc Bernal ’s Barcelona extension, from 2029 to 2031 with a 500m euro clause, was reported by El Gol Digital on 12 October as closed but unsigned. One non-tier-one source, no club confirmation, and worth watching rather than believing. Barcelona’s last official announcement on the midfielder was a renewal to 2029 a year ago. Certainty: single-sourced report of an agreement. Concrete interest, with a club saying no Alex Scott is the window’s clearest example of a selling club getting its answer in first. Bournemouth have told Chelsea and Real Madrid that the midfielder is not leaving in January, per talkSPORT as relayed on 7 October. Chelsea bid more than 60m pounds in the summer and were refused. Reports of a nine-figure valuation are the writers’ estimates rather than anyone’s quoted number, and the two best accounts of his contract length contradict each other, one saying a single year remains and one saying 2028. Certainty: concrete interest, no sale sanctioned. Rumour, and treat it that way A 70m euro January bid from Liverpool for Barcelona ’s Jules Kounde was reported on 14 October by TheHardTackle, attributing it to the Spanish site Fichajes, with the admission that no formal talks have happened. That is a low-reliability chain and nothing more. The same applies to Pedro Porro to Real Madrid and to the various claims about Florian Wirtz ’s future, both of which currently live on aggregator sites rather than with any reporter who would put a name to them. The loudest of the lot deserves a flat warning. The widely circulated story that Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Barcelona in 2027, with a figure around 130m pounds attached, traces back to an unverified social-media account and has been repeated by outlets that did not check it. There is no statement from either club or from the player, and Spanish reporting indicates there is no relegation release clause of the kind the story depends on. Certainty: noise. It is included here only because readers will have seen it everywhere else. Stated needs, which is where real deals start Paris Saint-Germain were reported by L’Equipe in early September to want two things in January: a right-footed centre-back to understudy Marquinhos , and an attacker. Juventus want a striker. Milan need a centre-back. Manchester United want a left-back. Those four sentences are more predictive of what actually happens on 1 January than any name currently trending, and three of the four needs were created by injuries or exits that happened in the last six weeks. The 2027 Bosman class The list of players whose contracts are reported to expire next summer is, as ever, the quietest and most consequential document in football. It currently includes Bruno Fernandes , Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw at Manchester United ; Alisson and Virgil van Dijk at Liverpool ; Mateo Kovacic at Manchester City ; Richarlison at Tottenham ; Kane at Bayern Munich ; Rudiger and Brahim Diaz at Real Madrid ; Koke at Atletico Madrid ; Hakan Calhanoglu at Inter ; Christian Pulisic and Fikayo Tomori at Milan ; Kevin De Bruyne , Frank Anguissa and Stanislav Lobotka at Napoli ; Paulo Dybala and Lorenzo Pellegrini at Roma ; and Marcel Sabitzer at Borussia Dortmund . The compilation is a secondary aggregator’s rather than any club’s, and renewal status varies from name to name. Courtois is the obvious one already resolved. The managers’ market Venezia sacked Giovanni Stroppa on Tuesday after six defeats in six, five goals scored and sixteen conceded. Gianluca Di Marzio reported on Wednesday that Davide Nicola has agreed a deal to 2028, and Cremonese confirmed he had terminated his contract there by mutual consent. Certainty: agreed, Venezia announcement pending. In MLS, LAFC dismissed Marc Dos Santos on 27 September and appointed Xavi Tamarit as interim. Borussia Monchengladbach are still winless under Alexander Blessin , who arrived on 22 September. Around the Leagues Premier League Hide Leaders: Manchester City, 18 points from 6. Most goals: Brighton. Most goal involvements: Joao Pedro, 8. One team has turned the Premier League into an arithmetic problem. Manchester City have won all six, and the gap at the top is three points over Arsenal with Brighton a further two back. The chasing has been done in near silence: Enzo Maresca inherited a squad that was supposed to need rebuilding and instead has 16 goals and five conceded, and the 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday was his first genuinely hostile away afternoon. Joao Pedro of Chelsea leads the division for goal involvements with eight, five goals and three assists, per BBC Sport , which tells you how open the rest of it is. Behind City, the most convincing football is being played in two places nobody is shouting about. Brighton are third, are the division’s top scorers, have won three successive league games without conceding and have had ten different scorers; Fabian Hurzeler told Sky “it is not about having one good goalscorer”, which is both a boast and a recruitment strategy. They won 2-0 at Sunderland with ten men after Pascal Struijk was dismissed on a VAR review, with Maxim De Cuyper and a debutant, Rayan Hadjam , scoring. Chelsea answered a 3-0 defeat at Brentford with a 5-1 against Bournemouth in which Jordan Henderson scored after 65 seconds and again from 25 yards, Joao Pedro scored twice, and Xabi Alonso switched to a back three after conceding a league-high twelve goals in his first five games. Brentford and Everton are both still unbeaten. The bottom half is where the season is actually happening. Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite Rodrigo Bentancur being sent off for a headbutting motion at Luke Shaw , a dismissal that triggered a touchline brawl and still was not enough; Dominic Solanke equalised in stoppage time for a Spurs side who have not won a league match since May despite spending over 300m pounds in the summer, and whose manager Roberto De Zerbi said last month he had “never seen a team like us, so fragile and inconsistent”. Fulham are bottom on two points, Alvaro Arbeloa insisting “I don’t feel fear” after a 2-1 loss at Ipswich Town built on two goals in the last three minutes. Coventry City beat Newcastle United 4-1 on Monday for their first top-flight home win in more than 25 years, Jayden Mfuni becoming their youngest Premier League scorer, after which Matthias Jaissle apologised to the travelling support and said conceding eight in two away Mondays “is not good enough for the Premier League”. And at Crystal Palace , Oliver Glasner returned with Nottingham Forest , led after three minutes, and lost 3-1. In the Women’s Super League, Manchester City lead on 15 points from Chelsea on 13 and London City Lionesses on 12, the Lionesses having won 6-1 at Tottenham with Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani scoring twice each. La Liga Hide Leaders: Barcelona, 24 points from 8, still perfect. Pichichi: Raphinha, 12. Eight matches, eight wins, 34 goals. Barcelona have not been this ruthless this early in a very long time, and Saturday’s 3-0 over Getafe was their 23rd consecutive home league win. Anthony Gordon scored his first Barcelona goal inside two minutes, Gabriel Jesus and Jules Kounde added the others, and Hansi Flick used the afternoon to make a point about workload, praising the squad and saying Lamine Yamal ’s minutes must be managed. They did it without Raphinha , who leads the Pichichi race with twelve and is nursing a hamstring edema picked up with Brazil . Flick’s line of the week, relayed from AS: “We want trophies, not records.” Race tracker The Pichichi race after eight rounds Raphinha, Barcelona 12 Camello, Rayo Vallecano 7 Mbappe, Real Madrid 7 Lamine Yamal, Barcelona 7 Zabiri, Racing Santander 7 Budimir, Osasuna 6 La Liga goals scored, as of the Associated Press table of 11 October, which excludes Monday’s Levante v Sevilla. Everything else in Spain this week was chaos of one kind or another. Rayo Vallecano ’s first home match of the season, against Athletic Club , was abandoned after supporters protesting against president Raul Martin Presa threw paper onto the pitch; the referee restarted it once, stopped it again and told both coaches it could not continue. No official resumption date has been set, Spanish reporting points towards early November behind closed doors, and the regulations do not simply award Athletic the points. Athletic, who also had a September fixture at Levante postponed by a flooded pitch, have two games in hand. Elsewhere Levante drew 3-3 with Sevilla on Monday in a match that produced three goals after the 90th minute and a red card for Isaac Romero for his celebration; Real Betis beat Osasuna 5-2 with two from Isco to go third on 19 points; and Javier Aguirre began at Valencia with a 2-2 at Racing Santander in which the 18-year-old Otorbi scored his first senior goal. Bundesliga Hide Leaders: Freiburg and Dortmund, 13 points from 5. Top scorer: Schick, 5. Record pace: 172 goals in five matchdays. Germany is in the middle of the highest-scoring start in its history: 172 goals in the first five matchdays, beating the 170 of 1984/85, at 3.82 a game. On Saturday it produced a record that may never be beaten. Augsburg ’s Robin Fellhauer scored after 8.4 seconds, the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, when Manuel Neuer chipped the kick-off straight to him. Bayern Munich drew 2-2, Harry Kane assisting both goals without scoring, and Vincent Kompany defended his goalkeeper on the grounds that Neuer “has played football long enough”. The table has rearranged itself around that. SC Freiburg are top, level on 13 points with Borussia Dortmund and ahead on goal difference, after a 2-1 over Schalke 04 won with ten men, Ritsu Doan ’s compatriot Goto heading in a Vincenzo Grifo cross on 85. Dortmund dropped their first points of the season in the strangest fashion, leading Werder Bremen 2-0 with two minutes left and drawing 2-2, all four goals arriving in the final ten minutes and Niclas Fullkrug scoring against his former club. Bayern are third on eleven and have not won in four weeks. RB Leipzig beat Eintracht Frankfurt 6-0, Christopher Nkunku scoring the first pure hat-trick by a Leipzig player in the Bundesliga and reaching 50 league goals with the second, and Patrik Schick leads the scoring charts with five in five for Bayer Leverkusen . Two sides are in open crisis. Frankfurt have conceded sixteen in five, and Adi Hutter substituted his captain Robin Koch at half-time of the Leipzig game, saying he expects more from a captain and that a signal was needed; Koch told Kicker that running away “is not an option” and will start and captain the side against Koln on Friday. Borussia Monchengladbach are bottom with no points from five, with six players out including captain Tim Kleindienst , Ko Itakura and Nicolas Kuhn . Bayern have a European problem of their own making. Michael Olise was sent off in Stavanger for a second booking after throwing the ball into the face of Viking captain Zlatko Tripic . Kompany was blunt. He called it “uberblod”, said the dismissal was “100 per cent his mistake”, and noted that Tripic had been the smarter man. Olise misses the home game against Arsenal on 21 October. Serie A Hide Leaders: Inter and Lazio, 16 points from 6. Best defence: Roma, 3 conceded. Capocannoniere: Malen, 6. Serie A has produced the most unlikely leader in Europe, and it is not even top on its own. Lazio are level with Inter on 16 points after five wins from six, the best start of the three-points era for the club, with the division’s second-best defence. Gennaro Gattuso beat Monza 3-1 on Sunday with goals from Nuno Tavares , who had not scored in three years, Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti . Roma are third with three goals conceded in six games. Cagliari are fourth. Juventus are sixth and Napoli , the reigning point of reference, eighth. Inter are the story, because Inter are two clubs at once. At home in Serie A they beat Parma 3-0 with Hakan Calhanoglu back from injury. In Europe they have no points and no answers: beaten 2-1 at Real Madrid on matchday one and then 4-3 at the San Siro by Club Brugge , who were given a hat-trick by Nicolo Tresoldi despite Inter having 31 shots. They have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League matches. Cristian Chivu took it on himself, telling Sky Sport Italia that two big chances went begging, “so a little frustration set in, we got frenetic, lost our balance”, and adding: “I take responsibility.” Gazzetta’s verdict was six words long: dominant in Italy, disastrous in Europe. Napoli are in the same hole and are being louder about it. Beaten 3-1 at Villarreal after Amir Rrahmani had put them ahead, they also have nothing from two matchdays, and Massimiliano Allegri used the aftermath to deliver the week’s most Allegri sentence: in Italy, knowing how to defend “has become almost a disgrace”. He also warned that if his players travel to Venezia on Saturday without humility, “we will come out with broken bones”. Venezia, for their part, sacked Giovanni Stroppa on Tuesday. Como lost their first ever Champions League match on Wednesday, 3-2 at Feyenoord , having led through Assane Diao , who then limped off on 23 minutes. The week’s administrative news was substantial. The Milan administrative court rejected five challenges to the sale of San Siro to Inter and Milan, clearing the way for the new stadium, while Serie A’s twenty clubs meet in Milan on Friday to consider a JPMorgan plan to create a media company and lift international television income from around 250m euros towards 500m. Two dismissals defined the weekend’s temper. At Cagliari, where Randal Kolo Muani rescued a 1-1 for Juventus, referee Marcenaro sent off both managers, Luciano Spalletti and Fabio Pisacane , after a post-match confrontation. Both were banned for a match, Spalletti missing Sunday’s visit of Lazio. Donyell Malen , Serie A’s leading scorer on six, serves a one-game ban for the red card he collected at Como. Ligue 1 Hide Leaders: Monaco, 14 points from 6, unbeaten. Top scorers: nine players on 4. France has the most genuinely open table of the six, and the club at the top of it is the one that sold its best young attacker to the champions. Monaco are unbeaten on 14 points under Filipe Luis , the former Brazil and Atletico left-back appointed in July, having drawn 2-2 at home with Toulouse after leading 2-0 at half-time. Lille are second on 13 under Davide Ancelotti , Rennes third on the same points, Lyon fourth, Paris FC fifth and Paris Saint-Germain sixth. Nine players share the top of the scoring charts on four goals apiece, among them Ferran Torres , Esteban Lepaul and Amine Gouiri . The week’s real subject, though, was tackling, and the Ligue 1 clubs are no longer being polite about it. Lyon lost Lois Openda , on loan from Juventus, to a fractured fibula in Friday’s 2-1 defeat at Lens , and issued a statement criticising referee Jeremy Stinat for the number of fouls he left unpunished. Openda is out until at least the November international window. Two days earlier Lille had gone public over Tiago Santos , whose knee was caught by Le Havre ’s Amir Richardson in a tackle that drew no card from referee Bastien Dechepy and no VAR intervention. Santos has a complete cruciate rupture and a meniscal lesion and will be out more than six months. Lille’s statement noted that “no sanction was pronounced, not even a warning”. Le Havre replied that both referee and VAR judged no sanction necessary and that a retroactive punishment would fall outside the rules. The rest: Marseille ended a run of five consecutive defeats in all competitions by winning 2-0 at Troyes through Amine Harit and a 98th-minute penalty from Himad Abdelli , which lifts Bruno Genesio ’s side to thirteenth and no higher. Lens beat Lyon for Yannick Cahuzac ’s first win since he replaced Dino Toppmoller , who was dismissed in September after six matches. And Lille settled 26.6m euros of stadium-related debt, which in the current French financial climate counts as a result. Major League Soccer Hide Leaders: Nashville SC, 63 points. Golden Boot: Messi, 23 goals. Decision Day: 7 November. The American season is five matchdays from its end and has one runaway and one record in play. Nashville SC lead the overall table on 63 points from 28 games, thirteen clear in the East, at a club-record 2.22 points a game; the league’s single-season record is the 74 Inter Miami posted in 2024, and as of the start of October Nashville needed fifteen points from their last seven to beat it. They won 4-1 at Austin FC on Saturday. Vancouver Whitecaps lead the West, and are the only side so far confirmed through. Decision Day is 7 November. Nine clubs qualify from each conference, the eighth and ninth seeds meeting in a single-game Wild Card on 18 November, with a best-of-three first round from 20 November and MLS Cup on Friday 18 December. Lionel Messi leads the Golden Boot with 23 goals and 13 assists, four clear of FC Dallas ’s Petar Musa on 19, with Rafael Navarro , Milan Iloski and Brian White on 17. Four days after his international farewell, a 3-0 win over Benin in Buenos Aires in which he scored his 126th Argentina goal from the penalty spot and cried at the end of it, he scored twice in Miami’s 4-0 against DC United , with Luis Suarez also scoring twice. He is contracted at Miami through 2028. Around that: Philadelphia Union beat Real Salt Lake 2-1 to extend a club-record unbeaten run to thirteen games, Iloski scoring his 17th. St. Louis City beat LA Galaxy 6-2 with a Magnus Holse hat-trick inside 21 minutes. LAFC , who dismissed Marc Dos Santos on 27 September and are being run on an interim basis by Xavi Tamarit , drew 1-1 with Vancouver despite the visitors losing a man in the seventh minute; Son Heung-min has 13 assists and six goals for them this season and Hugo Lloris has twelve clean sheets. And the structural news that will outlast all of it: this is the last full season of the spring-to-autumn calendar, with the league planning a shortened 14-match transitional season in early 2027 before moving to a summer-to-spring schedule. Numbers of the Week 8.4 Seconds into Augsburg against Bayern Munich before Robin Fellhauer scored the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, after Manuel Neuer chipped the kick-off straight to him. 172 Goals in the Bundesliga’s first five matchdays, a competition record, beating the 170 scored in 1984/85. 4 Matches of Vinicius Junior ’s ban from the Spanish federation, which takes in Sunday’s visit of Sevilla and the Clasico at Barcelona on 25 October. 6 Manchester United ’s points from six league games, their fewest at this stage of a season since 1986/87. 0 Champions League points for both Inter and Napoli after two matchdays. Inter have lost seven of their last eight matches in the competition. 23 Lionel Messi ’s goals in MLS this season, four clear at the top of the Golden Boot race, with 13 assists alongside them. Sporting won 2-0 and have a maximum six points. Sabah of Azerbaijan won their first ever league-phase Champions League match, 2-0 against Slavia Praha , through Kaheem Parris and a late Joy-Lance Mickels breakaway.
