k: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, every Tuesday No. 9 · Season 2026-27 Tuesday 13 October 2026 Catch-up edition, published October 26, 2026. In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead A new contract, two wins in four days, and the answer last month's defeat demanded Arsenal came back from the international break needing to prove the 3-0 defeat at Brighton was a blip. They signed their manager to 2030, came from behind to beat unbeaten Leeds United and then took Lille apart in seven second-half minutes. T he week began with paperwork. On Wednesday 7 October Arsenal confirmed that Mikel Arteta had signed a new contract, reported as a four-year deal running to 2030. His previous agreement was due to expire at the end of this season. It was the least surprising announcement of the autumn, and it was treated that way. Arteta , 44, is the longest-serving manager in the Premier League now that Pep Guardiola has left Manchester City . He arrived in December 2019, won the club's first league title in 22 years last season and took them to a Champions League final they lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. “It's a privilege to commit my future to the club,” Arteta said in the club's announcement. “This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel.” He added that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together . The co-chairs, Stan Kroenke and Josh Kroenke , said: It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead. Two days later, in his press conference before the Leeds game, Arteta spoke more personally. He told reporters the thing he would remember was the moment of signing: looking around the room and seeing excitement in their eyes . He named Stan and Josh Kroenke , chief executive Richard Garlick , James King and sporting director Andrea Berta . Then he closed the subject: Now I have to earn the right every single day to continue at this level, and make the most of it. He did not have to wait long to start earning it. Saturday: a crowd that told them to wake up For fifty-five minutes on Saturday, the Brighton hangover looked real. Leeds United , unbeaten and with only three league goals conceded all season, came to the Emirates for the 12:30 kick-off and did exactly what Daniel Farke 's side had done to everyone else. They sat in shape, defended the box and waited. Arsenal had one meaningful chance in the first half, a Kai Havertz header straight at James Trafford . Gabriel Gudmundsson should have put the visitors ahead just before the break and was denied by a strong save from David Raya . According to the PA Media report, one supporter shouted Wake up as the players went down the tunnel at half-time. Ten minutes after the restart, Leeds scored. Gudmundsson drove a low cross into the six-yard box, Raya could not deal with it and James Justin blasted in from close range. It was the 55th minute. The equaliser came seven minutes later and changed the afternoon. Noni Madueke , starting on the left in place of the injured Christos Tzolis , crossed to the far post. Ben White nodded the ball back across goal and Riccardo Calafiori ran in to finish from close range. It was his first goal at the Emirates. A minute later Arteta sent on three players at once: Bruno Guimaraes for Myles Lewis-Skelly , Jurrien Timber for White and Viktor Gyokeres for Havertz . It took Guimaraes seven minutes to decide the match. A quickly taken free kick was flicked between several players, Declan Rice laid it into his path and the seventy-five million pound midfielder drove it into the bottom corner from just outside the box on 70 minutes. It was his first goal at the Emirates and his second for the club. This is the level for Arsenal , every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at. Mikel Arteta , after Leeds Raya also turned an Ao Tanaka drive over the bar, and Arsenal saw it out. Arteta told TNT Sports the team had come in with something to prove. We weren’t pleased about what we did against Brighton , and today was an opportunity to prove that right , he said, and of the winner: The timing, I think, the connection and the execution of it, it was a beauty. The losing manager was gracious. Arsenal is the most consistent team in Europe, one of the best in the world , Farke said, before adding that he was heartbroken and gutted for players who had deserved to travel home with points. Justin , the scorer, put it more simply: Their mentality is unbelievable. Guimaraes had been told publicly that he was not at the level required at Brighton , where he had made his only league start and been withdrawn around the hour. His answer was a goal and a promise. I felt amazing and I can't wait to score more goals now , he said. We know how tight the Premier League is, so we're very happy with the win. For a little over twenty-four hours, Arsenal were level on points with Manchester City at the top. Then City went to Anfield on Sunday and won 3-0 after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second booking on 62 minutes, with Erling Haaland , Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scoring. City have won six from six. Arsenal are three points back. Tuesday: seven minutes of football The week ended under a cloud and in a blaze. On Tuesday the club announced the death of its life president, Ken Friar , at 92. That evening the Emirates stood to applaud him before kick-off against Lille , and then watched one of the best spells of football Arsenal have produced this season. Arteta made five changes from Saturday. Guimaraes got his first Emirates start, Eberechi Eze and Gyokeres started, and Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Havertz began on the bench. For an hour it was patient and not particularly sharp. Guimaraes fired wide from close range and had a deflected shot palmed away by Berke Ozer . Mikel Merino headed at the goalkeeper. Eze , arriving on the penalty spot, shot straight at him. Lille had a goal from Ayase Ueda ruled out for offside. Then it opened up. On 64 minutes Madueke slipped in Timber , and the Dutchman dinked a finish over Ozer . Timber said afterwards that his teammate had been screaming, ‘Shoot, shoot, shoot’ as he went through. A minute later Arteta made another triple substitution: Saka for Madueke , Odegaard for Merino , Havertz for Gyokeres . On 67 minutes Guimaraes found Saka , whose low cross was turned in by Eze with a slight deflection. On 71, Odegaard slid Havertz through, Havertz cut it back and Saka curled it into the far corner. Three goals in seven minutes, from three different scorers. Sky Sports' match page recorded that Lille did not manage a shot on target all night. It was a joy to watch, the three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings. Mikel Arteta , after Lille Arteta was candid about the first half. He said his side's technical quality wasn't good enough to deliver moments of real threat before a positional change at half-time lifted it. The more telling line was about the season as a whole: When other aspects aren't working, we need to make sure we have a variety of ways to win football matches. It is hard not to read that as a reference to set-pieces, which have not yet produced a single corner goal this season. Lille coach Davide Ancelotti , son of the Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti , told UEFA.com: I don't think the players deserve this scoreline. His side have no points after two games, having lost to Real Betis on matchday one. Arsenal have six, and share top spot in the league phase with Barcelona and Sporting CP . Not everything about the week was clean. The team that beat Leeds lost two players in a session after the final whistle, and the attack, for all the brilliance of Tuesday, is still not converting enough of what it creates. But Arsenal entered the week with questions about their nerve after Brighton . They leave it with a manager tied down, two wins, five goals across the two games and a bench that changed both matches. The bench that won the week Two triple substitutions, and two matches turned by the players who came off the bench. On Saturday Arteta sent on three players at 63 minutes, and one of them, Guimaraes , scored the winner seven minutes later. On Tuesday the three he sent on at 65 minutes were involved in both goals that followed inside six minutes, Saka with a goal and an assist and Havertz with an assist. Arteta called the timing of Tuesday's change instinctive. I felt it was the right moment to make the triple substitution with the way the game was panning out , he said, and he spread the credit: that's credit to the starters, and as well the ones who come in to create those moments. It is a striking contrast with the start of the season, and with Arsenal Women, whose problem this autumn has been exactly the opposite: games drifting away the moment the changes are made. No WSL matches were played between 7 and 13 October. Off the Pitch Ken Friar, 1934 to 2026: the boy who chased a ball and stayed eighty years The club's life president died aged 92. He saw the men's team win twenty-five major honours under seven managers, the last of them in May. On Tuesday 13 October Arsenal announced the death of Ken Friar OBE. It is with profound sadness that we announce the death of Life President Ken Friar OBE , the club's statement began. It went on to say that no one has had an influence on the club quite like Mr Friar . His story is the kind that clubs no longer produce. He was born in Islington on 13 August 1934. In 1946, aged twelve, he was retrieving a ball outside Highbury when the manager, George Allison , noticed him. He was given a job running messages from the box office for half a crown a week, and joined the permanent staff in 1950. He became club secretary in 1973, succeeding Bob Wall , and managing director in 1983, appointed by Peter Hill-Wood . As managing director he handled player and manager contracts. With director Danny Fiszman , he was central to the move from Highbury to the Emirates, which opened in 2006. He received an OBE for services to football in 2000 and the freedom of Islington in 2004. He stepped down from the board in 2020, after seventy-four years of service, and became life president. The bridge that links the stadium with the surrounding streets is named after him, and a statue at its entrance shows him as a boy playing football outside Highbury. This week, scarves and flowers were laid there. It's a really sad day for everybody that loves Arsenal Football Club or anybody that has come across him. Mikel Arteta , after Lille The Emirates held a moment of reflection before the Lille game and stood to applaud. Afterwards Arteta said : I had the privilege, the honour to meet him, to spend time with him, to learn from him. Former players followed. Tony Adams called him the epitomisation of all that Arsenal stands for . David Seaman said: Ken Friar is an Arsenal icon and his achievements will never be forgotten. Charlie George , speaking to Arsenal.com, said: He knew everything and every person in the building. Supporters' groups joined in. The Arsenal Supporters' Trust said Ken's extraordinary lifetime of service to Arsenal speaks volumes about his loyalty, dedication and love for the club. A fuller tribute, arranged with his family, is planned for the home game against Everton on 24 October. In a 2012 interview with the journalist Nick Ames , quoted again this week, he explained himself in a sentence: But look, I work because I love the place and the people. The Golden State Valkyries, an expansion team in only their second season, swept the defending-champion Las Vegas Aces and host Games 1 and 2 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Saturday and Monday. No WNBA Finals game has ever been played in San Francisco. Two are now guaranteed. Then the building barely cools. The Warriors come home to open against Memphis on October 23 and play seven home games before November 10. Down in San Jose the Earthquakes have three home games left in the regular season, and Bay FC close their season at PayPal Park on November 1. Outside the arenas it is peak autumn. Half Moon Bay's pumpkin festival, Oakland's Autumn Lights, A Toast to Sausalito and the Potrero Hill R&B Festival all land on the same weekend, and Market Street fills with free performances for a single evening on October 17. Day of the Dead season runs from a 21-and-over NightLife at the Academy of Sciences on October 22 to a Symphony concert and Redwood City's altars on November 7 and 8. Wine Road's Sonoma weekend and a Diwali night market in Yerba Buena Gardens close the window. The weekend read Dry and warming, with no rain expected through Sunday. Monday is clear with a high near 66, Tuesday turns overcast west of Twin Peaks with gusts to 20mph, Wednesday is sunny near 72, and Thursday spikes to around 82. Two cautions. A Coastal Flood Advisory runs through Tuesday afternoon, and the National Weather Service warns of sneaker waves and breakers up to 20 feet at exposed beaches: stay off jetties, piers and rocks. Fire-weather concern rises inland later in the week as it dries out. Pick of the Month WNBA Finals Games 1 and 2: Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream Saturday October 17, 12:30pm, and Monday October 19, 5pm · Chase Center, 1 Warriors Way, San Francisco · Ticketed, online only The reason is scarcity, not hype. The Valkyries made the playoffs in their first season, and in their second they are the only expansion team in WNBA history to reach the Finals in year two. They got there by sweeping the defending champions, closing it out 87-77 in overtime in Las Vegas on October 9. Chase Center is down for Games 1, 2, 5 and 7, but only the first two are certain to be played. Games 3 and 4 are in Atlanta on October 21 and 24. If the series ends in four or five, Monday night may be the last WNBA Finals game San Francisco sees for years. Street fairs come round every autumn, and the Warriors play 41 home games. This does not repeat. Practical advice: Saturday tips at 12:30pm on NBC and Monday at 5pm on USA, so leave time for security. Game 1 ticket holders get a violet Finals t-shirt. Take Muni's T Third to the UCSF/Chase Center stop rather than driving, and if you are in the area early on Saturday, the free Bay Area Science Festival is running on the UCSF campus next door. In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Editor’s note, 26 October This edition was never produced at the time. It has been written now for the archive and covers 1 to 7 October 2026. It is written as of Wednesday 7 October, so nothing below uses what happened afterwards, and the fixtures under What to Watch are listed as they were scheduled then. The Lead The clock started at 7pm on Thursday Manchester City have appealed. The verdict stands until a new panel says otherwise, the punishment has not been set, and the timetable for both is now the most important document in English football. T he deadline was Friday. Manchester City did not wait for it. The club confirmed on Thursday 1 October that it had lodged its appeal at 7pm that evening, against the independent commission that found it guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. The appeal went to the Chair of the Premier League’s Judicial Panel, ITV News reported . The league says the Appeal Board hearing will stay private and confidential until its outcome can be published. City ’s statement repeated the line it has held since the verdict. The commission’s opinion, it said, contains “clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.” It added, without qualification: “The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League.” “This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history.” Richard Masters , Premier League chief executive What the appeal is actually about The commission found that sponsorship income booked by the club was, in large part, not paid by the sponsors at all. NBC Sports’ summary of the findings puts it at around 87 per cent of the reported commercial income over the period, supplied instead through the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group. City ’s central argument, as ITV describes it, is that government funding through the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Court helped sponsors meet their obligations. The commission rejected that account as a narrative built after the fact. That is the ground the appeal will be fought on: not whether money moved, but whose money it was. The timetable, and why it matters The Premier League handbook says an appeal hearing must finish within twelve weeks of being lodged. Counted from 1 October, that lands on Christmas Eve. The appeal panel then has 30 days to rule, which points to a decision in January. There are two catches. Sports Mole noted that it is unclear whether these fast-track rules apply to a case that began before they were introduced. And City ’s chief executive Ferran Soriano has warned that the process could take considerably longer. Route and key facts The Premier League v Manchester City The charges Serious breaches of financial rules over nine seasons, 2009/10 to 2017/18, plus charges of failing to co-operate with the investigation. The verdict Guilty of all the serious-breach charges and most of the co-operation charges. Communicated on 24 September, redacted decision published on 29 September. The appeal Lodged at 7pm on Thursday 1 October, a day inside the deadline. Heard in private by a fresh panel. The clock Hearing to finish within twelve weeks, around 24 December. Ruling within 30 days of the hearing, so likely January 2027. The sanction A separate hearing, with no date set. City can appeal any sanction too. Waiting in the wings Arsenal , Liverpool , Manchester United and Tottenham , who reserved the right to claim compensation in 2024. The Football Association is reviewing the findings. The punishment nobody has priced yet The sanction is a separate process, and nobody has said when it will be heard. Several Premier League clubs want it settled before the end of this season, according to The Sun as relayed by Sports Mole, and believe the new fast-track rules should apply. The precedents are small next to the scale of this case. Everton lost eight points across two profitability cases in 2023/24. Nottingham Forest lost four. Those were single-season accounting breaches; this is nine seasons and a finding of deliberate concealment. The Football Association has added another layer. It said it is reviewing the commission’s findings, that the decision has “significant implications for the integrity of the game”, and that it may act where appropriate. It will say nothing more while proceedings continue. The second front: money Four clubs preserved the right to sue back in 2024: Arsenal , Manchester United , Liverpool and Tottenham . The Independent has reported they are planning to act, with a combined claim of around 200m pounds discussed. The Times put the potential exposure to rival claims at more than 100m pounds. None of that can start yet. Legal action can only begin once the case and its appeals are finished, which is another reason the January date matters so much. And the football carries on Through all of this, City are top. Enzo Maresca ’s side have won all five league games and lead on fifteen points. Their first match back from the break is at Anfield on Sunday, against Liverpool . That is the strange shape of the autumn. The club playing the best football in England is also the club whose place in the league depends on a hearing held in private before Christmas. Every point City win between now and January is a point that may or may not count for anything. The bill for the longest break in memory Club football in Europe’s big leagues has been dark since 20 September. As it ends, the clubs are counting what four internationals in one window cost them. FIFA’s new calendar folded two international windows into one this autumn. National teams played up to four matches between 24 September and 6 October, and the big European leagues paused for three weekends. It returns this Friday. Niko Kovac spoke for a lot of coaches on Wednesday. “Those four games were definitely too many for me. The break was too long,” the Borussia Dortmund coach said, in comments carried by dpa . His point was not only about injuries. “We also had two and a half weeks with no rhythm at all,” he said. That matters for a side that won its first four league games and leads the Bundesliga. “When you have to play four games, there’s a lot of travel, and the squads are relatively small.” Niko Kovac , Borussia Dortmund coach Dortmund ’s own list shows why. Konstantinos Karetsas and Daniel Svensson came back with colds. Nico Schlotterbeck hurt an ankle in Germany training and is doubtful for Friday. Julian Ryerson is nursing a knock from a collision. In Barcelona the worry is Raphinha . He left the Brazil squad early with muscular swelling in his right thigh after the win over Australia . Early signs were not serious, but Marca reported that Hansi Flick will not rush him back. The reason is last season. Raphinha hurt the same thigh on Brazil duty in September 2025, his return was accelerated, and he broke down again. He then missed 58 days and 13 matches, Sports Mole recalled . Napoli had problems before the break and have more after it. Tuttomercatoweb reported on Wednesday that Antonio Vergara has a strain of the right soleus and will miss at least four or five matches. Mati Olivera came back from Uruguay with a groin problem. Costantino Favasuli , hurt with Italy ’s under-21s, is probably out until after the November break. They join a list that already included Alex Meret , Alessandro Buongiorno , Scott McTominay and Frank Anguissa . That leaves Massimiliano Allegri with nine matches between 10 October and 4 November, and a squad that is thinner than it has been all season. Elsewhere the damage had been done earlier in the window. Real Madrid diagnosed Kylian Mbappe with a hyperextension of the back of his left knee, picked up while scoring for France against Turkiye , and said he would be out for two weeks or more. Bayern Munich lost Jamal Musiala to a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh in the warm-up for Germany ’s game with the Netherlands . Transfer News Certainty tracker Where this week’s threads actually sit Medical passed, awaiting the league Dani Carvajal to Getafe , free. Needs La Liga to approve the club’s spending position. Wants out, no deal JJ Gabriel , Manchester United . Turned 16 on Tuesday. Barcelona and Real Madrid reported as favourites. Concrete interest, club says no Alex Scott , Bournemouth . Not for sale in January, per talkSPORT. Preliminary contact Nick Woltemade and Bayern Munich , per Tuttosport. Nothing imminent. Noise Erling Haaland to Barcelona , from an unverified social-media account. The sixteen-year-old who wants to leave Manchester United JJ Gabriel turned 16 on Tuesday. That was the day he was due to sign scholarship terms at Carrington. Instead, the talk is of Barcelona and Madrid . JJ Gabriel is the most talked-about academy player in England. He has 29 goals in 32 games for Manchester United ’s under-18s and has already scored twice in two Premier League 2 matches. He made his senior debut in a pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid this summer. Last month he told the club he wanted to leave. He turned 16 on Tuesday 6 October, and Sports Mole reported that day that his time at United is “seemingly coming to an end”. The German journalist Florian Plettenberg names Real Madrid and Barcelona as favourites. Both are said to be ready to offer a large salary, bonuses and a signing-on fee. Bayern Munich are described as interested but behind. The player reportedly prefers Barcelona . He has trained there since announcing he wanted to go, and his family are regular visitors. The route matters as much as the destination. A move to a club in the European Union at 16 depends on holding the right passport. Plettenberg reports that Gabriel is set to receive a Cypriot passport through his mother, which would make a free move possible in January. There is friction too. His representatives were said to be angry that he was left out of United ’s Champions League squad against Sabah . They had wanted him to get at least 20 minutes in that game and in matches against Brighton and Bournemouth . Where it stands Player wants out and clubs are circling. No agreement with any club has been reported, and United have not released him. The passport route is single-sourced. Carvajal picks Getafe , if La Liga allows it A six-time European champion with Real Madrid has said yes to a club on the southern edge of the city. The last word belongs to the league’s accountants. Dani Carvajal is 34 and has been a free agent since his Real Madrid contract ended on 30 June. He has not played an official match since. This week he chose his next club, and it is Getafe . This week, Getafe president Angel Torres confirmed that Carvajal had passed a medical and that the agreement with the player was closed. Fabrizio Romano reported a verbal agreement too, citing ABC. Coach Jose Bordalas called the player himself to explain his role, and the response was positive. The terms of the contract, including its length, have not been published. Where it stands Agreed with the player, medical passed. Getafe still need La Liga to approve the registration under the club’s squad-cost limit, and Torres said it cannot be called final until then. The obstacle is the spending cap. Getafe operate with far less room than the clubs Carvajal spent his career with, and Bordalas admitted as much in September. Even a free transfer has to fit under the limit, and that is now a conversation between the club and the league. Bournemouth put up the closed sign for Scott Chelsea are expected to come back for Alex Scott . Bournemouth have already given their answer. Bournemouth will not sell Alex Scott in January, talkSPORT reported, as relayed by SoccerNews on 7 October . Club sources say he stays until at least the end of the season. Chelsea had a bid of around 64m pounds turned down in the summer and are said to be preparing another. Real Madrid are also watching. Scott , 23, has not agreed a new contract, which will keep the story alive. A week earlier, the journalist Dean Jones had reported the same stance for Flashscore and put Bournemouth ’s valuation at around 110m euros. Treat that number as an estimate, not an asking price. Where it stands Concrete interest, no sale sanctioned. Two separate reports agree on Bournemouth ’s position. The Rumour Mill What else is moving, and how much of it is real Everything simmering, with the reliability stated plainly. The windows are shut, so almost all of this is about January or next summer. Preliminary contact Bayern Munich have been in touch with the representatives of Nick Woltemade , Tuttosport reported via Sport Witness on 29 September. The forward is on loan at Juventus from Newcastle United . Newcastle would reportedly want about 60m euros to sell next summer. The report itself stresses that nothing is imminent. Certainty: early contact only. Contract work in progress Real Madrid were reported by AS in mid-September to be preparing a new deal for Thibaut Courtois to June 2028. His current contract runs to 2027. Nothing has been announced. Certainty: talks reported, no agreement confirmed. Noise, and treat it that way The story that Erling Haaland will join Barcelona in 2027 came from a transfer “insider” on X, citing unnamed Barcelona sources. No club or player has said anything. The Spanish paper Sport reported that Haaland ’s contract, which runs to 2034, has no release clause for relegation or anything else. That is the useful fact here. Certainty: noise. Stated needs The most reliable guide to January is not names but gaps. Napoli ’s injury list is long and getting longer. Manchester United may be about to lose their best academy prospect for little more than training compensation. Getafe are trying to fit a free agent under a spending cap. Watch those three before you watch the gossip. Around the Leagues No top-flight league in Europe played this week. This is a round of standings, injuries and what comes next. Leeds United arrive at the Emirates on Saturday unbeaten, and the champions still cannot say where the next one is coming from. T he last competitive football Arsenal played was on 19 September, and it was awful. Brighton and Hove Albion pressed them man for man, watched them panic and won 3-0. Pascal Gross curled in from distance after half an hour. Charalampos Kostoulas struck fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had been denied at the other end. Chema Andres headed in a Gross corner nine minutes after the break. Mikel Arteta said his side did not respect the game and were extremely poor technically . Then the international calendar swallowed three weeks whole. The table says the damage was contained. Arsenal are second on twelve points from five, three behind Manchester City , who have won all five. Four goals conceded is championship-grade. The problem is at the other end. Eight scored is the lowest in the top seven and exactly half of Brighton 's sixteen. It is not hard to see why. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal for a club-record sixty million pounds in August, Leandro Trossard to Besiktas , Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Christos Tzolis , bought from Club Brugge for thirty-four million as Trossard 's replacement, is out with a hamstring strain. Kai Havertz pulled a hamstring for Germany and is a doubt. Noni Madueke has drifted so far out of the picture that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are watching. And Viktor Gyokeres , the centre-forward, has five Arsenal appearances and no goals. We have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can’t happen again. Mikel Arteta , after Brighton What Arsenal do have is the thing that won them the league. Nicolas Jover 's routines produced a Premier League record from corners last season, and the league responded over the summer with fresh instruction to referees to clamp down on holding and wrestling in the box at set-pieces. Five games in, the champions' first-choice route to goal is being refereed differently and their open-play alternative has been sold. That is why January already feels load-bearing. Saturday is harder than the names suggest. Leeds United are fifth and unbeaten, two wins and three draws, with three goals conceded in five matches. Only Brighton have a better defensive record. They are the opposite of the fixture Arsenal need: a low block with a tidy structure, against a side with no left winger and a striker without a goal. Arteta 's questions are not about shape. They are about who plays in front of Gyokeres , and whether Eberechi Eze or Dowman is trusted to unpick an organised defence. Behind that, the defence is a jigsaw. William Saliba has not played since July, when he came off in the first half of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain with a back problem he had carried for weeks. L'Equipe report he is targeting November. Ezri Konsa , the fifty-one million pound answer to that absence, was released by England with a quad complaint after ninety minutes against both Spain and Croatia . Gabriel Magalhaes and Piero Hincapie can cover, but a 12:30 kick-off on the first weekend back is exactly when a patched back four gets found out. The record-breaker who cannot score for Arsenal Viktor Gyokeres spent the break rewriting the Nations League record book. He returns to a club where he has not scored all season. Earlier this week in Bucharest he scored the only goal of a 1-0 win over Romania , pouncing on the rebound after Sebastian Nanasi 's shot came off the post. It was his seventh consecutive Nations League match with a goal, a competition record , past Aleksandar Mitrovic and Benjamin Sesko , and his twenty-fifth for Sweden, moving him ahead of Marcus Berg . He had scored against Bosnia and Herzegovina on 3 October too. Two columns tell the story: for Sweden four appearances and four goals, for Arsenal five appearances and none. Sofascore rated him 6.5 against Manchester City , 6.4 against Chelsea , 6.6 at Napoli , 6.2 at Ipswich Town , 6.5 at Brighton . The uncomfortable reading is that this is a supply problem rather than a finishing one: Arsenal , with Martinelli and Trossard sold and Saka carrying the width almost alone, give him possession and few crosses worth attacking. Transfer News The winger hunt is already on, and Leipzig is where it starts Arsenal did not sign a left-sided attacker in the summer. Five games into a title defence, the January search has a name attached to it. David Ornstein set the frame before the season began. Asked in a Q and A for The Athletic whether Arsenal would sign an attacker in January, he said: I could see something happening because they wanted to, I thought they needed to, in the summer and they didn't. He noted the club has money but operates close to UEFA's financial limits. Summer pursuits of Vinicius Junior , Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers all came to nothing. On Tuesday a name arrived. CaughtOffside's Ahad Shaukat reported , citing sources close to the agents industry, that Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig is now Arsenal 's top January target, with Andrea Berta preparing a fresh approach after the club looked at him in the summer and moved on. Nusa is twenty-one, a Norway international, and exactly the profile Arsenal no longer have: a left-sided dribbler who can beat a man. Ole Werner , his coach at Leipzig , has said of him: He is a player who will be world class in the near future. Mind the certainty tier: a single-sourced report of concrete interest, not advanced talks, with no fee attached and no Leipzig -side corroboration in the German media yet, which is usually where a deal like this surfaces first. What makes it worth reporting is that it fits Arsenal 's stated need. The alternative on the same list, Kenan Yildiz of Juventus at around eighty-five million pounds, is a January fantasy rather than a January plan. Madueke is drifting, and Europe has noticed One goal, a shrinking role and two Champions League clubs watching. Noni Madueke is in the Arsenal Champions League squad and barely in the team. He has one goal and a role that has contracted as Arteta has leaned on Saka and Eze , and Sports Mole reported this week that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are both monitoring him ahead of January, with Arsenal braced for bids. Twelve clubs, one sixteen-year-old, and a decision Arteta keeps deferring Max Dowman scored twice at Ipswich Town , was called up by England and sent off by England under-19s inside three weeks. Dowman scored twice in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town, is the highest-rated player in the under-21 side and already has two senior goals, more than Gyokeres . Reporting in late September put loan enquiries into double figures, more than twelve approaches, with Arteta publicly open-minded about letting him go for regular minutes. He assisted and was then sent off for England under-19s against the United States on Friday, then withdrew with an impact injury, having been named in Thomas Tuchel 's senior England group before being released alongside Konsa . A sale funding a purchase is the only version of January that fits all three. If Madueke 's situation hardens into a bid, expect the Nusa story to accelerate. The Squad A back four held together, and a manager committing to five more years The break cost Arsenal two forwards and returned four fit players. Meanwhile Arteta and his entire coaching staff are being tied to 2030. Arsenal lost Christos Tzolis to a hamstring strain inside twenty minutes of Greece's 2-2 draw with the Netherlands , reported at two to three weeks, which takes out Saturday, Lille and probably Nottingham Forest . They lost Kai Havertz to a hamstring problem in the 1-1 draw between the Netherlands and Germany, Jurgen Klopp 's first game in charge of the Germans, with the German federation calling it a muscle strain and Klopp hoping he would be relatively quickly available again . They also nearly lost the centre-back they bought to fix a centre-back problem. Ezri Konsa played ninety minutes against Spain and ninety against Croatia carrying a quad complaint and was sent home before Tuesday's game with Czechia . Thomas Tuchel put it plainly: He played versus Spain, which made it worse. He tried everything for Croatia and gave the green light. He got another hit on the quad, and it caused some light trauma. Against that, four returns: Ben White (groin), Piero Hincapie (muscular), Cristhian Mosquera (hamstring, out since late August) and Declan Rice , held out of the England squad and rested in Dubai. Selection: the shape of a thin attack If Havertz does not make it, the options for a 12:30 kick-off against the division's second-best defence are Gyokeres through the middle, Saka right, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard in the creative positions, and a choice on the left between Noni Madueke , out of the picture, and Max Dowman , sixteen and coming off a red card and a knock. Mikel Merino is the hybrid who gives height in the box. Set-pieces, and the contracts that follow Arsenal 's dead-ball operation was the biggest competitive advantage in English football last season, producing a Premier League record from corners. Over the summer the league instructed officials to take a stricter line on holding and wrestling in the penalty area at set-pieces. Which makes the contract news interesting. Nicolas Jover is in talks over a new deal, and Daily Cannon reported on Tuesday that Andrea Berta is leading the negotiation personally. Arsenal's staff and players remain very much aligned on the value of set-pieces, and the club are willing to recognise that with a good contract , the report said. Above him, Mikel Arteta has agreed a four-year contract expected to run to June 2030, first reported by Sami Mokbel for the BBC in late September and corroborated by ESPN and the Irish Times, with Fabrizio Romano adding it carries a rise on his existing salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. The agreement remains verbal and formally unannounced. The Athletic reported the whole coaching staff will sign for the same four years: Albert Stuivenberg , Jover , Inaki Cana , Miguel Molina and, on enhanced terms, Gabriel Heinze . Arsenal Women Tenth, four goals in five, and a manager insisting she still has the board Arsenal have surrendered leads in three of their last four matches. The expected-goals numbers say the problem starts the moment Renee Slegers makes a substitution. This is the second-worst start to a Women's Super League season in Arsenal 's history. They are not being outplayed. They are being out-finished and out-lasted. One win in five, two draws, two defeats, five points, four goals scored and six conceded, tenth in a fourteen-team league. Manchester City lead on fifteen. Sunday at the Etihad was the clearest version yet. Lisa Baum put Arsenal ahead on forty-three. Lauren Hemp equalised in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo curled Arsenal back in front five minutes after the break. Then Kika Casparaji levelled on sixty-three, Hemp scored again on seventy-two and Georgia Shaw added a fourth on eighty-four. Manchester City 4-2 Arsenal , from a position of control, for the second time in a week. The first time was in Paris. Arsenal led Paris FC 2-0 in the Champions League on 30 September and drew 2-2, with Leah Williamson conceding a penalty . Slegers did not attend the post-match press conference, later explaining that it was important to spend time with the players after the game . They get immediate effect when they make their changes. We haven’t had the same effect as last season. Renee Slegers , after Manchester City Tim Stillman 's analysis for Arseblog put numbers on it. Against Paris FC , Arsenal were 2-0 up having generated 1.3 expected goals; over the following forty minutes of substitutions that rose only to 1.7, and they conceded twice in the final eighteen minutes. Against HB Koge the xG line totally flatlined between the 65th and 85th minutes . The full piece is worth reading . Stillman 's diagnosis is a squad-profile problem. Geraldine Reuteler , signed from Eintracht Frankfurt after a year of pursuit, has barely been used. Selina Cerci has four appearances totalling fifty-nine minutes. Mariona Caldentey is played wide, which fields four midfielders and leaves Arsenal with nobody to stretch a low block. Some of this is the cost of the most aggressive overhaul in the club's modern history. Seven players arrived and thirteen left . In came Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig , Isabella Damm from Brondby , plus Reuteler and Cerci . Out went Beth Mead to Manchester City after nine years, Katie McCabe to Chelsea , Victoria Pelova to Tottenham Hotspur , Laia Codina to West Ham United and Manuela Zinsberger to Borussia Dortmund . That is a rebuild, not a refresh. Slegers was unambiguous about her position on Sunday. She told reporters there is a strong togetherness and I've really felt [the board's] support , naming Clare Wheatley , Richard Garlick , James King and Jodie Taylor , and added: I believe in the potential that we possess. She is the manager who won the Champions League in 2025 after taking over as interim. She has earned time. Europe is salvageable. A 1-0 win over HB Koge and the 2-2 in Paris leaves Arsenal unbeaten in the league phase, with Benfica at home on 28 October, Barcelona away on 11 November, OL Lyonnes at home on 19 November and Inter away in December. Off the Pitch Arsenal will not be building a bigger stadium After months of speculation about 80,000 seats and a temporary move to Wembley, the club has chosen renovation over reconstruction. Arteta was one of the voices against. Arsenal have ruled out a major expansion of Emirates Stadium. The decision was communicated at an Arsenal Advisory Board meeting, where co-chair Josh Kroenke and chief executive Richard Garlick said the club had shared a commitment to continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge scale masterplan . Arseblog News reported the detail and the decision was confirmed elsewhere the same week. The option on the table was a rebuild taking capacity to around eighty thousand, which would have required Arsenal to play home matches at Wembley during construction. Mikel Arteta opposed that, concerned about severing the connection between team and supporters at the moment the club had rebuilt it. Capacity stays at 60,704. Instead come smaller things: expanded hospitality and retail, a catering identity called 1886 by Arsenal with Legends Global, 5G and stadium-wide connectivity, seat refurbishment and concourse work. Safe standing is already operational in the Clock End, with the North Bank to follow in 2027-28. The commercial logic is not subtle. Arsenal 's matchday income passed one hundred and fifty-four million pounds in 2024-25, and premium hospitality yields several times general admission per seat. It is also, for anyone who has spent a decade on a season-ticket waiting list, the end of a hope. The verdict that landed while Arsenal were away Manchester City were found guilty of more than a hundred financial breaches on 29 September. Arsenal are one of four clubs reported to be preparing a claim. On 29 September an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all the serious charges brought by the Premier League, covering 2009-10 to 2017-18. The commission concluded the club had arranged what it described as sham contracts and used schemes to inflate revenues artificially, with figures above nine hundred million pounds cited in reporting of the findings. Manchester City say they are disappointed and surprised, maintain the opinion contains clear material errors, and have appealed. No sanction has been imposed. Guilt and punishment are separate stages. Sky Sports reported that rival clubs do not expect Manchester City to be in the top flight next season if the appeal fails, and that a single-season points deduction is widely regarded as insufficient. The appeal is expected before Christmas. The Arsenal angle is twofold. First, money. Arsenal joined Manchester United , Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur in reserving the right to seek compensation in November 2024, because the Limitation Act allows six years for breach-of-contract claims. The Independent has since reported the four clubs are now planning to launch an action, with combined claims potentially exceeding two hundred million pounds. Arsenal finished fifth in 2016-17 and were runners-up to Manchester City in 2022-23 and 2023-24. Second, the table. Manchester City are top with a perfect record and Arsenal are three points behind. Any sanction applied this season would reshape a title race Arsenal are currently losing by the margin of one game. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, told properly Wednesday Edition · 30 September 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Guilty: the verdict that rewrites nine seasons of English football An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of serious financial wrongdoing across nine seasons, ruling that the club inflated its revenues and cut its costs by more than £900 million through contracts it called commercial and the panel called sham. The sanction is still to come. Everything about the Premier League now bends around it. The document that landed on Tuesday afternoon runs to a redacted core decision and a conclusion that leaves almost no room to stand. An independent commission, appointed under Premier League rules, found Manchester City guilty of every charge relating to serious breaches of the league's financial regulations across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. It also upheld three of the four charges alleging that the club failed to co-operate with the investigation that produced them. In the panel's words, by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the rules, and it made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the league's inquiry. The mechanism, as the commission describes it, was not a rounding error or an accounting disagreement. Commercial partners were required to pay only part of the sponsorship fees that appeared in the club's books, with the remainder funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment and Development, the ownership vehicle. Other arrangements allowed costs to be recorded at artificially low levels. Between them, the panel found, these structures inflated revenue and suppressed expenditure by more than £900 million, roughly $1.2 billion, across the period in question. Accounts were misstated. Auditors and regulators were kept from the real picture. Both Premier League and UEFA spending limits were breached, substantially. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters put the finding in a single sentence: the core decision, he said, details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. That is the sort of language a regulator uses when it believes it has won. “By its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules.” The independent commission, in the redacted core decision How the public came to know is its own story, and not a flattering one for the league. The commission's decision was communicated on Thursday 24 September. Club executives were briefed at a shareholders' meeting the same day and asked to sign non-disclosure agreements. Within about a day the substance was in The Guardian, The Athletic, the BBC, The Times and on Sky Sports. The Premier League then published its redacted core decision on Tuesday 29 September, five days after the parties who stand to claim compensation had already been told the outcome. Several outlets have characterised the ruling as 114 of 115 charges proven; the league's own statement simply says all charges of serious breach, plus three of four on co-operation. City's response was defiant and carefully lawyered. The club said it was disappointed and surprised, insisted a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence supports its positions, and declared that it would be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums. The opinion, it argued, contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. It noted pointedly that it had respected due process for eight years on the understanding that the Premier League board would behave as an impartial regulator free from partisan influence. Chief executive Ferran Soriano took no questions. The Case: Route to the Verdict Origin Football Leaks documents obtained by Rui Pinto and published from 2018 triggered scrutiny of the club's sponsorship structures. UEFA A two-year European ban imposed in February 2020 was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which left a €10 million fine in place. Charged February 2023, after a four-year Premier League investigation, with more than 100 alleged breaches. Hearing A closed hearing before an independent commission, held over a period of months. Verdict Communicated Thursday 24 September 2026. Reported publicly by Friday 25 September. Redacted core decision published Tuesday 29 September. Appeal window City have until Friday 2 October to appeal to a fresh three-person commission under Section W of the rules. There is no route to CAS, though a High Court challenge alleging procedural unfairness remains open. Sanction A separate hearing, still to be listed. The Times reports it is expected within weeks rather than months. Sources: Premier League statement, 29 September 2026; Sky Sports; The Times; Al Jazeera. Which brings us to the only question anyone in England is actually asking. What does it cost? The Premier League deliberately publishes no tariff, on the reasonable theory that a fixed price for cheating is simply a budget line. The commission has discretion to fine, to deduct points, to impose other sporting sanctions, and in theory to expel. Expulsion is the exotic option and worth understanding properly: it would not relegate City to the Championship. A club outside the league is outside the pyramid, and would have to apply to the Football Association to rejoin, entering the English Football League at League Two subject to a majority vote of EFL clubs. The Premier League would be left with nineteen teams and, most likely, two relegation places that season. The realistic range is a points deduction, and the precedent ledger is where the argument will be fought. Everton lost eight points in total in 2023/24 across two profitability cases, six of them after a successful appeal against an initial ten. Nottingham Forest lost four in the same season. Further down the pyramid, Derby County were docked 21 points in 2021/22 and Luton Town 30 in 2008/09. The football finance academic Kieran Maguire has suggested that a proportionate penalty here would sit between 40 and 60 points, which would have placed City eighteenth last season. Figures inside other clubs, according to The Times, want a deduction heavy enough to amount in practice to relegation. Precedent: points deductions in English football Luton Town, 2008/09 (agent payments and improper administration exit) 30 pts Derby County, 2021/22 (administration and financial irregularities) 21 pts Everton, 2023/24 (two profitability cases, combined) 8 pts Nottingham Forest, 2023/24 (profitability) 4 pts Chart built from published sanctions. No penalty has yet been set in the Manchester City case, and the commission is not bound by any of these figures. Then there is the second front, which may ultimately cost more than any deduction. Several Premier League clubs have already taken legal advice on compensation claims, the BBC reports, arguing that City's conduct affected their own league positions, European qualification or, in the worst case, their relegation. The template exists. In June, Burnley won a £35 million settlement from Everton on exactly that reasoning, a decision Everton are appealing. Multiply that logic across nine seasons and a dozen aggrieved clubs and the exposure becomes genuinely existential, whatever happens to the points column. The cruellest detail is the football. Manchester City go into October top of the Premier League with a perfect record: five wins from five, fifteen points, seven consecutive victories in all competitions under Enzo Maresca , who replaced Pep Guardiola in the summer and has lost only the Community Shield. Erling Haaland leads the division's scoring charts. Reports in Spain say there is no relegation release clause in Haaland's contract, which runs to 2034, though nobody at the Etihad pretends a severe sanction would leave the squad intact. Sponsors, the Mirror reports, are already examining their agreements against the possibility of a season without European football. Guardiola himself broke cover on Wednesday, posting that he wanted every City supporter to know he was there, more than ever, behind his club, his owner, his chairman, Ferran Soriano , the players, the staff, Maresca and the fans, and adding that they would get through it together. Maresca had been more oblique on Sunday, posting a line of Socrates on Instagram: the only thing I know is that I know nothing. Time to breathe, he added. Time to analyse. Time to learn. There is one more layer of irony, and it is not small. This is the first season of the Premier League's new financial architecture. Profitability and Sustainability Rules expired with 2025/26. In their place sits the Squad Cost Ratio, which caps on-pitch spending at 85 per cent of football revenue adjusted for player trading, with a multi-year allowance to exceed that by 30 percentage points at a financial cost, alongside a Sustainability and Systemic Resilience test of working capital, liquidity and positive equity. The league built a new rulebook and, in the same autumn, found that the old one had been dismantled from the inside for the better part of a decade. Whatever the sanction, that is the finding that will follow English football around. Secondary Feature The window that ate October: inside FIFA's first XL break Club football stopped on 20 September and does not restart until 10 October. In the gap, an experiment: four internationals instead of two, three weeks instead of one, and a Nations League that has already produced the result of the year. FIFA's answer to a crowded calendar was to consolidate rather than trim. The September window ran from 24 September to 6 October, national teams were handed up to four fixtures rather than the customary two, and the October break was abolished altogether. Add the buffer either side and the big five European leagues are dark from 20 September to 10 October. The stated logic is player welfare and travel: with the World Cup final falling on 19 July, the season started late and FIFA wanted two international windows a season rather than three. The remaining breaks are 9 to 17 November, 22 to 30 March and 7 to 15 June. UEFA slotted the Champions League league phase around it, with matchday one on 8 to 10 September and matchday two not until 13 and 14 October. The effect on the ground is strange and, for a European league fan, slightly disorienting. Three weekends without domestic football is not a pause, it is a mid-season break. Lower divisions in England kept playing. MLS took a fortnight off its own run-in. And the international game, handed the entire stage, has filled it. Start with the only story that can compete with Manchester for column inches. Greece have beaten Germany for the first time. Dimitris Kourbelis scored the goal, deflected, on 75 minutes in Augsburg on Sunday, and Jürgen Klopp lost his first match as Germany head coach on his home debut. Klopp took the blame without flinching: the line-up and the many changes, he said, were 100 per cent on him. He also insisted he would rather have a bad start than a bad ending. Captain Joshua Kimmich was blunter, describing a side that struggled against a deep block and was too static and not creative enough. Germany have one point from two; Greece have six and lead the group. Elsewhere the new managers are mostly thriving. Zinédine Zidane has won both with France , 1-0 in Türkiye through Kylian Mbappé and 1-0 in Belgium through a slaloming solo goal from Michael Olise two minutes from time. Jorge Jesus has won both with Portugal , with João Félix scoring in each. Xavi Hernández began at Netherlands with a 1-1 draw against Germany rescued by a Cody Gakpo volley in added time, then won 2-1 in Serbia through two goals from debutant Mexx Meerdink . Roberto Mancini 's Italy lost 2-0 at home to Belgium and then went to Türkiye and won 4-1, Pio Esposito and Michael Kayode among the scorers. And the world champions keep winning. Spain came to Wembley on Saturday and beat England 3-2, a result that will feel familiar to anyone who watched the last two finals these sides have contested. Lamine Yamal scored inside two minutes, Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane turned it around before half time, Kane struck the bar from the penalty spot on 54 minutes, and then Álex Baena equalised on 60 and Mikel Oyarzabal won it on 74. Three days later Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 in Seville with Yamal scoring twice. Thomas Tuchel 's England recovered by winning 2-0 in Czechia against ten men, Gordon and Kane again. The bill for all this arrives at the training grounds. Mbappé suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee in Türkiye and is expected to miss around two to three weeks, which for Real Madrid compounds a defensive injury list that already included Ibrahima Konaté and Fede Valverde . Jamal Musiala tore a muscle fibre in his right thigh. Gakpo went off with an ankle problem seventeen minutes into the Serbia game; Alexander Isak returned to Liverpool with a thigh complaint. Sunderland lost Brian Brobbey to a hamstring, Manchester United fear the same for Patrick Dorgu , and Barcelona had a scare with Eric García 's left knee before tests found nothing wrong. Four matches instead of two was always going to read like this. Also This Week The fight for FIFA reaches a Florida courtroom The other governance war escalated sharply. On Wednesday the Swiss Football Association withdrew its support for Gianni Infantino 's re-election as FIFA president, a remarkable rebuke from his home federation, which had pledged backing as recently as June. The Swiss cited two things: the secretive FIFA Forward Enterprise plan to sell stakes in World Cup commercial operations, revealed on 28 July and abandoned within days, and pressure from United States president Donald Trump not to impose a mandatory one-match ban on the USA forward Folarin Balogun after a red card against Belgium at the World Cup. Credibility, transparency, accountability and effective statutory bodies, the federation said, are essential to trust in the governance of the game. A day earlier, FIFA had filed a 21-page response through the law firm Linklaters in the Southern District of Florida, opposing UEFA's application to obtain documents and testimony for a planned criminal complaint in Switzerland. UEFA alleges the FFE proposal was developed with a small circle of advisers outside normal governance, that investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a stake in a business valued near $20 billion with no open auction or independent valuation, and that a $30 million commissioner role was earmarked for Infantino. FIFA calls the application bad faith and harassment, accuses UEFA of a misinformation campaign timed to influence the election, and argues it would have been a dereliction of duty not to evaluate such a project at all. Club football has taken a side. On 25 September the Premier League , LaLiga , Lega Serie A and the Bundesliga issued a rare joint statement calling for structural reform, arguing that the FIFA presidency should not combine unchecked regulatory, commercial and political power, and describing what had happened as one of the biggest abuses of power in FIFA's history. UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation had already written that leadership of the game should never be treated as personal property. Nominations close on 18 November and the vote is in Rabat on 18 March 2027. UEFA meets its 55 member federations in Berlin next week, still without a candidate. That is the thing to watch: not the filings, but whether a challenger emerges before the deadline. Transfer News The European windows are shut. That has never stopped the business, and with three weekends of empty fixtures the agents have had the floor to themselves. One story dominates, and it belongs to a boy who cannot legally sign a professional contract for another week. The boy who turns sixteen on 6 October Manchester United have a generational forward in their academy who has asked to leave, an Irish passport that lets him, and a birthday next Tuesday that makes it possible. Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel , known to everyone in English football as JJ, was born in Enfield on 6 October 2010. He passed through the academies at Chelsea , Arsenal and West Ham before joining Manchester United in 2022. In April 2025, aged fourteen, he became the youngest player ever to appear for United's under-18s and scored twice on debut against Leeds United . In May 2026 he was named the under-18 Premier League player of the season. He has nine England youth caps across the under-15, under-16 and under-17 age groups. He wears the number 95 at Carrington. He has never played a senior minute, and he is already the most consequential transfer story in Europe. The reason is a passport. Gabriel holds Irish citizenship, which makes him eligible under FIFA's rules to move to a club inside the European Union from the age of sixteen rather than waiting until eighteen, as an English-only player moving abroad would have to. He turns sixteen next Tuesday. In mid-September he formally asked United to terminate his registration with immediate effect, stopped training, missed a Premier League 2 fixture against Brentford , and travelled to Barcelona. United refused to release him. Barcelona are the club most heavily linked, having first hosted him on a tour of the facilities in August 2024, when he met Lamine Yamal . Real Madrid are described by ESPN as monitoring the situation closely, with Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain also watching. One outlet, 101greatgoals, has gone further and reported that Gabriel will join Real Madrid on a free transfer on his sixteenth birthday; that claim is single-sourced and should be treated as such. Fabrizio Romano has pushed back on part of the narrative, stating that Gabriel did not hold direct talks with Barcelona in person and that it is his representatives who are speaking to several clubs. Romano's reading of United's position is that they are not giving up and still hope to keep him. United's head coach, Michael Carrick , has tried to lower the temperature, saying only that JJ is a young boy, that it is important nothing is played out in public, and that making sure he is all right is what matters. The hard-edged reality is simpler. If United retain his registration he cannot join an English club this season, which leaves a move to continental Europe as the only live route, and leaves United to argue about training compensation rather than a fee. For a player of this billing, that is the difference between a windfall and a rounding error. Certainty check: JJ Gabriel Where it sits Advanced interest and representative-level talks. In the space where the football should have been, their manager agreed to stay until 2030, their great rivals were found guilty, and the injury list kept growing. T he extended international break meant Arsenal 's men went from the 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion on 19 September to a blank calendar. Their next game is Leeds United at the Emirates on 10 October. That left the week to the people in suits, and they were busy. The big one had broken on the Tuesday before this week began. Sami Mokbel reported for the BBC that Mikel Arteta had agreed an improved contract, ending months of talks . His existing deal runs out at the end of this season. In May, co-chair Josh Kroenke had called securing the manager's future the club's priority. On Thursday the shape of the deal arrived. Fabrizio Romano reported that the agreement is valid for the next four years , which would presumably take Arteta to June 2030, and said the verbal agreement is done . Mokbel described a sharp pay increase on a current salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. No new figure has been published. It is not only the manager. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that Arteta 's backroom staff are in the process of renewing their deals, and Romano said they will sign for the same four years. Ornstein did not name names. Arseblog News thought it reasonable to assume the group includes Albert Stuivenberg , set-piece coach Nicolas Jover , goalkeeping coach Inaki Cana and tactical assistant Miguel Molina , with Gabriel Heinze also in line for improved terms. There is one thing missing: an announcement. As of Tuesday night the club had confirmed nothing. Arseblog News reported the announcement was unlikely to come quickly because the club had yet to film the content that goes with it. For a manager who ended the long wait for a league title last season, after three straight second-place finishes, the paperwork feels like a formality. It is still paperwork. The verbal agreement is done. Fabrizio Romano , on Arteta ’s new deal The timing matters. Arsenal won their first four league games of the title defence and then were taken apart at Brighton . A contract signed in that light is a statement that the club sees one bad afternoon for what it was. It also gives Arteta security going into a stretch that, after the break, runs straight into Leeds United , Lille in the Champions League and a run of games every three or four days. The other contract news of the week was about Declan Rice . Romano reported on Thursday that a new deal is really, really close , with final details being sorted and paperwork going to lawyers before an announcement. His current contract runs to 2028, so the extension would land before it enters its final year. That good news came with a worry attached. Rice had withdrawn from the England squad on 21 September, with football.london reporting his workload was being managed. Then Thomas Tuchel confirmed on Saturday that he was carrying a problem. The England manager said he saw straight away on TV that something was off while watching Rice at Brighton , and that the player just confirmed that impression . After fifty-five games for Arsenal last season and seven of England's eight World Cup matches, the rest looks sensible rather than alarming. Key Facts: the week at a glance Played Nothing. October in San Francisco is the real summer: the fog backs off, the evenings stay warm and the city spends every weekend outdoors. The first weekend sets the tone. Hardly Strictly Bluegrass fills Golden Gate Park from Friday October 2 to Sunday October 4, the Castro Street Fair closes four streets on the Sunday, and Fleet Week starts the same day and runs to October 12, with the Blue Angels overhead from October 9 to 11. Jack Johnson and Jon Batiste are at the Greek in Berkeley the same week. The sport has a genuine storyline for once. The Valkyries are in the playoffs as the second seed and, if they keep winning, Chase Center hosts semifinal games on October 4 and 7 and the opening games of the Finals on October 17 and 19. The Warriors are back for preseason on October 6 and open their home season on October 23. The Oakland Roots say goodbye to the Coliseum on October 10. Mid-month is festival weekend in every direction: the Autumn Lights in Oakland, the Art and Pumpkin Festival in Half Moon Bay, the 626 Night Market in Pleasanton, Open Studios at the Shipyard and two street fairs in SF on October 17 alone. Then the window closes on Halloween, which falls on a Saturday this year, with the Castro block party, Nightmare on Front Street the night before, and the Quakes, Dons and Valkyries all potentially at home that day. The weekend read Forecasters were calling for an early-autumn warm spell from Tuesday September 29, with San Francisco and Oakland in the 70s and inland valleys in the mid-80s to 90s. The National Weather Service expected above-average temperatures to persist into the middle of October. That raised the prospect of San Francisco's first run of ten straight 70-degree October days since 2015, with the warmest neighbourhoods, like the Mission, touching the low 80s. The coast stays cooler, in the 60s and low 70s, so Ocean Beach and the park's western meadows will still want a layer. Warm, dry weeks also mean elevated fire risk inland. Pick of the Month San Francisco Fleet Week Sunday October 4 to Monday October 12, 2026 · Northern Waterfront and Marina Green, San Francisco · Free. Air show October 9 to 11. Fleet Week is the rare San Francisco tradition that is free, enormous and genuinely for everyone. For nine days the Navy, Marines and Coast Guard are in town, and the waterfront between Fort Mason and Pier 39 becomes the best seat in the house for something you cannot see anywhere else in the country. The centrepiece is the air show from noon to 4pm on Friday October 9, Saturday October 10 and Sunday October 11, headlined by the Blue Angels flying between the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz. On the Friday morning the Parade of Ships comes in under the bridge from 11am, with the reviewing stand at Marina Green. From October 7 to 12 the ships themselves open for free tours at Piers 27 and 35, first come, first served. Practical advice: pick your viewing spot by noon, because the Marina Green, Crissy Field and the Aquatic Park bleachers fill early. Do not drive to the waterfront; Muni and a long walk will beat any parking search. Bring a layer even in a warm October, because the wind off the bay picks up just as the jets arrive. k: UEFA and FIFA are at war over who owns the World Cup, and this week the fight moved openly into the 2027 election campaign.
x: World Football, Weekly The Weekly Soccer Digest Reporting, analysis and the transfer paper trail Wednesday, September 23, 2026 · No. 1 · Arsenal covered separately In This Edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Football's Cold War Reaches the Ballot Box Two months after Gianni Infantino tried to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial future to private capital, the withdrawal has not settled anything. A conciliatory letter landed on Monday. By Tuesday the German federation had called it a campaign stunt, and on Wednesday UEFA's president was talking about broken trust. The 2027 election has effectively begun. Governance · Analysis T he letter went out on Monday to all 211 of FIFA's member associations, and it was written in the register of a man who knows he has a problem. Gianni Infantino told the federations he was willing to put his own house under outside inspection. "First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of FIFA's current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements," he wrote, in a passage reported by Reuters . Of the scheme that triggered the crisis, he was blunt: "It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed." The scheme was FIFA Forward Enterprise. Announced on 28 July, it would have moved World Cup and Club World Cup broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing rights into a commercial subsidiary valued at roughly $20bn, with Joshua Kushner 's Thrive Capital taking about 20 per cent for $4.2bn. The sweetener was aimed at the small federations who hold the votes: annual development funding would have climbed from $8m to $20m for the 2027 to 2030 cycle. For the confederations that generate the revenue, it was the sale of an asset FIFA holds in trust rather than owns. The revolt was faster than anyone at FIFA appears to have modelled. On 30 July all 55 UEFA associations voted unanimously to boycott future World Cups and FIFA competitions. CONCACAF and its 41 members rejected the plan. The Asian Confederation's Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa called it "totally unacceptable." Infantino withdrew it on 31 July, three days after announcing it. That is not a retreat. That is a rout. Gianni Infantino is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process. He has squandered all credibility. Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association, 22 September Withdrawal did not buy peace. On 27 August UEFA launched legal action against Infantino personally, alleging he had "fraudulently" offered the stake without proper FIFA authorisation at an "absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn," and describing the vehicle as a way for "Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets." The boycott was suspended only once FIFA confirmed in writing that the plan was "irrevocably and permanently withdrawn" and would "not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form." UEFA added that the underlying crisis had not been resolved. Reporting differs on where the action was filed, so we are not naming a venue. ( Yahoo Sports ) Which brings us to this week, and to the reason Monday's letter did not land the way it was meant to. Within twenty-four hours Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association , went on the record with Reuters : "I regard Gianni Infantino's letter as a transparent ploy to secure his re-election next year." He added that Infantino "is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process" and "has squandered all credibility." Germany is not a peripheral federation lodging a protest. It is a four-time world champion, the host of the last European Championship, and one of the four or five associations whose position other federations read before settling their own. On Wednesday it escalated again. The Associated Press reported UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin speaking directly to the damage, framing the task ahead as repairing trust broken by Infantino's World Cup plan ( AP, 23 September ). The choice of word is deliberate. A governing body that has to litigate against its own president to establish what he is authorised to sell has a problem no external review can write away. The arithmetic, though, still favours the incumbent, and that is the uncomfortable part for the reformers. Reuters reports that Infantino stands for re-election in March 2027 and that sources believe he retains the votes to win, with opponents concentrating on limiting his powers rather than fielding a rival. FIFA's electorate is one association, one vote, which means Germany and Gibraltar count the same. The federations that were offered a tripling of their development grant in July are the same federations who will fill in the ballot in March, and Infantino's letter took care to promise that a federation's position on governance "would not affect their treatment by FIFA." It is a sentence that only needs writing if people were worried about the opposite. So the shape of the next six months is clear. Europe and CONCACAF have the money, the clubs and the lawyers. Infantino has the ballot box. Every reform proposal from here will be read by both camps as a vote count, and the confederations will keep the litigation running because discovery is the only mechanism capable of establishing what was actually promised in July and to whom. None of it is incidental to the football. The question underneath is who decides what the World Cup is for, and it will be settled by a show of hands in a conference hall. How We Got Here 28 July 2026 FIFA announces FIFA Forward Enterprise: World Cup and Club World Cup commercial rights into a subsidiary valued near $20bn, with Thrive Capital taking about 20 per cent for $4.2bn. 29 to 30 July UEFA says the plan crosses a line governing institutions should never cross. All 55 UEFA associations vote unanimously to boycott future World Cups. CONCACAF's 41 members and the AFC reject it. 31 July Infantino withdraws the proposal, three days after unveiling it. 27 August UEFA begins legal action against Infantino personally. The boycott is suspended after FIFA confirms in writing the plan is permanently dead. UEFA says the underlying crisis is not resolved. 21 September Infantino writes to all 211 member associations offering an independent external governance review. 22 September Germany's Bernd Neuendorf calls the letter a transparent ploy to secure re-election. 23 September AP reports UEFA's Aleksander Ceferin on the need to repair trust broken by the World Cup plan. Figures as reported by Reuters and Yahoo Sports. A reported figure of roughly $64m a year for a prospective FFE commissioner role originates with The Athletic and is not confirmed by FIFA. The Election Clock The date. Infantino stands for re-election at the FIFA Congress in March 2027. One association, one vote, 211 votes in the room. Support withdrawn. Italy's FIGC (August) plus Finland, Wales, Serbia, Sweden, Greece, Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands' KNVB (30 August) have publicly withdrawn backing for his re-election. Loudest voices.
