Spain Has Its Own Civil War, and It Is Not About Football Real Madrid lost a derby, the referees' committee conceded one of the three big calls, and within forty-eight hours the club had formally demanded the resignation of the league's president. Meanwhile Barcelona quietly went seven from seven. The match itself was tight and bad-tempered. Atletico Madrid beat Real Madrid 2-1 at the Metropolitano on Sunday. Dean Huijsen was dismissed after a VAR review, Alejandro Grimaldo converted the resulting penalty on fifty minutes, Jonathan David made it two on 59 and Antonio Rudiger headed a consolation on 89. Real Madrid's own match report, published on the club's website, carried the headline "Un pesimo arbitraje decide el derbi" : a dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby. Clubs do not usually put that on their own front page. On Monday and Tuesday the Spanish referees' technical committee published its review, and the outcome was genuinely split. The committee ruled that Lee Kang-in 's 44th-minute challenge on Fede Valverde was a clear and obvious error: it should have been a red card and VAR should have intervened. It also ruled that the earlier incident involving Cristian Romero and Jude Bellingham was correctly handled, and that Huijsen's red card and the penalty were correct ( via El Nacional ). Two right, one wrong. Madrid had a legitimate grievance and, in the committee's judgement, not the one they were shouting loudest about. Jose Mourinho , in his first Madrid derby since returning to the Bernabeu bench in June, did not wait for the review. "Son dos tarjetas rojas claras," he said, two clear red cards, before turning on the video official: "this gentleman has a very complete history as a VAR referee in Real Madrid matches" ( La Opinion ). It is the oldest script Mourinho owns, and at the Bernabeu it plays. Then the institutions took over. On Tuesday Real Madrid issued a formal statement calling it "intolerable that the LaLiga president uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid," and said the competition required "a leader capable of administering it with the essential duty of neutrality" ( EFE ). The trigger was Javier Tebas 's social-media reply to the refereeing row, in which he said that arguing referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy. Tebas answered the statement the same day and aimed straight at Florentino Perez : "The president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition. Neither is the president of Real Madrid." And: "I am not the owner of LaLiga and I will not run it as though it belonged to a single club. Respect for everyone. Subordination to no one." ( beIN Sports ) Two things are worth holding onto. Tebas is also among the loudest voices calling for Gianni Infantino to resign, which made this a week in which Spanish football's most combative administrator fought on two fronts at once. And then there is the table. While all this went on, Barcelona won 3-1 at Sevilla to move to seven wins from seven. Real Madrid are fourth, six points back, and go into the break without Fede Valverde , whose club medical report described a severe trauma to the left ankle ( Real Madrid ). Spanish outlets say two to three weeks. The club has given no date. Transfer News A Four-Time European Champion, a Rome Clinic and a Club 15th in Serie A The summer window shut three weeks ago, which is exactly why the free-agent market is suddenly the most interesting room in football. David Alaba has picked the least predictable door in it. The best transfer story of the week did not involve a fee. David Alaba has been without a club since his Real Madrid contract expired on 30 June, and on Wednesday Fabrizio Romano reported that Udinese had reached a verbal agreement with him. Tuttomercatoweb photographed the Austrian arriving at the Villa Stuart clinic in Rome for medical tests the same morning, with a journey north to Udine to follow. Foot Mercato reports he turned down Inter Miami , Union Berlin and Austria Vienna to take it. Contract length has not been disclosed. Status: medical completed, announcement pending. On paper it is absurd. Alaba won four Champions Leagues across Bayern Munich and Real Madrid and took eleven trophies from 131 Madrid appearances. Udinese have conceded eleven goals in five matches. But that second number is the explanation: Kosta Runjaic has an injury-thinned back line and a defender with 400 elite matches behind him is available for nothing. The risk is his fitness record. The upside is the most decorated centre-back in the division, at no cost. He is not the only serious name changing address outside a window. Juventus lost goalkeeper Kamil Grabara to a ruptured cruciate ligament in training on 22 September and moved within a day: Gianluca Di Marzio and Tuttosport both reported a deal agreed for free agent Neto , 37, on a contract to 30 June 2027, nine years after he left the club. He will back up Guglielmo Vicario . Alfredo Pedulla had flagged Neto as the first name on the list from Saturday. Status: agreed, signature imminent. Luciano Spalletti dedicated Saturday's win over Atalanta to his injured players, Grabara in particular, and the goalkeeper posted on Wednesday that he never wanted to have to publish such a message. A third name joined the available list. Wolfsburg , relegated last season, announced on 22 September that they had mutually terminated Christian Eriksen 's contract, which ran to June 2027. Sporting head Dieter Hecking said the decision belonged to the player: "we wanted to give him this freedom in this particular situation" (via Tuttomercatoweb). Eriksen is now the most accomplished unattached midfielder in Europe. No next club has been reported. Certainty Tiers, and Where This Week's Deals Sit OFFICIAL. Tyrell Malacia to FC Cincinnati (free, 18 Sept). Matt Miazga to NYCFC via waivers (22 Sept). Franjo Ivanovic to Lens on loan from Benfica, no purchase option. Richard Hughes leaves Liverpool for Al-Hilal. MEDICAL. David Alaba to Udinese, free. Romano reported the verbal agreement; TMW placed him at Villa Stuart. AGREED. Neto to Juventus, free, one year. Chiesa and Endo leaving Liverpool in January. Reporters are named in the prose. Where an item rests on a single outlet we say so. The First of January Is Closer Than It Looks Anyone whose contract expires in June 2027 can open talks with a foreign club on New Year's Day. That clock is now ticking on Harry Kane, Christian Pulisic and a surprising number of others. The single biggest expiry in world football belongs to Harry Kane , who is in the final year of the deal he signed with Bayern Munich in 2023 and who on 18 September became the fastest player ever to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in his 98th appearance. Bayern are not hiding. Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has said the club are "having productive discussions" and expects matters to wrap up after the international break; president Herbert Hainer has gone further: "We want to extend his contract further, and I also think that's what will happen" ( bundesliga.com ). Kane himself, on the night of the record: "All I can say is that I enjoy every minute of it. I'm extremely happy here. The talks are ongoing" ( beIN Sports ). Bild has reported a target of 2029, a broadly flat salary near €25m a year and an exit clause under discussion. Status: advanced, not signed. The renewal nobody is covering properly is Christian Pulisic 's. Marco Conterio of Tuttomercatoweb reported on Wednesday that the American's AC Milan deal runs to 2027 with a club option, that he currently earns around €4.5m net, that his camp opened at €8m and would settle at €7m, and that this sits above Milan's wage ceiling. The detail that matters is procedural rather than financial: talks were serious in the autumn and then stalled, and Pulisic's side expected a formal written proposal of the kind other players received and never got one. A club that values a player's commercial weight in North America while declining to put a number on paper is a club that may find itself negotiating with Barcelona's lawyers in January instead. Elsewhere on the expiry board: Jude Bellingham 's Real Madrid deal runs to 2029 and Matteo Moretto has reported an extension to 2030 or 2031 is close, though we could only reach that reporting second-hand and are labelling it accordingly. Kevin De Bruyne 's Napoli situation produced the week's cleanest contradiction: Nicolo Schira reported on Wednesday that renewal talks on his 2027-expiring contract are stalled and the parties look close to parting at season's end, while the player told reporters from the Belgium camp a day earlier that he "never considered the idea of leaving Napoli" and is very happy there ( Fantacalcio ). Both can be true. Only one will be true in June. And then there is the renewal that is not happening. Alexis Mac Allister is contracted to Liverpool until 2028 but said earlier this month that he felt a little sad watching Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai sign long-term deals while his agent was told the club was "not in a position to renew." On 22 September, on Argentina duty, he softened it: "it was more about my emotions than judging the club," and if it is two more years, "that's absolutely fine" ( Sports Illustrated ). Read the club's behaviour rather than the player's manners. Liverpool are comfortable letting a 2028 contract run down, and that is usually the first visible step toward a summer sale. In Barcelona the news was better. Sporting director Deco told the club's general assembly on 19 September that renewals for Raphinha (to 2030), Marc Bernal (to 2031) and Xavi Espart (to 2030) had been all but completed, with formalisation expected within a week (Football Espana). None had been signed as of Wednesday, which is a distinction worth preserving. Given what Raphinha has done in the first seven matchdays, it is also the cheapest business the club will do this season. Barcelona Close the Alvarez File, and Laporta Lights It on Fire The summer's most expensive non-transfer got its epilogue this week, and it doubled as a warning about what Barcelona can and cannot do in January. Barcelona bid €100m for Julian Alvarez in late May and Atletico Madrid refused to sell to them specifically. On 21 September Joan Laporta finally said out loud what the club had been briefing privately: "They acted offended; they had no way to justify their attitude. We were constantly hearing that they would sell him to every club except Barca. Then they dropped the pretense and said it openly." He added that he had suspicions about why, but no proof, so he would keep them to himself ( Sports Illustrated ). It is not the language of a president who intends to try again in eight weeks. The finances say the same thing more plainly. Barcelona's vice-president for economics, Ferran Olive , told Cadena SER this week that the club will have positive financial fair play headroom in January but would still need to sell before buying, and that the move to Montjuic during the Camp Nou roof works is expected to push them back outside the one-to-one rule in the summer of 2027 ( El Desmarque ). Earlier modelling by Cronica Global put Barcelona's registration room at roughly €43m against an Alvarez package costing €50m to €55m a year. The gap is real, the political route is closed, and in the meantime Raphinha has scored twelve league goals in seven games playing centrally. Status: dormant, and we would treat any January revival as a rumour until Atletico say otherwise. The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with a certainty label on each. This is where the not-yet-official stories live, and where the reader should keep a hand on their wallet. Endrick to AC Milan. The best-triangulated January link on the board. Daniele Longo of Calciomercato reported on 22 September that Ruben Amorim wants a left-footed number ten and that Endrick is the first name on the list, with feasibility resting entirely on whether Florentino Perez will do business. Separately, Joaquin Maroto has reported the player is increasingly frustrated with his role at Real Madrid . Two outlets, two countries, same direction. Complicating it: Romano quoted Madrid in mid-September saying they remain "absolutely confident in Endrick." Concrete interest. Rayan Ait-Nouri to Juventus. Gazzetta dello Sport, relayed by Tuttomercatoweb on 23 September, reports that Juventus re-established contact with the left-back's entourage during this international break after first talks in late August, and are weighing a loan with an option to buy so the permanent negotiation can wait until summer. The premise is that he is behind the queue at Manchester City under Enzo Maresca . Concrete interest, contact made. Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo out at Liverpool. Both were left out of Liverpool 's Champions League squad. Endo has played no minutes at all this season; Chiesa has five goals in 50 appearances since arriving from Juventus in 2024 and is now behind Bradley Barcola , Rio Ngumoha , Cody Gakpo and reportedly the 21-year-old Lewis Koumas . Italian outlets have him linked with a Serie A return ( via SportBible ). Strongly signposted exit, no destination agreed. Bernardo Silva is being forgotten at the Bernabeu. This one is ours to flag rather than anyone's to confirm. Silva joined Real Madrid on a free from Manchester City this summer on a two-year deal. Under Jose Mourinho he has 282 minutes in six league games with no goals and one assist, including eight minutes across the last two fixtures (Fichajes, a low-tier outlet, though the minutes are checkable). Barcelona pursued him in the summer before talks collapsed over money and playing time. A 32-year-old who is ninth choice by late September, with a domestic rival who wanted him six weeks ago, is a January story forming in plain sight. Speculative. No contact reported. Alejandro Garnacho's loan is failing, and the clause may be why. Three appearances for Aston Villa and benched for the last two. Unai Emery earlier this month: "We continue working with him, but for now there are others performing better." The loan from Chelsea reportedly carries an appearance-triggered obligation to buy, which is precisely the mechanism that gives a club a reason not to play someone. The Daily Mail reports Spanish clubs want him in January (via the Daily Mail). Concrete interest, no talks reported. And briefly. Manu Kone to Chelsea : Corriere dello Sport says Roma now want around €100m, roughly double the summer figure. Rumour. · JJ Gabriel , the 15-year-old at Manchester United who turns 16 on 6 October: Romano called Real Madrid favourites with Barcelona in contact, and Christian Falk added Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain on 23 September (CaughtOffside). Rumour, but serious reporters on it. · Thiago Pitarch , 19, has played no minutes for Real Madrid and was sent to Castilla for the break after the club blocked a summer move to Fulham . Interest expected to revive. The Fee That Keeps Talking: €145m Liverpool paid a reported €145m to Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola , the biggest fee of the summer. Five matches in, he has 248 minutes, no goals and no assists. Andoni Iraola on the fit: "He has very good passing quality. In counter-attack situations, we didn't find him twice, so we need to learn these movements" ( Foot Mercato ). Set beside Florian Wirtz at a reported €125m, who also started slowly and is now the subject of exit stories, Liverpool have roughly €270m tied up in two attackers who are not yet firing. The league table is less forgiving than the performances: Liverpool are sixth on nine points, six behind Manchester City, having drawn three of their first five. Around the Leagues Premier League Manchester City are five from five and Enzo Maresca 's first autumn in charge is already producing the sort of numbers that make a season feel decided in September. Sunday's 5-3 win over Sunderland was the most entertaining match of the round and statistically one of the strangest of the Premier League era. City took the lead three separate times before half-time, which Opta records as only the seventh instance in league history. Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick and lost, the sixth time that has happened in the Premier League and the first since Roque Santa Cruz managed it for Blackburn in December 2007. Erling Haaland scored the fifth and in doing so completed the set: he has now scored against all 25 Premier League clubs he has faced. Regis Le Bris took charge of his 100th Sunderland match, the first manager to reach that mark at the club since Roy Keane . The result that will echo longest, though, was on Friday night. Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0, and the underlying numbers are alarming for Xabi Alonso . Chelsea have now conceded 23 set-piece goals since the start of last season, joint-worst in the division, and have gone 22 consecutive league matches without a clean sheet at a rate of 2.2 non-penalty goals conceded per game. This was their eleventh defeat of the calendar year, more than in the whole of 2025 ( Sky Sports ). Alonso was direct: "We concede the first goal, you're still in the game but then we lose the shape. We were out of control." Levi Colwill went further: "At times we have been bullied." Brentford are unbeaten through five for the first time in their history. All of this arrived four days after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter agreed to sell their combined 25 per cent stake to majority owner Clearlake Capital, taking Clearlake to 86.5 per cent in a deal valuing the club at £5bn ( Sky Sports ). At the other end, two very large clubs are in genuine trouble. Manchester United have five points from five, equalling their joint-worst Premier League start, and Michael Carrick spent the week absorbing it: "I'm totally happy taking responsibility, absolutely no problem with that, it doesn't bother me" ( Irish News ). The 1-1 at Fulham prompted Gary Neville to call a passage of United's play the worst fifteen minutes he had ever seen from them in possession, and Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa to complain that officials do not like Manchester United to lose. Tottenham are bottom of the table on two points with no wins, and the reporting on Roberto De Zerbi is contested. Fabrizio Romano was the clearest: "the message from Tottenham, as of today, remains a message of confidence in Roberto De Zerbi," and "I don't have any indication of Tottenham exploring different ways" ( via Football365 ). Other outlets have run harder lines. Weigh accordingly. Around them: Coventry City won at Nottingham Forest through Jay Dasilva for their first top-flight victory since 2001, having failed to score in their opening four matches. Oliver Glasner said he had felt the heaviness of Forest's past for the first time; they have not won a home league game since December (Sky Sports). Everton are unbeaten in seven, matching David Moyes 's own 2006-07 side, and spent Wednesday morning mocking The Athletic on social media for leaving every Everton player out of its in-season top fifty. Off the pitch, Profit and Sustainability Rules are gone: this is the first season of the Squad Cost Ratio, capping wages, transfers and agent fees at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net player-sale profit, with a six-point deduction for breaching the red threshold ( Premier League ). And Daniel Levy received a £27m exit payment from Tottenham, taking his total earnings there to £88m, reported by The Athletic as the second-largest payout to a departing Premier League executive ( via Yahoo Sports ). La Liga Barcelona have won all seven. The engine is Raphinha , who has twelve league goals in those seven games, three of them penalties, a total bettered at this stage of a season this century only by Cristiano Ronaldo 's thirteen in 2014-15. He scored hat-tricks in consecutive matches: seven days after putting three past Racing Santander in a 7-2 win he produced a perfect one at Sevilla , header, curled finish and chip, in a 3-1 away victory in which Barcelona's expected goals read 3.26 to 0.45 ( beIN Sports ). Around him, Lamine Yamal is now a club captain at 19, the youngest in Barcelona's history to wear the armband on a Champions League debut, and leads the team for chances created. Hansi Flick 's one worry going into the break is Andreas Christensen , who went off at the Pizjuan with a thigh problem. Behind them the table is unusual. Atletico Madrid are second after the derby, level on sixteen with Manuel Pellegrini 's Real Betis . Real Madrid are fourth. Alaves are sixth on eleven, their best start in La Liga history, and promoted Deportivo La Coruna are seventh with Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , 37, on five goals. At the bottom, Valencia confirmed Javier Aguirre as head coach on Wednesday, his seventh La Liga club, ten days after sacking Carlos Corberan and football chief executive Ron Gourlay (Fichajes.net). He starts at Racing Santander on 11 October. One fixture went unplayed: Levante against Athletic Club was postponed under an official weather alert after flooding in Valencia and is rescheduled for 21 October (El Desmarque). Bundesliga Two things happened in Germany this week and both were emphatic. Borussia Dortmund won 1-0 at VfB Stuttgart through a 70th-minute Maxi Beier finish, assisted by Jobe Bellingham , and went into the break top of the table with four wins from four, their best start in eleven years. It was, remarkably, Dortmund's first shot on target of the match from ten attempts ( BVB ). Niko Kovac is doing it without Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias , both with cruciate ligament injuries. Meanwhile Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0. Michael Olise scored a hat-trick and took 88 per cent of the man-of-the-match vote; Harry Kane scored twice and became the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in his 98th appearance and demolishing Dieter Muller 's 129-game benchmark (bundesliga.com). The league is scoring at a rate not seen in forty years: 137 goals in the first 36 matches, 3.8 a game, the third-highest total after four matchdays in Bundesliga history (bundesliga.com). Freiburg are third and set a club record with six straight competitive wins before drawing at Eintracht Frankfurt . Promoted SC Paderborn beat Hoffenheim 3-1 for their first Bundesliga win since 2020. At the bottom, Borussia Monchengladbach have no points from four: Eugen Polanski was dismissed on 13 September and Alexander Blessin confirmed on 22 September on a deal to 2028, arriving from St Pauli ( bundesliga.com ). Union Berlin have one point and seventeen conceded, and Mauro Lustrinelli is next in the queue. Off the pitch, Jurgen Klopp , now Germany head coach, named a first squad of 44 players for the four Nations League fixtures ( DFB ), and the cartel office's August ruling that 50+1 is lawful only if applied consistently has left the exemptions held by Wolfsburg, Leverkusen, Hannover and Leipzig looking exposed. Serie A Three clubs are level at the top on thirteen points and the separation is goal difference: Roma first, Inter second, Lazio third. Gian Piero Gasperini 's Roma have conceded three goals in five matches, the best defence in the division, and drew 2-2 with Inter at the Olimpico in the round's best match: Manu Kone scored twice in the first half, Lautaro Martinez twice in the second ( Corriere dello Sport ). Fourth, and this is not a misprint, are Cagliari on twelve points with two goals conceded in five under Fabio Pisacane . Promoted Frosinone are sixth. Juventus beat Atalanta 2-0 through Francisco Conceicao and Bremer , which leaves Maurizio Sarri with three straight defeats and one goal scored in them, his first such run at Atalanta. AC Milan are fifth and unbeaten domestically after a 3-0 win over Lecce . Napoli are ninth on seven points, their worst start in a decade, and Corriere dello Sport reported a heated dressing-room confrontation at the Franchi in which Massimiliano Allegri made clear he had wanted two more signings, a centre-back and a striker of substance (Corriere dello Sport; press reconstruction, not on the record). Bologna sacked Domenico Tedesco on 16 September after one point from four and installed Raffaele Palladino on a three-year deal the same afternoon (Il Fatto Quotidiano). Away from the table, Italian football buried a monument: Sandro Mazzola died on 19 September aged 83 (Sky Sport Italia), and the disciplinary judge fined Juventus €10,000 after a small section of the Curva Sud turned their backs during his minute's silence. Lazio published accounts showing a €10m loss against a €104.6m wage bill, with no European football and a supporter boycott costing roughly 25,000 season tickets (Corriere dello Sport). The Meazza, meanwhile, turned 100. Ligue 1 France has produced the most disorderly table in Europe. Monaco lead on thirteen points, Lyon are second on eleven with the division's best goal difference after thrashing Rennes 4-0, and Paris FC are third, also on eleven. The reigning champions, Paris Saint-Germain , are sixth on eight. Marseille are seventeenth on three. Sunday's Classique at the Velodrome went to PSG 2-1 in front of 61,499: Ferran Torres , the €50m summer signing from Barcelona, scored seven minutes after coming on for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , Amine Gomes equalised for Marseille on 72 and Marquinhos won it two minutes later ( Foot Mercato ). Luis Enrique was measured afterwards: his side controlled the first period without creating, started the second brilliantly and missed clear chances. Marseille are the story. Five straight defeats in all competitions, including a 4-1 beating at Besiktas in the Europa League, no signings in the summer window, and a balance sheet that recorded €105m of losses for 2025 against a €120m injection from Frank McCourt . President Pablo Longoria has left for River Plate , prompting RMC's Jerome Rothen to say on air that he hoped Longoria had filled his pockets, because look at the state of the club. Bruno Genesio says the situation is not normal but has no intention of resigning (Foot Mercato). Elsewhere: France's Cour de cassation rejected Achraf Hakimi 's appeal on Wednesday, confirming his referral to the Hauts-de-Seine criminal court on a rape charge relating to 2023, a procedural ruling and not a finding of guilt ( Foot Mercato ). And Zinedine Zidane began work as France head coach, switching to a 4-3-3 with Kylian Mbappe left and Ousmane Dembele central: "I want a team that plays, that decides to take command of the game" (Foot Mercato). Major League Soccer A correction worth making, because it changes how you read everything else: MLS Decision Day this year is 7 November, not early October. The 2026 season was rebuilt around the World Cup, so most clubs still have around eight of 34 matches to play, the Wild Card round begins 18 November and MLS Cup is 18 December. Nashville SC lead the Supporters' Shield race on 57 points from 26 games, eight clear of Vancouver who have a game in hand, and have already clinched a playoff berth. Below that it is brutally tight: both conference playoff lines are separated by a single point. In the East FC Cincinnati hold ninth on 33 from NYCFC on 32; in the West Portland hold ninth on 32 from San Diego FC on 31 ( MLSsoccer.com ). Lionel Messi has 20 goals and 13 assists in 23 games and is the second player in league history to score 20 or more in three consecutive seasons. His free kick in Inter Miami 's 2-2 draw with San Diego FC was his 101st goal for the club since July 2023, and he leads MLS in both goals and assists ( MLSsoccer.com ). Miami have drawn four in a row, though, and sit third in the East on the wins tiebreaker. Denis Bouanga passed Carlos Vela as LAFC 's all-time regular-season top scorer, 79 goals in 127 appearances against Vela's 78 in 152, assisted by Son Heung-min ( MLSsoccer.com ). And Philadelphia trailed Sporting Kansas City 3-0 and won 4-3, scoring in the 64th, 66th, 68th and 73rd minutes. Robert Lewandowski , 38, has six goals and two assists in his first ten MLS appearances since joining Chicago Fire in late June, but Chicago are winless in seven and their expected goals have fallen from 2.15 a game before the World Cup break to 1.56 after it. Real Salt Lake lost Diego Luna for the season to meniscus surgery (MLSsoccer.com). And the structural story rumbles on: from 2027 MLS switches to a summer-to-spring calendar with a winter break and MLS Cup in May. This season is the last of the old format. Europe The Champions League did not play this week. Matchday 1 was 8 to 10 September and Matchday 2 is 13 and 14 October, so the European football in this window was Europa League Matchday 1 on 16 and 17 September, and it belonged to England. Crystal Palace beat Lech Poznan 4-0 with four different scorers, Bournemouth won 2-1 at Real Sociedad , and Sunderland beat AZ Alkmaar 1-0 through an Enzo Le Fee penalty in their first European match in 53 years (Sky Sports). His Champions Get a Warning. The BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Arsenal and their manager have agreed terms on a new long-term contract. It lands three days after Brighton & Hove Albion pulled the champions apart on the south coast, and the sequence tells you a great deal about how this club now sees itself. T here is a particular kind of week that only happens to a club that has finally won something. Sami Mokbel of the BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Mikel Arteta has agreed a new long-term contract at Arsenal , with a significant rise on the roughly 10 million pounds a year he currently earns. No end date has been made public and no announcement has been issued. The old deal ran only to 2027, and for most of this year the absence of a new one has been the quiet hum underneath everything else at London Colney. That hum has now stopped. What has not stopped is the noise from Saturday evening, when Brighton & Hove Albion beat Arsenal 3-0 at the Amex and made it look less like an upset than an inevitability. Pascal Gross struck from distance on the half hour. Charalampos Kostoulas added a second on the stroke of half time, fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had tamely missed a chance to equalise. Chema Andres headed in a corner nine minutes into the second half. It was the first defeat of the season, the end of a seven-match winning run, and the first time since the title was won in May that anyone had been able to say out loud that this Arsenal side looked ordinary. The timing is coincidence rather than cause and effect. But put the two stories side by side and you get the truest picture of Arsenal in September 2026 that anyone is going to draw: a club that has decided the manager is the answer, and is now discovering that the squad still has a question in it. Start with the defeat, because it was more instructive than the scoreline. Brighton & Hove Albion pressed Arsenal from the first throw-in, which is close to the phrase Arteta reached for afterwards, and the champions had no coherent way through it. David Raya was imprecise with the ball at his feet and the nervousness travelled up the pitch from him. Gabriel Magalhaes gave Gross the yard he needed. The defending at the corner for the third was, in the view of even sympathetic Arsenal writers, not really defending at all. And when Arsenal did reach a promising area, there was no pace to run beyond anyone and no Plan B to reach for. That last point is the structural one, and it did not appear on Saturday. It has been there since the window shut on September 1. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal . Gabriel Jesus went to Barcelona . Leandro Trossard went to Besiktas . In came Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge , a fine footballer who has already started to build something with Kai Havertz and Riccardo Calafiori , but who arrived as a replacement for three departures rather than as an addition on top of them. “A very disappointing result and performance. They were another gear from us in the basics of the game.” Mikel Arteta, after the defeat at Brighton David Ornstein of The Athletic has been blunt about what that means. Arsenal wanted a player to raise the level of their attack this summer and did not get one. Vinicius Junior was the headline pursuit. Julian Alvarez was a long-standing admiration. Malick Fofana was looked at as an investment. Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers were explored and ruled out. None of them moved at a price Arsenal were willing to pay, so the money stayed in the building. The owners, Ornstein says, showed a willingness to fund a marquee signing. The club simply could not land one. The consequence is visible in a number that should trouble nobody and yet nags at everybody: eight goals in five Premier League matches, from around 6.8 expected goals. Arsenal are not failing to create. They are creating and then wasting, and they are doing it while scoring nothing at all from set pieces, the single most reliable source of goals in last season's title win. A team that took 19 league goals from corners in 2025-26, a competition record, has taken none from any dead ball in eight matches this term. Arteta delivered the Premier League title, ending a 22-year wait and taking the club's tally to 14. He took them to a Champions League final in Budapest in May, where they drew 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain after extra time and lost 4-3 on penalties. He lost an EFL Cup final to Manchester City in March, then beat the same opponent 3-0 in the Community Shield in August. Tying him down now, with the squad unfinished, says the club believes the ceiling is above the roof they have already touched. And the contract work does not stop with him. TEAMtalk has reported that talks with Declan Rice , Martin Odegaard and Jurrien Timber are all advancing alongside the manager's. The architecture of the next five years is being built during an international break, which is exactly when clubs of this size do their least visible and most consequential work. There are three weeks until Arsenal play again, at Leeds United on October 10. That is an unusually long time to sit with a 3-0 defeat, and an unusually good time to fix what caused it. Arteta called Saturday a big lesson. He has just been handed the time, and the mandate, to prove he learned it. Four Away Days and a Reckoning: Inside the Brighton Defeat The 3-0 at the Amex was Arsenal's fourth consecutive away fixture in all competitions. By the end of it, the accumulated wear was visible in every department. Arsenal had been to Naples, to Sunderland, to Ipswich and then to Brighton without a home fixture in between, and they won the first three. The night at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on September 9 was close to a masterclass: 76 per cent possession and eventually a Martin Odegaard strike off the post. Four days later came a 2-0 win at Sunderland . Three days after that, 4-2 at Ipswich Town with nine changes. By Saturday the legs had gone and so had the shape. Fabian Hurzeler set Brighton & Hove Albion up to be, in his own description, horrible to play against, and they were. The press was relentless, the second balls were theirs, and Arsenal kept giving the ball back in the worst possible areas. The midfield is where the argument will settle. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes have not yet found each other. The 75 million pound signing from Newcastle United was sloppy in possession at the Amex, and the pair's lack of connection dragged Odegaard deeper and deeper to plug the gap, removing Arsenal 's best creator from the places where he does damage. That is the puzzle Arteta has to solve before Leeds United . Paul Scholes argued afterwards that Rice should have been sent off rather than booked. He was not, and he is available for the resumption. That will be the least of Arteta 's concerns. Sources: Arseblog match analysis , Three Interlull Things . TRANSFER NEWS The Superstar Arsenal Did Not Sign, and the January Question It Left Behind Ornstein: the owners were willing. The market was not. Now the same question rolls into the winter. The most important piece of Arsenal reporting this past week did not concern a player who is arriving. It concerned several who are not. David Ornstein of The Athletic has confirmed what the shape of the summer already implied: Arsenal needed and wanted a player to raise the level of their attack, and failed to sign one. The list of names is not short. Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid was the primary target. Julian Alvarez at Atletico Madrid has been admired for years. Malick Fofana was assessed as an investment rather than a finished article. Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers were both looked at before being ruled out. In every case the valuation or the availability, or both, made the deal impossible at the price Arsenal had set for themselves. Ornstein 's framing of what comes next is worth quoting carefully, because it is a question rather than a prediction. One of the intriguing things, he said, whether it be January or next summer, is who is going to be the Arsenal attacking recruit to help take them to even greater heights. He added two caveats that matter: Arsenal must remain careful about UEFA's financial regulations, and a marquee arrival may require Viktor Gyokeres to be sold first. Certainty tier: this is credible reporting on intent and market position, not a live negotiation. Nobody has bid. Nobody is in talks. Treat any January headline that attaches a fee to Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez with the suspicion it deserves until a second reliable name is attached to it. There is a counter-argument, made by Sky Sports this month: with Odegaard , Havertz and Saka fit at the same time, Arsenal may not need the blockbuster. Odegaard scored once in 36 matches last season and opened this one with three goals in four across all competitions. Havertz matched him, and the trio supplied every one of Arsenal 's first six league goals. The flaw in the argument is the one it has always had: it needs three players to stay healthy for nine months. Sources: Ornstein on the failed summer , Ornstein on January . Rice Close to Five More Years, With Odegaard and Timber Behind Him A reported 280,000 pounds a week, and an international break cleared specifically to get it done. Declan Rice withdrew from England 's Nations League squad on Saturday. The stated reason was workload, and it is a real one: 55 matches for Arsenal last season, seven of England 's eight World Cup games while managing nerve pain in his hamstring, a curtailed pre-season, and then all five league games plus the trip to Napoli . He is also, according to a FootballTransfers exclusive by Steve Kay published on Tuesday, on the verge of signing a new five-year contract worth a reported 280,000 pounds a week. His current deal runs to 2028 with a one-year option in Arsenal 's favour, so there is no cliff edge here. This is a club paying to keep its most important player happy rather than one negotiating under duress. Two cautions. First, the wage figure and the five-year length are single-sourced and have not been confirmed by a tier-one reporter or by the club. Second, nothing is signed. What can be said with more confidence, because TEAMtalk has reported it alongside the manager's own extension, is that Arsenal are working simultaneously on new deals for Rice , Martin Odegaard and Jurrien Timber . Certainty tier: advanced talks, single-sourced on terms. Watch for David Ornstein or Fabrizio Romano to put their name to it. That is the moment it becomes real. Sources: FootballTransfers exclusive , TEAMtalk on the contract slate . Madueke Stays: Arsenal Shut the Door on Juventus and Atletico Twenty-four league minutes, a Carabao Cup goal, an England omission, and a manager who is not selling. Noni Madueke has played 24 Premier League minutes this season, both from the bench, with no goals and no assists. He started the Community Shield, featured in the win at Napoli and volleyed one in at Ipswich Town . He was also left out of Thomas Tuchel 's England squad, with insufficient match fitness given as the reason. Juventus and Atletico Madrid have both been monitoring the situation, and Juventus are reported to have explored a mid-season loan. Per Football Insider, relayed by Goal on September 21, Arsenal will reject any January approach. Mikel Arteta wants his attacking group kept intact, particularly given the squad is already lighter than he wanted it to be. The complicating factor is not Bukayo Saka , who is untouchable on the right. It is Max Dowman , who is 16 and who keeps producing on the nights he is given. Madueke is reported to be willing to fight for his place. He will have to. Sources: Goal on Arsenal's decision . THE SQUAD The Set-Piece Machine Has Stalled, and It May Not Be an Accident Nineteen corner goals last season, a Premier League record. None from any dead ball in eight matches this one. A rule change is hovering over the explanation. The most striking statistic about Arsenal 's start is not the eight goals or the one defeat. It is the zero. Eight matches into 2026-27, across the Community Shield, the Premier League, the Champions League and the Carabao Cup, Arsenal have not scored from a corner or a free kick. To understand why that is remarkable you have to remember what last season was. Arsenal scored 19 Premier League goals from corners, breaking a record that had stood since 1992-93. Add indirect free kicks, direct free kicks and long throws and the total reaches 25 non-penalty set-piece goals, the most in the division and around 35 per cent of their 71 goals. No champion had previously taken more than 30 per cent of its non-penalty goals from dead balls. At the other end they conceded only eight set-piece goals, a net swing of 17 and the best figure in the league. The architecture belongs to Nicolas Jover , who arrived from Manchester City in July 2021 and built a system around crowding the goalkeeper in the six-yard box and attacking the flick-on at the back post. Gabriel Magalhaes was the primary target, winning first contact on 13 crossed corners. Declan Rice became the principal taker with 95 corners, 87 from the left, producing seven goals and 6.9 expected goals, the best of any taker in the league. Bukayo Saka handled the right. CHART: THE CORNER COUNT 2025-26 19 Premier League goals from corners, a competition record 2024-25 16, the previous record, also Arsenal 2020-21 6, the season before Nicolas Jover arrived 2026-27 so far 0 in eight matches, from any dead ball Arsenal goals from corners in the Premier League. Bars are scaled to the 19-goal record. So what has changed? One candidate is the refereeing guidance introduced for this season, which instructs officials to be stricter about holding, pulling and wrestling in the penalty area at set pieces, with penalties explicitly available as a sanction. The guidance retains a high bar for intervention, and the Premier League has not framed it as being about any one club. Observers have nonetheless nicknamed it the anti-Arsenal rule, because the screening that lets Arsenal 's runners get free is precisely the behaviour under review. The counter-view, argued at Arseblog, is that this is an anomaly rather than a problem. Arsenal have come close: Jurrien Timber headed in an Odegaard delivery against Sunderland only to be ruled marginally offside. Eight games is a small sample against a season of evidence. Both things can be true, and how quickly the first corner goes in after the break will tell us which is dominant. The other selection question is the centre-forward. Viktor Gyokeres scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, 14 in the league, and finished as Arsenal 's top scorer. He has started twice in six this season and has not scored. At Napoli , where Arsenal generated more than four expected goals, he did not have a single shot. Tim Stillman 's diagnosis at Arseblog is that he is a specialist in a system that does not have a specialism for him: limited in hold-up play, weakly involved in build-up, and not a volume scorer who compensates for either. Kai Havertz started the Champions League final. That is the hierarchy, whatever the fee said. On the injury front there is genuine cause for optimism. Ben White is back in training and expected for the resumption. Cristhian Mosquera is close. Piero Hincapie was withdrawn from Ecuador duty as a precaution. William Saliba remains the long wait: a back problem with no return date, though Arteta has described the progression as really positive and the defender has been registered for the Champions League league phase, which Arteta called an easy decision. HALE END Dowman Takes Over at Portman Road Two goals at 16, a debut at centre-back for Marli Salmon, a draw at Birmingham and a Dortmund loanee winning every week. The academy has rarely had a busier seven days. Mikel Arteta made nine changes at Ipswich Town on September 15 and still won 4-2, and the reason was a boy born on the last day of 2009. Max Dowman scored in the seventh minute after skipping past Cedric Kipre and finishing with his weaker foot, then scored again two minutes into the second half after adjusting to a ricochet off a Martin Zubimendi pass. Noni Madueke volleyed a third in the 16th minute and Mikel Merino curled a fourth off the post just before the hour. Anis Mehmeti and Chuba Akpom replied for the hosts. Dowman already holds a shelf of records, set out in the box below. He has now added the first senior brace of his career. Arteta called some of his individual actions outstanding and then, in the same breath, insisted the club's job is to protect his long-term progression rather than accelerate it. That tension is going to define the next twelve months. He was not the only teenager making a mark. Marli Salmon made his senior debut at centre-back at Portman Road and was, by the accounts of those watching, entirely composed. Four academy players finished the match on the pitch. Salmon has since withdrawn from the England Under-18 squad, while Dowman is away with the England Under-19s. The Under-21s drew 0-0 away at Birmingham City on September 18, a third draw in four Premier League 2 matches. Ben Clarke and Elijah Upson were praised for defensive solidity, Ceadach O'Neill and Ayden Hashi created in the first half, and 16-year-old Elyon Mbala made his Under-21 debut at half time. Two days earlier the same age group beat Leyton Orient 2-1 in the EFL Trophy, Archie Stevens equalising on the stroke of half time and Andre Harriman-Annous winning it in the 90th, with goalkeeper Khari Ranson making a crucial double save. James Scanlon , the 19-year-old signed from Manchester United in the summer, now has two goals in three and made the winner. David Horseman said he was really proud of them, and that it gave the group half a chance in the final group game. Out on loan, the headline remains Ethan Nwaneri at Borussia Dortmund , who have won four straight. He played 62 minutes in Saturday's 1-0 win at Stuttgart , having hit the post in a 3-2 Champions League win over Villarreal and started a 3-0 win against Paderborn . The rest had a harder weekend. Tommy Setford played 90 minutes for Stevenage in a 1-0 defeat at Leyton Orient , though his arrival had coincided with the club's first wins of the League One season. Ismeal Kabia played 77 minutes for St Mirren in a 3-0 home defeat to Dundee United . Charles Sagoe Jr played all 90 for Kalmar FF in a 5-0 loss to BK Hacken and was one of the few to emerge with credit. One more thread worth tracking: Andrea Berta 's youth recruitment. The sporting director completed an out-of-window move for 16-year-old Liverpool academy striker Vincent Joseph on September 18, the sixth significant teenage signing of his tenure, after Mylo Bernard , Axel Donczew , James Scanlon , Habeeb Ogunneye and the pre-contract for Andria Bartishvili . ARSENAL WOMEN Europe Arrives at Meadow Park With the Goals Still Missing Two goals in three WSL matches, a 94th-minute rescue against Manchester United, and a Champions League campaign that starts tonight. Renee Slegers has been careful not to panic, and she is right not to. Arsenal are unbeaten in the Women's Super League, with five points from three matches and one goal conceded. What they have not done is score, and in a league this tight that is the only statistic anyone is discussing. The sequence, set out in the box below, produced two goals in three games with almost three hours between them. Slegers has been precise about the diagnosis: the way Arsenal progress up the pitch is good, the way they dominate is good, and then the final third is where it goes. She frames it as both a tactical and a psychological problem, which is an unusually honest thing for a manager to say in September. Tonight the competition changes. Arsenal open their Women's Champions League league phase against HB Koge at Meadow Park, the first of six games in a group that also contains Lyon , Barcelona , Benfica , Paris FC and Inter Milan . The Danish champions are backed by Ballard Capital, the ownership behind the Kansas City Current , they sit top of their domestic league, and they counter quickly through two dangerous forwards. Arsenal beat them 3-0 in the same competition in November 2021. Slegers has signalled heavy rotation, with Chelsea away on Sunday and Paris FC away on September 30 immediately behind it, and she has framed the squad depth as something that lets her select with confidence rather than reluctance. Geraldine Reuteler has yet to make her Arsenal debut and should feature. Selina Cerci , who came on against Manchester United , is likely to start. The context for all of this is a genuinely radical summer. Arsenal signed Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Selina Cerci from Hoffenheim , Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Isabella Damm from Brondby , Elisa De Almeida from Paris Saint-Germain and Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig , most of them on free transfers. The numbers behind the arrivals are striking. Opta noted that Stanway has completed more passes in the opposition half since 2022-23 than anyone in the Bundesliga, at 2,919, and scored 24 league goals with 19 assists. Cerci scored 32 in 43 Bundesliga appearances at a shot-conversion rate of 25.4 per cent, against 15.8 for Alessia Russo and 16.7 for Stina Blackstenius . Batlle won 43 tackles, joint-most of any defender in the Champions League over the period measured. If the finishing is the problem, Arsenal have at least bought specifically for it. Michelle Agyemang and Katie Reid are both back in training after cruciate injuries. Elisa De Almeida is not expected back until after the October window, and Lotte Wubben-Moy was to be assessed before kickoff tonight. It is worth remembering the standard being defended. Arsenal won the Women's Champions League in 2025, reached the semi-finals last season before losing 4-3 on aggregate to OL Lyonnes , and beat Corinthians 3-2 after extra time at the Emirates in February to win the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup, Caitlin Foord scoring in the 104th minute. Slegers signed a contract through 2029 on the back of it. Two goals in three league games is a blip measured against that. It only becomes a story if it is still true in November. GUNNERS ABROAD Seventeen Gunners, Nine Countries, One Extended Interlull The merged September and October window keeps Arsenal's players away until the first week of October. Twice this week they play each other. This is the first season of the combined September and October international window, and it is why Arsenal do not play a club fixture again until Leeds United on October 10. Seventeen players have gone, spread across nine national teams, which is the largest group the club has sent away in a single break. The fixture of the week is Saturday at Wembley, where England host Spain . Bukayo Saka , Eberechi Eze , Myles Lewis-Skelly and Ezri Konsa line up against David Raya , Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino . Thomas Tuchel named a 27-man squad for the four-game window after England 's World Cup bronze. Lewis-Skelly 's recall is the notable selection, having missed the tournament through a shortage of minutes. Madueke 's omission is the notable absence. There is a second Arsenal-against-Arsenal fixture on Thursday, when Jurrien Timber 's Netherlands host Kai Havertz 's Germany in Amsterdam, and the two meet again in the reverse arrangement later in the window. Havertz is scheduled for only the first two matches of the window. Elsewhere: Martin Odegaard captains Norway against Denmark on Thursday and Portugal on Sunday. Riccardo Calafiori has Italy against Belgium on Friday and Turkiye on Monday. Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes are with Brazil for friendlies against Australia on Friday and again next Tuesday, both at three in the morning Pacific time for anyone sufficiently committed. Christos Tzolis is with Greece against Serbia and then Germany . Viktor Gyokeres is with Sweden against Romania and Poland , and has rarely needed a goal more. Two academy players are away with senior squads: James Scanlon with Gibraltar , for a friendly on Wednesday and a Nations League tie against Andorra on Sunday, and Ceadach O'Neill with Northern Ireland against Georgia and Hungary . Max Dowman is with the England Under-19s. Two withdrawals. Declan Rice pulled out of the England squad to manage his workload and will remain at London Colney. Piero Hincapie was withdrawn from the Ecuador squad with a groin issue and the same load-management reasoning. k: Europe's great managerial reshuffle faces its first verdicts as Maresca's Manchester City go four from four and Mourinho's Real Madrid chase Barcelona.
x: World football, every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Edition of Wednesday, September 16, 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The Great Reshuffle Meets Its First Reckoning Seven of Europe's biggest clubs changed manager inside a single calendar year. Four games into the new season, the early returns are already brutally uneven. There is a version of this season that will be written in a year's time as the most consequential managerial turnover in the modern history of the European game, and the remarkable thing is that we are only four matchdays into finding out whether that is true. Pep Guardiola is gone from Manchester City . Jose Mourinho is back at Real Madrid . Arne Slot was dismissed by Liverpool three weeks before the World Cup final and Ruben Amorim , sacked by Manchester United in January, is now standing in the technical area at AC Milan . Almost every door in the sport swung at once. The scale is easier to grasp in numbers than in names. Between the first day of January and the end of May, the Premier League's traditional big six lost seven managers: six sackings and one voluntary departure, an average of one every twenty-one days. Chelsea alone got through two, dismissing Enzo Maresca on New Year's Day and Liam Rosenior in April before settling on Xabi Alonso , who began work on the first of July. Tottenham Hotspur also burned through two before landing on Roberto De Zerbi . Only Mikel Arteta , in post since December 2019, has watched the whole carousel from a fixed seat. What makes this week the right moment to take stock is that the evidence has finally started arriving. The Champions League league phase opened on September 8 and the domestic leagues have now played four or five rounds. That is a small sample, and anyone claiming certainty from it is selling something. But it is no longer nothing, and the spread between the best and worst of these appointments is already wider than anybody would have predicted in July. The best of it, and the worst of it At the top of that spread sits Enzo Maresca , which is not where most people expected to find him. Handed the hardest inheritance in football, he has taken Manchester City to four wins from four in the Premier League, a 2-0 win at Porto in Europe and a 1-0 victory at Old Trafford, all while presiding over a squad that has been rebuilt around him rather than for him. Rodri , the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner and a World Cup winner with Spain in July, was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds. Savinho went to Tottenham Hotspur . Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah . Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid on a free. In their place came Elliot Anderson for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , and, on the window's final day, Enzo Fernandez for a fee that equalled the British record. It is a total rebuild conducted at full speed, in public, by a manager in his first month. At the other end sits the season's genuine emergency. Tottenham Hotspur have played four Premier League matches and scored zero goals. Not one. They sit seventeenth with two points and a goal record of nought scored and five conceded, which is the sort of line that normally belongs to a side already cut adrift in April, not one four games into September under a coach hired precisely because he is supposed to make teams play. Roberto De Zerbi arrived from Marseille on March 31 on a long-term deal, with sporting director Johan Lange calling him one of the most creative and forward-thinking coaches in world football. The creativity has not yet shown up on a scoresheet. “We worked four years in the same structure and we always felt comfortable. Now, we need time.” Unai Emery , whose Aston Villa won the Europa League in May and have one point from four Neither a triumph nor a disaster, yet Between those poles, the picture is genuinely difficult to read. Andoni Iraola , who left Bournemouth for Liverpool in June, has one win and three draws from four: unbeaten, but blunted, and a goalless home afternoon against Fulham did nothing to quiet the question of whether his high-pressing model survives contact with the expectation at Anfield. He did at least win his European opener, edging Atletico Madrid 2-1. Michael Carrick 's Manchester United are thirteenth in the league but put four past Sabah in Europe. Matthias Jaissle inherited a Newcastle United side that sold its three best players in a single summer. And then there is Madrid. Jose Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu on June 11, signing until 2029, sixteen years after he first walked in and three managers after Xabi Alonso left in January. His Real Madrid have twelve points from five, beat Inter 2-1 on the opening night in Europe through Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde , and put four past Rayo Vallecano at the weekend. They are also, already, three points behind a Barcelona side that has won all five of its league games with a goal difference of plus seventeen. The reshuffle gave Madrid a serial winner. It did not give them a head start. The honest summary is that the market for managers behaved this year less like a market and more like a panic. Clubs did not so much choose replacements as grab whoever was nearest when the music stopped, and the reason the table already looks strange is that several of them grabbed well and several grabbed badly. The next three months will sort them. What is not in doubt is that the sport has never asked so many new men to answer so many questions at once. Arsenal lead on goal difference. Also in the lead Europe's Second Tier Opens, and Three English Clubs Step Into the Unknown The Europa League league phase begins tonight and tomorrow. Sunderland , Crystal Palace and Bournemouth have never been here in this form, and AC Milan and Juventus would rather not be. The Europa League returns this evening with the first of its eight league-phase matchdays, and the entry list tells you a great deal about how the last eighteen months have gone for some very large football clubs. AC Milan open at home to Benfica . Juventus host N.E.C. tomorrow. Celtic , Lyon , Marseille , Real Sociedad and Bayer Leverkusen are all here too. This is a deep field by any historical standard. For the three English entrants it is something closer to genuinely new territory. Sunderland begin at home to AZ Alkmaar tonight, seeded thirty-third of thirty-six and playing continental football for the first time in decades. Crystal Palace host Lech Poznan tomorrow, and Bournemouth , seeded eighth and the best placed of the three, travel to Real Sociedad under Marco Rose , who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer. The format rewards consistency over survival. Each of the thirty-six clubs plays eight different opponents, the top eight go straight to the last sixteen, ninth to twenty-fourth drop into a knockout playoff round, and twenty-fifth or lower means elimination from Europe altogether. There is no group to escape and no easy draw to hide behind, which is why a slow start here is far more expensive than it used to be. The holders are not in the field. Aston Villa won this competition in May, beating SC Freiburg 3-0 in Istanbul through Youri Tielemans , Emiliano Buendia and Morgan Rogers for a first trophy in thirty years, and were promoted into the Champions League for their trouble. Two of those three scorers have since been sold. That is a story for the transfer pages, and it is not a happy one. Transfer News City Pay the British Record to Undo Their Own Midfield Enzo Fernandez cost 125 million pounds and reunites with the manager who sold him. Rodri went the other way. The single largest transaction of the summer was also its strangest. On deadline day, Manchester City paid Chelsea 125 million pounds for Enzo Fernandez , a fee that equals the British record set when Liverpool bought Alexander Isak from Newcastle United in 2025. The Argentine signed a five-year deal. The move was confirmed by Sky Sports , ESPN and Al Jazeera . Status: official. The symmetry is almost too neat. Enzo Fernandez now plays for Enzo Maresca , the manager who coached him at Stamford Bridge and was sacked by Chelsea on New Year's Day. Chelsea, meanwhile, booked an 18 million pound profit on a player they bought for 107 million three and a half years ago, which is a respectable piece of accounting and an awkward piece of squad-building. It was awkward because the replacement did not arrive. Chelsea had a 47 million pound deal in place for Lamine Camara when Monaco withdrew from the sale late, leaving Xabi Alonso a midfielder short on the day he lost his most expensive one. Chelsea honoured the Fernandez sale regardless. Set that against City's other business and a coherent, if severe, logic appears. Rodri was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds in mid-August after seven years and a World Cup win with Spain . Savinho and Omar Marmoush went to Tottenham Hotspur , the latter initially on loan. Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah for around 52 million pounds and Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid for nothing at all. In came Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for a reported 81 million, and Iliman Ndiaye . City spent roughly 319 million pounds. They also tore out the spine of the most successful English side of the last decade and replaced it with players whose combined age barely reaches the one they sold. Madrid Build a Spine and Pay For Almost None of It Two of Jose Mourinho 's six signings arrived on free transfers. The one they did pay heavily for cost 140 million euros. Real Madrid 's summer is the clearest demonstration this year of what a club can do when it plans two years ahead of a contract cycle. Ibrahima Konate joined from Liverpool on a free transfer on a four-year deal, a move confirmed by ESPN and Sky Sports . Bernardo Silva arrived from Manchester City , also free, on a two-year deal. Status on both: official. The paid-for business was substantial. Marc Cucurella came from Chelsea in a deal Sky valued at 51.8 million pounds and Madrid's own books at around 60 million euros, announced by the club on June 15. Denzel Dumfries joined from Inter . And Yan Diomande arrived from RB Leipzig for a reported 140 million euros on a deal to 2033, the second-largest fee of the entire window. Endrick returned from a loan at Lyon . Out went an era. Dani Carvajal left at the end of his contract after twenty-three seasons at the club. David Alaba also departed as a free agent, and Dani Ceballos left by mutual agreement. Antonio Rudiger signed a one-year extension to 2027. Newcastle Sold Their Three Best Players, and Say They Would Do It Again Bruno Guimaraes , Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon all left in one window. The sporting director is unapologetic. No club in Europe had a stranger summer than Newcastle United . Sandro Tonali went to Tottenham Hotspur for 92.5 million pounds. Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for a reported 69.3 million. Bruno Guimaraes , the captain and the emotional centre of the side, went to a Premier League rival for 75 million. The club then spent roughly 295 million pounds rebuilding. Eddie Howe had already gone, replaced by Matthias Jaissle . What is unusual is not the churn but the candour about it. Sporting director Ross Wilson told reporters that if you want to be a successful club in the Premier League you have to trade players, and that if you do not, you get stuck. He went further, naming Lewis Hall and Tino Livramento as players who may themselves leave in time. Chief financial officer Simon Capper was equally blunt about the mechanics, explaining that one incoming deal required Nick Woltemade 's loan to Juventus to clear the wage space first. This is profit and sustainability regulation as a design constraint rather than a threat, and it is worth watching closely, because Newcastle are describing openly what several of their rivals do quietly. The early league evidence is inconclusive: twelfth after four, one win, one defeat at home and a trip to face Hull City on Saturday. Paris Sold an Attack, Bought Another, and Forgot How to Win at Home Bradley Barcola left for Liverpool in a deal worth up to 123 million pounds. Luis Enrique says he could not promise him a starting place. Paris Saint-Germain are the reigning European champions and the five-time reigning champions of France. They are also, this morning, seventh in Ligue 1 with five points from four matches. The gap between those two sentences is the most interesting thing in French football. The squad turnover explains a good deal of it. Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in a deal reported at up to 123 million pounds including variables. Goncalo Ramos went to AC Milan for around 63.7 million. In came Ferran Torres from Barcelona , among others. Luis Enrique was unusually direct about the Barcola exit, telling reporters that the player's desire was to play a more important role in the side, something the manager could not guarantee him. He called the window exceptional. The results have not agreed. Paris went four matches without a win, drawing twice from two goals down and losing 2-1 at home to Monaco on September 4, before finally beating Brest 1-0 on Sunday through, appropriately enough, Ferran Torres . Ousmane Dembele , the reigning Ballon d'Or holder, Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had gone four games without a goal between them. Then, on September 9, the same team put six past Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League with a Ferran Torres hat-trick. Whatever is wrong in Paris, it is not the forwards' finishing, and it is probably not permanent. Luis Enrique 's own assessment, offered with characteristic serenity, was an invitation to bet on who would be champion at the end of the season. Arsenal's business is covered in the companion edition and is not shown. The Rumour Mill The window shut on September 1, so everything below is January business or contract business. Certainty labels are attached to each. Treat the unlabelled as gossip, because that is what it is. Bruno Fernandes and the option year Advanced talks, no agreement David Ornstein reported to Sky Sports after the Manchester derby that Bruno Fernandes remains in discussions with Manchester United over a new contract but that the parties have not found common ground. His deal expires at the end of this season and United hold a one-year extension option. The 32-year-old is the reigning PFA Players' Player of the Season, is nominated for this year's Ballon d'Or and has five goal involvements in five matches. This is the most consequential contract situation in England. JJ Gabriel wants out of Old Trafford Reported, single-sourced on the destination The Sun reports that Manchester United fear teenage forward JJ Gabriel will join Manchester City after asking to leave. The Athletic separately places Real Madrid in the running. Gabriel is fifteen. Both strands are credible on the player's desire to go and thin on where he goes. Endrick to United in January Speculative link AS in Spain suggests Manchester United could move for Endrick in January if the Brazilian becomes available. He has just returned to Real Madrid from a loan at Lyon and is behind Kylian Mbappe in the order. No talks have been reported by either club. Branthwaite, revived Concrete interest The Daily Mail reports that Manchester United have restarted their long pursuit of Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite . This link has been live in some form for three windows and has never yet reached a bid that Everton were willing to discuss. Araujo's option to buy Loan active, purchase undecided Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool from Barcelona in August on loan with an option to buy, confirmed by Liverpool and Sky Sports . Fabrizio Romano reported on September 13 that Liverpool are pleased with how the move has gone. Whether the option is exercised is the question that will define Liverpool's January. Barcelona want a number nine Gossip talkSPORT lists Harry Kane , Erling Haaland , Julian Alvarez and Nick Woltemade as Barcelona striker targets. That is less a shortlist than a list of good strikers, and it should be read accordingly. Separately, Sport reports the club is negotiating a contract extension with Raphinha , who has six league goals already. The Raphinha strand is the one worth following. Henderson set for a Palace payday Reported The Daily Mail reports Dean Henderson is poised to become Crystal Palace 's highest-paid player on a new contract, despite interest from Nottingham Forest . Around the Leagues Premier League Four matchdays in, the table has two perfect records at the top and a genuine curiosity beneath them. Manchester City are unbeaten with twelve points and won the Manchester derby 1-0 at Old Trafford on Sunday, a result that said as much about Michael Carrick 's side as Enzo Maresca 's: Manchester United are thirteenth with four points despite Bruno Fernandes playing some of the best football of his career. Behind the leaders, Leeds United and Hull City are third and fourth on eight points apiece, which nobody forecast in August. Daniel Farke 's Leeds are unbeaten. Sergej Jakirovic 's newly promoted Hull have taken points off Chelsea and Aston Villa already. The bottom of the table is where the season's real stories are. Tottenham Hotspur have not scored a league goal. Four matches, nought goals, two points, seventeenth, and a 0-0 at home to Everton on Saturday that extended the drought. Aston Villa are nineteenth with one point, which is remarkable for a team that lifted the Europa League in May. Their summer explains most of it: Morgan Rogers sold to Chelsea for 117 million pounds, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa both gone, two of the three scorers from the final in Istanbul now playing elsewhere. Unai Emery has asked for patience, saying after a goalless draw with Hull City that his side deserved more and that he feels the team is progressing. Reports that the club is weighing Emery's position trace to a single former club scout speaking to Football Insider, and should be treated as exactly that thin. Villa did at least win 3-2 at Club Brugge in the Champions League through John McGinn , Emiliano Buendia and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson . Below Villa, Coventry City have the worst start of any promoted side in recent memory: four defeats, no points, no goals scored and ten conceded, including a 5-0 home defeat to Brighton on Sunday. Frank Lampard took them up and is discovering how unforgiving the step is. Liverpool sit eighth, unbeaten but drawn three times under Andoni Iraola , the goalless afternoon against Fulham the most telling of them. Brighton have scored thirteen in four, more than anyone. And Fulham are eighteenth with a point under Alvaro Arbeloa , who was managing Real Madrid in January and is now fighting relegation in west London, which may be the single most 2026 sentence in this edition. La Liga Barcelona have won all five, scored seventeen, conceded two and lead by three points. Raphinha is the division's top scorer with six. Lamine Yamal scored twice in Sunday's 4-2 win at Levante , where Karim Adeyemi also found the net. This is a side playing with the confidence of a double champion, which is what they are. Real Madrid are second on twelve, having beaten Rayo Vallecano 4-1 with two from Kylian Mbappe and goals for Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham . Atletico Madrid are quietly excellent, winning 3-0 at Real Sociedad through Alejandro Grimaldo , Jonathan David and Giuliano Simeone . The genuine surprise is Alaves , third on ten points. The promoted clubs have brought real romance. Racing Santander are back after fourteen years and beat Alaves 2-1. Deportivo La Coruna are back after eight and sit sixth. Malaga , also back after eight, drew at Celta Vigo . At the other end, Valencia have one point from five, which for a club of that history is an alarm rather than a slow start. Bundesliga Three matchdays in and Bayern Munich are fourth. Above them, improbably, are SC Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund , both perfect on nine points. Freiburg, beaten Europa League finalists in May, thrashed Borussia Monchengladbach 5-0 on Saturday and have a goal difference of plus nine. Bayern have seven points from three after winning 2-1 at newly promoted SV Elversberg . More striking is who is not on the scorers list: Harry Kane , winner of the Torjagerkanone in each of his three seasons in Germany, is not among the leaders. The top of that chart is shared on three goals by Younes Ebnoutalib of Eintracht Frankfurt , Yuito Suzuki of Freiburg , Phillip Tietz of Mainz , Patrik Schick of Bayer Leverkusen and Michael Gregoritsch of Augsburg . SV Elversberg have become the fifty-ninth club to play in the Bundesliga and sit sixth with six points, having already beaten Monchengladbach 4-3 away. Schalke 04 are back after three years and won 3-1 at Union Berlin on Friday. RB Leipzig beat Hamburg 5-0 under Martin Demichelis , and Bayer Leverkusen have four points from three in Carles Martinez Novell 's first season. Serie A Saturday evening in Rome is the fixture of the European weekend. Roma and Inter are the only unbeaten sides, level on points with Roma ahead on goal difference, and they meet at the Stadio Olimpico at 18:00 local time. Gian Piero Gasperini called it an opportunity to measure up against the best and show his side can do better, which is about as close to a gauntlet as he throws. Roma's form is built on Donyell Malen , who has six goals in four matches, equalling a club record set by Francesco Totti in 2001-02, with Paulo Dybala supplying him. Gasperini has praised how the two complete each other. Inter, the reigning champions, have won all three of theirs but lost 2-1 at Real Madrid in Europe. Elsewhere the champions-elect narrative is getting complicated. Juventus lost 3-2 at Sassuolo on Sunday after leading, with former Juventus player Vasilije Adzic scoring the winner, and Luciano Spalletti is already fielding questions about his future despite public backing. AC Milan drew 2-2 at Lazio in Ruben Amorim 's latest outing, with Christian Pulisic registering his first assist of the season. And Fiorentina , who lost their first three, won 4-2 at Venezia thanks to a hat-trick from Franco Mastantuono , who became the youngest Argentinian to score one in Europe's top five leagues, a record previously held by Lionel Messi . Ligue 1 Three clubs share the lead on ten points: Lille , Monaco and Rennes . Davide Ancelotti 's Lille beat Troyes 2-0 on Sunday through Santos and a stoppage-time goal from Ethan Mbappe . Filipe Luis 's Monaco were held 1-1 at Strasbourg . Rennes beat Marseille 1-0 on Friday through Adrien Thomasson . Paris Saint-Germain finally won, 1-0 at Brest through Ferran Torres , and are seventh on five points. Marseille have now lost two in a row under Bruno Genesio and travel to Besiktas in the Europa League tomorrow. Auxerre claimed a first win of the season, 1-0 over Nice . French football also spent the summer in mourning. Eric Roy , who coached Brest to the Champions League and was still in post last season, died on June 17 at the age of 58 after an illness. Julien Lachuer has succeeded him at Brest. Major League Soccer Nashville SC are eight points clear at the top of the overall standings and closing on a first Supporters' Shield. They drew 2-2 at Inter Miami at the weekend in the fixture of the regular season, Lionel Messi putting Miami ahead before Sam Surridge equalised late. The draw denied Nashville a playoff berth they will clinch shortly anyway. Lionel Messi leads the Golden Boot race with eighteen. Behind the headline act, the league's most interesting attacking story is at Orlando City , where Antoine Griezmann has eight goals and, outside Messi himself, the best non-penalty goal contribution rate per ninety minutes of any player with ten or more starts this season. Orlando beat Toronto 3-0. Rafael Navarro has four goals in two starts for St. Louis City since a reported twelve million dollar trade from Colorado , Philadelphia beat San Diego 5-0 with a brace from Cavan Sullivan , who now has seventeen goal contributions in under 1,400 minutes, and Vancouver Whitecaps lead the Western Conference. The regular season ends on November 7 and MLS Cup is on December 18. They are seventeenth. 59 goals in 59 games Erling Haaland 's Champions League record after his double at Porto on the opening matchday. 6 goals in four games Donyell Malen 's start for Roma , equalling a club record set by Francesco Totti in 2001-02. In Brief The 2026 Ballon d'Or will be presented on Monday October 26 at the London Palladium, the award's seventieth anniversary and its first ceremony in London.
