Tonight at Portman Road Arsenal restart the competition that humiliated them in March, with a defence held together by improvisation. Six months ago Arsenal walked up the Wembley steps as losers. Manchester City beat them 2-0 in the Carabao Cup final on 22 March, Nico O'Reilly scoring twice, and a season that ended with a first league title in twenty-two years began its run-in with a reminder that one pot has eluded this club since 1993. Tonight, at 12 noon Pacific, the Gunners walk out at Portman Road to start it all again. They do so having won everything they have played. The Community Shield against the same Manchester City , 3-0 . Coventry City at home, 3-0 . Aston Villa away, 1-0 . Chelsea at the Emirates, 2-1 . Napoli away in the Champions League, 1-0 . Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday, 2-0 . Eight goals scored in the Premier League, one conceded, twelve points from twelve, first on goal difference. What makes the run remarkable is who has not played a minute of it. William Saliba was withdrawn after half an hour of France 's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in July with a back problem the club described, in a statement on 23 July , as requiring a managed recovery programme and an absence of an extended period . There has been no surgery and, as of Mikel Arteta 's press conference on 11 September, no new timeline. That single absence reshaped the summer. Arsenal spent GBP 51m plus GBP 4m on Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on 21 August, a signing the club framed explicitly as cover for a centre-back crisis, and Konsa made his full debut against Chelsea because Cristhian Mosquera had gone off injured at Villa Park. Jurrien Timber only returned to team training in the second week of September after a groin problem dating to March. Ben White limped out of Saturday's win with a groin strain and missed Monday's session. “He will have his chance. He will have his minutes, and he will have to earn them like anybody else.” Mikel Arteta on Max Dowman, 14 September So the team that lines up in Suffolk will be a guess. Kepa Arrizabalaga is the expected goalkeeper. Timber needs minutes and may take one centre-back slot; the other could go to Marli Salmon , the seventeen-year-old who signed his first professional contract on 29 August and has not appeared for the senior side since the FA Cup tie at Mansfield Town in March. Piero Hincapie and Myles Lewis-Skelly are the likelier full-backs. Further forward the interest is in the players who have been watching. Martin Zubimendi has not started a Premier League or Champions League match this season. Viktor Gyokeres has played twenty-seven minutes across the opening four league games and has yet to start one. Noni Madueke , Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are all in the same bracket: expensive, capable, and short of rhythm. And then there is Max Dowman , who is sixteen until New Year's Eve, sits outside the twenty-five-man Premier League list because of his age, and has been an unused substitute four times already, including in Naples. He played an hour for the under-21s against Chelsea on Saturday instead of travelling to Sunderland. Arteta would not promise a start, which in the current climate is its own kind of answer. Ipswich Town , back in the division and tenth with six points from four, are not a soft landing. They have scored seven and conceded ten, which is to say they will have a go. Arteta 's line all week has been that there is no second tier to this squad, and that every competition counts. The argument for taking him at his word is sitting in the Wembley record books, unpleasantly recent. According to Fabrizio Romano that is about to stop being true. Mikel Arteta 's contract expires at the end of this season, a fact that has hovered over the club since the spring. Fabrizio Romano reported on 14 September that the extension is in its final stages , with lawyers working through the remaining details, and described Arteta as very, very close to signing. The proposed term is three years. The timeline matters. First contact with his representatives came in March or April, before the title was mathematically won. Josh Kroenke called a new deal an utmost priority in May. Arteta himself, speaking to Sky Sports on 15 August, said he wanted to stay and that the club would resolve it in a very organic way when the possibility arose. Nothing is signed. But a manager who has won the league, reached a domestic cup final and started the defence with six straight wins is not a difficult negotiation, and the direction of travel is unmistakable. Expect an announcement rather than a saga. Transfer News Zubimendi, Madrid and the January question nobody at the club wants asked A Spanish journalist says it is done. The evidence that matters is the team sheet. On 14 September Javi Roldan of El Confidencial said flatly that Martin Zubimendi is going to be Madrid's signing in the winter window . The figure attached by Spanish outlets is EUR 70m , the same sum Arsenal paid Real Sociedad in the summer of 2025. Treat the claim itself with care. It is one reporter, amplified by aggregators, with no corroboration from David Ornstein , Fabrizio Romano , the BBC or Sky. Nothing in it has reached even the concrete-interest tier. The underlying fact is another matter, and it is not in dispute. Zubimendi has made four substitute appearances in the Premier League and one in the Champions League this season. He has started neither competition. He lost his place late last season and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes for GBP 75m has not made getting it back any easier. TEAMtalk add, on their own sourcing, that Zubimendi would be willing to push for an exit if he is not playing regularly by January, that Real Madrid have kept contact with his camp, and that Chelsea are watching. That is a plausible shape for a story rather than a story. It is also the kind of thing that becomes true if a player spends autumn on a bench. The window that was: a level-raiser that never arrived David Ornstein 's verdict on Arsenal's summer was blunt, and the numbers behind it are stranger than the headline suggests. Arsenal spent heavily and ended the window without the attacking signing they wanted. Ornstein 's assessment, published on 2 September and relayed by Daily Cannon, was that the club failed to land a level-raiser in attack, having pursued Vinicius Junior as the primary target and then Julian Alvarez , Malick Fofana , Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers . Christos Tzolis , at GBP 34m from Club Brugge , was a replacement for Leandro Trossard , not an addition. The Vinicius thread is worth closing properly, because it keeps being resurrected. Ornstein reported that Arsenal were prepared to commit major funds and that the move had been approved at every level of the club. Romano reported on 5 August that Real Madrid had improved their offer materially. On 6 August the player signed a six-year extension to 2032. Anyone still writing that link is recycling. Alvarez failed for a different and more bruising reason. Ornstein , on 29 August : the Argentine spoke to Mikel Arteta and said he doesn't want to come , his heart set on Barcelona . Atletico Madrid would have done a deal. Arsenal were prepared to agree one club to club. The player said no. Reports of a January return are aggregator speculation and should not be attributed to Ornstein , who said the opposite. Two late near-misses give the window its texture. The Daily Mail's Isaan Khan reported that assistant manager Gabriel Heinze personally contacted Inter Milan about Lautaro Martinez in the final week; Inter refused to entertain it. And Chema Aragon , sporting director of Racing Santander , said publicly that a loan for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia seemed like it was done with Arsenal before Betis chose a co-ownership arrangement instead. What Arsenal did do was sell. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al-Hilal on 3 September for GBP 60m guaranteed , a club-record sale, two days after the English window had shut and so at a moment when the money could not be reinvested. The Squad A back four by committee, a No. 9 problem that is not a problem yet How Arteta is winning without his best defender, and why Kai Havertz keeps starting ahead of a striker who cost more than the house. Start with the defence, because everything else follows from it. Saliba is out indefinitely. Timber missed the first month. Mosquera was hurt at Villa Park. White came off at Sunderland. Arsenal have conceded one Premier League goal in four matches regardless, and that goal came inside ninety seconds against Chelsea . The solution has been positional rather than personnel-based. Gabriel Magalhaes anchors, Konsa slots in beside him or at right-back, Hincapie plays inside or left, and Lewis-Skelly has started all four league games at left-back, 273 minutes, no cards. In this edition At a Glance · Pick of the Month · The Map · The Calendar · Music, Arts and Nightlife · Food, Drink and Festivals · Outdoors, Sports and Active · On the Horizon At a Glance Five weeks from the Moon Festival to the pumpkin fields This edition runs five weeks, from the middle of September to the middle of October, and it is the busiest stretch of the Bay Area year. The first weekend alone has the Greek Festival, Oktoberfest on Front, the Autumn Moon Festival in Chinatown, the Haight Street Fair and Comedy Day, every one of them free to walk into. The last weekend of September is the loudest. Portola fills Pier 80 on September 26 and 27, Folsom Street closes on the 27th, and the Giants play their final home series against the Dodgers. If you would rather be somewhere quieter, the Presidio hosts a free Chuseok harvest festival and Pleasanton hosts Corgi Con. October opens with the best free weekend of the year. An all-star tribute to Steve Earle at the Masonic on October 1 leads into three days of Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, and the Castro Street Fair follows on the Sunday. Fleet Week arrives on October 4, with the Blue Angels over the Marina from October 9 to 11. Sport is everywhere. The Valkyries close the regular season with two home nights and head into the playoffs as one of the best teams in the league. The Warriors play three preseason games, and the Roots say goodbye to the Coliseum on October 10. 12 of the 40 listings are outside San Francisco, from Half Moon Bay to Lake Merritt. The weekend read The first weekend is a Mission and Chinatown weekend. Start at the Greek Festival on Valencia on Friday, walk to Front Street for Oktoberfest, and save Saturday for the Autumn Moon Festival on Grant Avenue. Sunday September 20 is the day to be in or near Golden Gate Park: Flower Piano closes, Comedy Day is in Robin Williams Meadow, and the Haight Street Fair is a short walk away. Bay FC and the Earthquakes are both in the South Bay that weekend if you want sport instead. Mid-September is usually the warmest part of the San Francisco year, but the fog still comes in by late afternoon in the west of the city. Carry a layer to anything in the park. The act-now clock Now Portola passes are on sale for September 26 and 27, with two-day passes from $380 and single days from $250 at launch prices. They go up as tiers sell out. Arrive early The Valkyries give a shoulder bag to the first 10,000 fans on September 19, with doors at 4:30pm. Every fan on September 18 gets a snapback. Book ahead Autumn Lights at Lake Merritt on October 15 to 17 sells out most years, Friday and Saturday first. Corgi Con tickets are cheaper online until September 25. Once only The Steve Earle tribute at the Masonic on October 1 is a single benefit night with Emmylou Harris and Jackson Browne. It will not repeat. Last chance Sunday September 27 is the Giants' last home game of 2026, and Sunday September 20 is the last day of Flower Piano. Pick of the Month Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Friday October 2 to Sunday October 4, 2026 · Hellman Hollow, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco · Free. No tickets, no wristbands. It is the second edition running that Hardly Strictly has been our pick, and the reason has not changed: it is the largest free music festival in the country, it is in our own park, and it is free forever because Warren Hellman endowed it that way. This is its 26th year. The 2026 bill is as strong as any in recent memory. My Morning Jacket, Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, Mavis Staples, Emmylou Harris, Alison Krauss and Union Station, Los Lobos, Marty Stuart, Old Crow Medicine Show, Sierra Hull, Jesse Welles, Hiss Golden Messenger and Kathleen Edwards are all confirmed. The night before, the Masonic hosts An Evening Honoring Steve Earle, with Earle himself, Emmylou Harris, Jackson Browne, Hot Tuna and Molly Tuttle, benefiting Sweetwater Spectrum. If you can get a ticket, do the pair. Practical advice: do not drive. The N Judah, the 5 Fulton and the 7 all serve the park and all will be full. Walk in from the east, pick one stage and stay put for a few sets, and bring a layer for when the fog arrives around four. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World Football, Every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Vol. 1, No. 37 Wednesday, September 9, 2026 In This Edition The Lead · The Benches · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Europe Reopens on a Map Nobody Recognises The Champions League league phase began on Tuesday with the holders in disarray at home, a returning heavyweight in the Real Madrid dugout and a Manchester City side that has spent a decade being one thing learning to be another. Eighteen matches across three nights, and the shape of the season is already arguing with itself. T here is a version of this competition that reads exactly as you would expect. Real Madrid beat Inter . Manchester City won at Porto because Erling Haaland scored twice. Borussia Dortmund came from behind in front of the Yellow Wall. Read the six Tuesday scorelines cold and you would conclude that European football has spent the summer standing still. It has done the opposite. The men in the dugouts have almost all changed. The champions of Europe are 14th in their own league. The best player in the Premier League for a decade is playing in Turkey. And the two clubs who contested last season's final have between them lost a manager, a talisman and, in one case, an entire idea of themselves. Matchday one was not a continuation. It was an audit. Start at the Bernabéu, because that is where the noise is. José Mourinho returned to Real Madrid in June on a three-year deal, installed by a president who had just survived an election fought over a trophyless season, and his first European night back ended 2-1 against Inter . It should have been a coronation. Instead it was a survival exercise. Kylian Mbappé finished neatly on 14 minutes, Fede Valverde punished a calamitous piece of goalkeeping three minutes later, and then Madrid spent an hour missing chances while Thibaut Courtois made save after save. Carlos Augusto scored late. There were whistles at the final whistle of a home win. That anxiety has a cause, and it is not the Champions League. Four days earlier Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis , beaten by a Troy Parrott goal and by Álvaro Valles saving a stoppage-time Mbappé penalty. Madrid demanded a retake for encroachment; the referee and VAR said no, correctly under the letter of the law, since Marc Bartra still had a foot planted outside the area. Mourinho's response was pure Mourinho. "If the VAR did not order the penalty retaken because they do not know the rulebook," he said, "they need to go home." Madrid are third in La Liga, three points off Barcelona , with Rodrygo out until 2027 and Ferland Mendy out until April. Four matches without a win, seven points behind Monaco, and Paris Saint-Germain responded by extending the manager who won them back-to-back European Cups until 2030. On the same day they lost. Which brings us to the genuine oddity of this September. Paris Saint-Germain are the double defending champions of Europe. They beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest in May after a 1-1 draw, then beat Aston Villa 2-1 in the Super Cup in August. They are also, as of Sunday night, 14th in Ligue 1 with two points from three games, beaten at the Parc des Princes by Monaco and beaten before that by Lens in the Trophée des Champions. Luis Enrique is not having it. Asked whether his players were physically short after a summer in which most of them went deep into a World Cup, he answered "No, no, no," pointed at the expected-goals numbers, and called the Monaco defeat "inexplicable". His club backed him on the spot: on Friday, hours before kick-off against Monaco, PSG announced contract extensions for Luis Enrique to 2030 and for João Neves , Willian Pacho , Lucas Beraldo , Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz . The French press has settled on the word "préoccupant". Concerning, not yet a crisis. It is worth remembering they sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool for a reported £106m and Gonçalo Ramos to Milan , and are integrating Ferran Torres and Maghnes Akliouche in their places. Manchester City , meanwhile, look ominously well. Enzo Maresca took a job nobody has held since 2016 and has won his first three league games and now his first European one, 2-0 at the Estádio do Dragão. Haaland scored on 67 and in stoppage time to reach 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances, four days after his winner against Coventry City became the 300th goal of his career. City spent something close to £320m rebuilding a midfield they had gutted, selling Rodri to Barcelona and buying Elliot Anderson , Ayyoub Bouaddi and, on deadline day, Enzo Fernández from Chelsea . "The squad is complete," Maresca said. On the evidence of eleven days, he is not wrong. The romance came from further down the pots. AEK Athens won a Champions League match for the first time in 20 years, Răzvan Marin bending in a free kick to beat LASK . Real Betis , in their first Champions League game in 21 years, went to Lille, fell behind twice and won 3-2 with two Marc Bartra headers either side of half-time and a Parrott finish on the hour. Aston Villa , who won the Europa League in May and have not scored a Premier League goal all season, went to Club Brugge and won 3-2 through John McGinn and Nicolas Jackson . That is the competition doing what the 36-team format promised: giving good clubs somewhere to be extraordinary. Borussia Dortmund 's 3-2 over Villarreal was the strangest of the six: five goals in the second half, an own goal by Renato Veiga , two from Serhou Guirassy including a penalty he won himself, then a Guirassy own goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time. It was also overshadowed. Konstantinos Karetsas , the 18-year-old signed from Genk in the summer, collapsed with circulatory problems in the 27th minute and was taken to hospital. The club said afterwards that he "is doing well under the circumstances", which was the only line from the night that mattered. The rest of matchday one lands across Wednesday and Thursday, and it is the better half of the card. Liverpool host Atlético Madrid at Anfield, which pitches Andoni Iraola 's high-line, high-pressing Liverpool against the one manager in Europe who has built a twelve-year career out of making that style look naive. Iraola has inherited a club that finished fifth, sacked Arne Slot , lost Mohamed Salah on a free transfer and replaced him with £161m of Barcola and Jérémy Jacquet . Diego Simeone arrives with Julián Álvarez , Ademola Lookman , Cristian Romero and Jonathan David , and having just been beaten 3-0 at Athletic Club . Anfield against Atlético has never once been dull. Elsewhere on Wednesday, Barcelona open at a Camp Nou now licensed for 62,652 and still being rebuilt around them, having scored 17 goals in four league games. Napoli , two straight league defeats in and missing Scott McTominay , host a visitor Massimiliano Allegri has publicly told his players is worth chasing 12 points in this phase for. And PSG, mercifully, get Slovan Bratislava . Thursday is the competition's exclusive night: Bayern Munich host Bodø/Glimt , Manchester United are back in the Champions League against Sabah , Roma return after seven years away at Fenerbahçe , and Como play the first Champions League match in their history at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, a 13,602-seat ground on the lake that UEFA formally cleared only five days ago. Eight games each, one table of 36, and a final in Madrid on June 5. This edition closed before Wednesday's results were confirmed, so treat the card below as the state of play at press time. The early reading is that the favourites are Manchester City and Barcelona, that Real Madrid are a better team than their nerves suggest, and that the holders have a great deal of work to do before anyone should write them off. Champions of Europe rarely stay 14th for long. Key Facts · The Route to Madrid Format. 36 clubs, one league table, eight matches each against eight different opponents. Top eight go straight to the last 16. Ninth to 24th play a knockout play-off round. Matchdays. MD1 Sept 8 to 10 · MD2 Oct 13 to 14 · MD3 Oct 20 to 21 · MD4 Nov 3 to 4 · MD5 Nov 24 to 25 · MD6 Dec 8 to 9 · MD7 Jan 19 to 20 · MD8 Jan 27, all kicking off simultaneously. Final. Saturday June 5, 2027, Estadio Metropolitano, Madrid. Holders. Paris Saint-Germain , who beat Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw at the Puskás Aréna, Budapest, on May 30. Also in Europe. Europa League league phase begins Sept 16 to 17. Conference League begins Oct 15 and runs to six matchdays, with the final at the Beşiktaş Stadium in Istanbul on June 2. Klopp came back, for a country. Mourinho went home. Zidane took France. If you stopped watching in May, almost nothing you knew about who stands on the touchline is still true. The scale of it only registers when you list it. Pep Guardiola resigned at Manchester City on May 22 after a decade, and did not take another club: he is now a global ambassador for City Football Group. Arne Slot was sacked by Liverpool eight days later, a year after winning the league, having taken 20 defeats in all competitions. Eddie Howe stepped down at Newcastle United at the end of July after nearly five years and a 12th-place finish. Neither Slot nor Howe has taken a new job. The vacancies cascaded. Enzo Maresca left Chelsea in January and, after a spell out, took the City job in June. Xabi Alonso , who left Real Madrid by mutual consent in January, is now at Stamford Bridge on a four-year deal, having succeeded a caretaker regime that followed Liam Rosenior 's April dismissal. Andoni Iraola went from Bournemouth to Liverpool; Marco Rose replaced him. Oliver Glasner left Crystal Palace for Nottingham Forest , and Pierre Sage came the other way from France. Álvaro Arbeloa , who managed Real Madrid for part of last season, is at Fulham . Marco Silva left Fulham for Benfica , where he replaced Mourinho. Mourinho, of course, went to the Bernabéu, appointed on June 11 and confirmed as one of Florentino Pérez 's explicit election promises. Pérez was re-elected on June 7 with 64.79 per cent against the challenger Enrique Riquelme , whose ticket had promised Jürgen Klopp as coach and Raúl as sporting director. Klopp went somewhere else entirely: on July 24 he was appointed manager of Germany , taking over from Julian Nagelsmann on a contract to 2030 after Germany went out of their own generation's World Cup in the round of 32, beaten on penalties by Paraguay . His Red Bull contract contained an exit clause written for precisely this job. He has not yet taken charge of a competitive game. His first is on September 27. Italy changed almost as completely. Rúben Amorim is at Milan , Massimiliano Allegri at Napoli , Luciano Spalletti at Juventus , Gian Piero Gasperini at Roma , Maurizio Sarri at Atalanta , Gennaro Gattuso at Lazio , Cristian Chivu at Inter . Nine of the twenty Serie A clubs changed coach before a ball was kicked, and Fiorentina have already changed again. In France, Zinedine Zidane has succeeded Didier Deschamps as national coach, Filipe Luís has taken Monaco to the top of Ligue 1, and Davide Ancelotti has his first job in charge of a major club at Lille . What ties it together is the World Cup. A tournament that finished on July 19 compressed every pre-season in Europe, delayed the Premier League by a week and the Bundesliga by another, and gave clubs a natural moment to end things. The cost is being paid now, in September, by squads that had four weeks instead of eight and by managers being asked to install new ideas in players who have not stopped running since February. Read the tables in that light and the surprises look less like accidents. Transfer News The European windows shut on September 1. What follows is the reckoning: who spent, who was dismantled, and which threads are still live. Status: all official. The single largest reallocation of capital in this window happened in one club's engine room. Manchester City sold Rodri to Barcelona for £65m on August 18, having already lost Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid on a free and Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah for £52m. Then they rebuilt from scratch. Elliot Anderson arrived from Nottingham Forest for £116m. Ayyoub Bouaddi , 19, came from Lille for a reported £81.4m on August 26. And on September 1, with the window closing, City equalled the British transfer record by paying Chelsea £125m for Enzo Fernández . They also took Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for £65m, with Jack Grealish going the other way on loan as part of the arrangement. "The squad is complete," Enzo Maresca said afterwards, which is the sort of line a manager only gets to use once. Three league wins from three and a 2-0 in Porto suggest the money has landed. The open question is the one nobody at the club will discuss on the record: the 130 charges the Premier League brought in 2023 remain, on every reachable public record, unresolved. We could not confirm any hearing outcome, and we are not going to imply one. Newcastle Sold Their Spine and Still Ended Up Net Spenders Gordon, Tonali and Guimarães all went. £265.3m came back in. The club insists none of it was panic. On paper it reads like a distress sale. Newcastle United sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m on July 1, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham for £92.5m five days later, and Bruno Guimarães for £75m on August 8. Their manager of nearly five years, Eddie Howe , had resigned at the end of July. Three of their four best players and the man who built the side, gone inside six weeks. The arithmetic argues otherwise. Newcastle's outgoings totalled £236.8m and their incomings £265.3m. Nico González arrived from Manchester City for £47m, Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for £51m on deadline day, Bazoumana Touré from Hoffenheim for £42.8m, Aladji Bamba from Monaco for £34m, Amar Dedić from Benfica for £30.7m and Sean Steur from Ajax for £23m. That is not a club raising cash. That is a club changing its mind about what it wants to be. Sporting director Ross Wilson has said the summer was "not chaotic" and that the club had prepared for Howe's exit. Matthias Jaissle , appointed on August 5, has taken five points from three games: a 2-2 with Liverpool , a 2-0 win at Tottenham and a 2-2 at home to Bournemouth . Nobody we could reach has linked the sales to profit and sustainability rules, and we are not going to assert it. One correction worth making, because it circulates: Alexander Isak 's £125m move to Liverpool happened in September 2025. He is not part of this story. Liverpool Let Mohamed Salah Walk, and Sold a Third of Themselves A free transfer to Trabzonspor, a £106m replacement from Paris, and a new ownership consortium at Anfield. Mohamed Salah left Liverpool on May 24 with his contract expired, after announcing in March that he would go. He pursued Beşiktaş first; those talks collapsed over shirt revenue and agent commission. On August 6 he signed a two-year deal at Trabzonspor , wearing number 10 after being welcomed in 61, the city's area code. He scored twice in his second start. Nine years, and it ended on a technicality of contract law. Liverpool replaced him at the top of the market. Bradley Barcola arrived from Paris Saint-Germain on August 31 for a reported £106m plus £17m in add-ons on a five-year deal, joining Jérémy Jacquet from Rennes at £55m and Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna at £34.5m. Ibrahima Konaté left for Real Madrid on a free, Curtis Jones to Inter for £25.7m and Andy Robertson to Tottenham. Ronald Araújo came in on loan from Barcelona with a €55m option. The bigger change was upstairs. On August 14, Fenway Sports Group agreed to sell a 38 per cent stake to 1892 Holdings , a consortium led by Amit Bhatia and reported to include Jeff Bezos , Eduardo Saverin and the Mittal family, with FSG retaining 62 per cent. Bhatia, who becomes vice-chairman subject to regulatory approval, called being a Liverpool investor "the stuff of dreams". No valuation has been published, and Liverpool's own channels have carried nothing on the deal, so treat the percentage and the named investors as reported rather than club-confirmed. Barcelona Bought a Premier League Midfield and Registered All of It Rodri, Gordon, Adeyemi and a deadline-day Gabriel Jesus, with no registration scandal for the first time in three years. The most consequential detail of Barcelona 's summer is administrative. For the first time since 2023 they got to the first matchday with every signing registered and nobody stranded outside the squad. Rodri (£65m), Anthony Gordon (£69.3m) and Karim Adeyemi (€22m from Borussia Dortmund ) were all lodged with La Liga around August 21, and Gabriel Jesus , signed for roughly €10m plus €4m on deadline day, was registered immediately and played the same week. The room was created by selling. Ferran Torres went to Paris Saint-Germain for €48.5m, Robert Lewandowski left on a free for Chicago Fire , Ronald Araújo and Marc-André ter Stegen went out on loan to Liverpool and Ajax , and Ansu Fati joined Monaco for €11m. Three games later they had no points, one goal and nine conceded, their worst start since 1935-36, and Fabio Grosso had been sacked. The manner of it was ugly. La Nazione reports the separation is not amicable and could reach a courtroom. The counter-example is Atalanta , who sold Marco Palestra and Honest Ahanor to Chelsea and banked a net trading profit of roughly €97m. And the strangest deal in Europe belongs to Como : Real Madrid exercised a €9m buy-back on Nico Paz , then sold him straight back to Como for €60m payable over four years, retaining a large sell-on and an €80m buy-back option next summer. Paz has since scored in a 4-1 win at Genoa and will play in Como's first ever Champions League match on Thursday. MLS Broke Its Own Records, in Both Directions A $12.25m intraleague trade, a $23m teenage defender sold to Hull, and a deadline moved to September to match Europe. The MLS secondary window closed at midnight on September 2, a new date chosen specifically to align with the rest of the world, and it closed on the biggest cash-for-player trade in league history. St. Louis CITY paid the Colorado Rapids up to $12.25m for Rafael Navarro , the Brazilian designated player who had scored 44 goals in 114 appearances in Denver. Colorado retained a sell-on. Gabriel Martinelli is an Al-Hilal player . The 25-year-old Brazil winger completed a four-year deal in Saudi Arabia late on Thursday, September 4, for a guaranteed fee widely reported in the British press at £60m, which makes him the most expensive departure Arsenal have ever sanctioned. The timing looked strange and was not. The English window shut on September 1; UEFA's rules restrict European clubs from buying after their domestic deadline, not from selling. The Saudi Pro League window remained open. Arsenal therefore had three extra days in which a bid they were willing to accept could arrive, and it did. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and explained Wednesday, September 2, 2026 · The Deadline Week Edition In this edition The Lead · Messi Steps Away · The Boardroom War · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The night the window broke its own record, then broke its word English clubs spent 3.46 billion pounds and sent a British record fee across Manchester. Then, in the two hours after the 11pm buzzer, two agreed deals fell apart and left Chelsea, Everton and Monaco staring at each other across the wreckage. T he 2026 summer window did not so much close as buckle. By the time the Premier League's 11pm deadline passed on Tuesday night, English clubs had committed a record 3.46 billion pounds in gross spending, comfortably beating the previous high of 3.14bn, with 475m of it transacted on the final day alone. The figures come from FootballTransfers founder Paul Macdonald , supplied to BBC Sport. They describe a market with no ceiling, only a clock. The headline act was a 200-mile move that felt like a defection. Enzo Fernandez left Chelsea for Manchester City for 125 million pounds , equalling the British record set twelve months earlier when Liverpool paid the same for Alexander Isak. Sky Sports and ESPN both reported a five-year contract. The Argentine had told Chelsea he wanted to go more than three months ago; the club set a bid deadline a fortnight out and held to it. Chelsea banked an 18m profit on the 107m they gave Benfica three and a half years ago, a modest return on a player of that stature and a sign of how completely the Stamford Bridge trading model now governs football decisions. There is a symmetry to where he landed. Enzo Maresca , Fernandez's head coach at Chelsea for a year and a half until December 2025, is now in the City dugout, appointed on 29 June to replace Pep Guardiola after a decade and costing around 17m in compensation. He inherits the two domestic cups, the most expensive midfield reconstruction in the sport's history, and two wins from two. Key Facts Manchester City rebuilt a midfield from scratch Out this summer: Rodri to Barcelona, Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid on a free, Tijjani Reijnders In: Enzo Fernandez 125m, Elliot Anderson 116m, Ayyoub Bouaddi 86m Combined outlay on those three: 327m pounds Club-record gross spend for the window: 458m pounds , net 154m Sources: Sky Sports, ESPN, FootballTransfers via BBC Sport And then the deadline passed, and the evening turned strange. Chelsea had spent the day executing a plan: sell Fernandez, replace him with Lamine Camara of Monaco for 47m. Sky's Kaveh Solhekol , who drove the coverage, reported that the agreement was written, signed and subject only to a medical, with a six-year contract waiting and the player booked to fly into London. Monaco had been willing to sell a first-team midfielder because they believed they were about to receive 40m from Everton for Folarin Balogun . That Balogun deal wobbled. The striker travelled to Merseyside and something in the medical gave Everton's doctors pause. Reporting from RMC Sport and Get French Football News described a failed medical; Monaco and the player's camp insisted he was fit, having played through the World Cup with a minor problem. Everton went back and renegotiated the terms. Monaco, suddenly comfortable again that the money was coming, informed Chelsea in writing that they were withdrawing from the Camara agreement . That notification arrived after 11pm. “Everything was done, written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London.” Kaveh Solhekol, Sky Sports, on Chelsea's collapsed move for Lamine Camara Then came the last turn of the screw. Shortly after midnight, with the deal sheets still running and Everton believing they had their striker, Balogun changed his mind and pulled out. Everton were described in Sky's reporting as stunned. So Monaco kept both players, Chelsea got neither, and Everton, having already sold Beto to Fiorentina for 15.4m, went to bed with Thierno Barry as their only recognised centre-forward. The detail that matters most is what Chelsea did next, which was nothing. They held a contractual option to cancel the Fernandez sale if the replacement fell through. They chose not to use it. Sky reported the club described Monaco's conduct as extraordinary and deeply unprofessional, and honoured their side anyway. It will be relitigated every time Chelsea's midfield looks light between now and January, and it has left a live grudge between two clubs who must talk again in four months. Zoom out and the window's shape is clear enough. The money moved toward two poles: Manchester City rebuilding for a new manager, and Liverpool spending 123m on Bradley Barcola to replace a departed Mohamed Salah . Four of the five largest transfers in Premier League history were completed in this single window. Tottenham spent 302m and have started the season with two defeats, no goals and bottom place. Ipswich Town , promoted in May, spent 171m. This is the first window run under the league's new Squad Cost Ratio regime, which replaced PSR in November on a 14 to 6 vote and caps squad spending at 85 per cent of revenue with a six-point deduction waiting at the red threshold. The first assessment checkpoint arrives in October. Somebody is going to fail it. What the numbers cannot capture is the sense that the deadline has stopped functioning as a deadline. Deal sheets extended completions by two hours. A signed agreement was torn up after the buzzer with no consequence. A player who had passed a medical walked away at half past midnight. The transfer window is supposed to be the one moment in football where the paperwork binds. On Tuesday night it was a suggestion. Messi closes the international book, and then scores four Six weeks after losing a World Cup final, Argentina's most capped player and record scorer said goodbye to the shirt. Two days earlier he had produced the best individual night of his MLS career. On Monday, Lionel Messi announced on Instagram that he had played his last match for Argentina . He is 39. The statement was drafted on 21 July, two days after the World Cup final, and he said the death of his father Jorge on 8 August made him more certain of it. He leaves with 207 caps and 125 goals, both national records, alongside the 2022 World Cup, the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and Olympic gold from 2008. He also holds the World Cup records for appearances, 34, and assists, 12, and is the oldest outfield player ever to start a final. The timing is worth sitting with. Argentina lost the final in New Jersey to Spain , 1-0 after extra time, to a goal from Ferran Torres . Messi finished as the tournament's second-highest scorer and made the Best XI. There was no decline to point at and no injury to blame. He decided a sixth World Cup was the end of the road and closed it himself rather than waiting to be closed out. A 2028 Copa America appearance has not been formally ruled out, but nothing in the statement invited that reading. Club football, meanwhile, is going rather well. On Saturday night Inter Miami beat CF Montreal 7-1, a club record for goals in a match, and Messi scored four of them and assisted a fifth . Two were direct free kicks. It took him to 927 career goals, to 74 free-kick goals, third all-time, and to 98 for Inter Miami. He is the 19th player in MLS history to score four in a game, and reached 20 multi-goal MLS matches in 72 appearances, faster than anyone before him. The win also ended a five-game winless run, which was the actual point of the evening. He now leads the Golden Boot race on 18 goals and 10 assists, and is chasing a third straight MVP. UEFA moves to prosecute the FIFA president A plan to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial arm to private investors has been withdrawn. The war it started has not been. The most consequential football story of the week involves no players. FIFA proposed creating a private commercial vehicle, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to run World Cup commercial operations, and selling a 21 per cent minority stake at a 20 billion dollar valuation to raise roughly 4.2bn. The lead investor was to be Thrive Capital, run by Joshua Kushner , with JP Morgan involved. Member associations were offered 40m dollars each over four years to approve it, on a 53-day deadline. All 55 UEFA members rejected it unanimously and threatened to withdraw European teams from every FIFA competition, which put the Women's Under-20 World Cup in September, the Under-17 tournament in October and the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil directly at risk. Concacaf's 41 nations also refused, citing the artificially short deadline and the absence of any review. FIFA folded. On 27 August, UEFA published a statement from its national association representatives confirming that FIFA had committed in writing to withdrawing the scheme irrevocably and permanently, and that the boycott threat was suspended. The same statement called the affair a profound failure of judgement and an abuse of presidential power, said the trust required to hold the FIFA presidency has been broken and cannot be restored, and committed the signatories to backing alternative candidates should Gianni Infantino seek re-election. Sky Sports reported the same day that UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings against Infantino in Switzerland for criminal mismanagement under Article 158, and has filed in the Southern District of New York to subpoena FIFA and its banks. Gabriel Martinelli is bound for Riyadh in the biggest sale the club has ever made. Julian Alvarez is still not an Arsenal player. With hours left in the window, the champions look leaner, considerably richer, and unbeaten. T here is a version of this deadline day in which Arsenal look like a club in retreat. Two forwards gone in twenty-four hours. A first-choice target who never wanted to come. A late alternative lost to Sunderland over a few million pounds. Read the outgoing column alone and you would guess the champions were dismantling something. The table says otherwise. Arsenal have played three competitive matches since lifting the title in May. They have won all three, scored seven, and conceded none. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in Cardiff, Coventry City 3-0 at home, and Aston Villa 1-0 at Villa Park on Monday night without ever looking troubled. That is the context for everything Andrea Berta has done this summer. Arsenal did not need to buy from a position of weakness, and they have not. Bruno Guimaraes arrived from Newcastle United for £75m on August 9 . Ezri Konsa followed from Aston Villa for £55m on August 21 . Neither was a panic buy. The selling has been just as deliberate, and rather more brutal. Gabriel Jesus completed his move to Barcelona for £8.6m after four years, 123 appearances and 32 goals. He took a pay cut to go. Gabriel Martinelli is on his way to Al-Hilal for a fee that will comfortably break the club's record for a sale. Key Facts: Deadline Day Window closes: 11pm BST Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. The women's window runs until 11pm BST on Thursday, September 3. Confirmed today: Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Fabio Vieira to Hamburg . Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan. Agreed, awaiting announcement: Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal . Unresolved at press time: Julian Alvarez. Gone elsewhere: Malick Fofana, to Sunderland . Two departures of that size would normally be balanced by a marquee arrival. That is where the summer has stalled. Julian Alvarez has been the target since the spring, and the pursuit has never once looked comfortable. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona , the club the player actually wants. Arsenal have spent weeks trying to be a destination rather than a fallback. Sky Sports reported on Friday that Atletico had set the player a deadline to commit or engage. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said publicly that Alvarez was "really struggling" and that "there were people who misled him, who left him confused." Not the language of a club expecting a clean resolution. "We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell. We have to be very careful, because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them." Mikel Arteta, August 30 Deadline Day Churn The reporting since has pulled hard in both directions, which is what deadline day does to a story. Spanish outlets suggested on Tuesday morning that Arsenal had stepped back and were assessing alternatives . Hours later, TEAMtalk and the Evening Standard were reporting the opposite: a green light at roughly £130m, a willingness to write a future Barcelona release into the contract, and help relocating the player's family. Treat that second version carefully. It is single-sourced, it is not carried by David Ornstein or Fabrizio Romano , and it arrived precisely when deadline-day traffic peaks. What is solid is Romano 's line that Barcelona now consider their incoming business closed after signing Jesus , and will not activate the €100m bid president Joan Laporta confirmed was still live. Which leaves Arteta where he has been all summer: with Kai Havertz fit and scoring, Viktor Gyokeres unused, and a squad that has not yet needed rescuing. He was blunt on Monday night. "We are trying to improve the squad, and until tomorrow night we're going to try to do that." He also warned against selling for the sake of it. The honest reading is that this window has been a success in structure and a frustration in ambition. Arsenal have upgraded midfield and defence, cleared £80m or more of wages and fees from players who were not going to start, and kept their powder dry on a striker they were never going to get cheaply. Whether that reads as discipline or as a missed opportunity depends entirely on what Havertz 's hamstrings do between now and January. Transfer News Martinelli to Al-Hilal: the Biggest Sale in Arsenal's History Seven seasons, 278 appearances, 62 goals, and a fee that pushes past Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's 2017 departure. Gabriel Martinelli has been left out of Arsenal matchday squads since the season began, which is usually its own kind of announcement. He is 25. He arrived as a teenager from Ituano and leaves as a Premier League champion. The fee has climbed as the week has gone on. Daily Cannon reported a verbally agreed £56.5m on Saturday. By Sunday, David Ornstein was reporting a €70m fixed fee , up from an earlier structure of €58m plus €8m in add-ons. James Benge reported that the two clubs had been working through a sell-on clause. At any of those numbers it is a club record for an outgoing transfer, comfortably clear of the £40m Liverpool paid for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain nine years ago. Gabriel Jesus Joins Barcelona, and Takes a Pay Cut to Do It A four-year Arsenal career that never quite recovered from a knee injury ends for £8.6m and a three-year deal in Catalonia. Gabriel Jesus arrived from Manchester City in 2022 for £45m and changed the mood around the club almost immediately. He leaves having started three Premier League matches last season, his campaign wrecked by the knee injury he suffered in the FA Cup in January 2025. Barcelona paid €10m, around £8.6m, on a contract running to June 2029. Jesus has since confirmed he reduced his salary to make the move happen. He consulted Raphinha , Joao Cancelo , Rodri and Eric Garcia before deciding. "I have the opportunity now to be here at Barca," he said on arrival. "It's a dream for me." He finishes with 123 appearances and 32 goals for Arsenal , plus a title medal he did much of the early work for. There is a strategic footnote. Romano reported that signing Jesus is what closed Barcelona 's incoming market and killed any late move for Alvarez . In selling a squad striker cheaply, Arsenal may have removed their own competition for a better one. Certainty tier: official. Announced by both clubs on September 1. Fofana Slips Away on a Question of Structure Personal terms agreed, structure not. Sunderland moved, Crystal Palace counter-moved, and the Belgian ended up doing his medical in France without knowing who for. Arsenal 's late look at Malick Fofana was first reported on Sunday night by the Evening Standard's Matt Verri . The 21-year-old Lyon winger fits an obvious hole: pace and directness from the left, which the champions have lacked since Martinelli stopped playing. According to Ornstein , Arsenal got as far as agreeing personal terms before refusing to meet Lyon 's €40m valuation. Romano added the detail that mattered: Arsenal only ever wanted a loan or a loan with an obligation, not a permanent purchase at that price. Sunderland had no such reservations and agreed roughly €30m plus add-ons, with a five-year contract to 2031. Crystal Palace then matched the package and tried to win the player on personal terms. What followed was the most deadline-day scene of the day. Two private jets waited at Lyon airport, one bound for the north east and one for London. French journalist Romain Molina reported that Fofana completed his medical in France while still deciding where he was going. He went to Sunderland . Certainty tier: dead for Arsenal . Confirmed independently by Ornstein and Romano . Nwaneri Goes to Dortmund, and the Reason Is Eze A season-long loan with a recall option for the 19-year-old, after a Marseille spell that fell apart through no fault of his own. Ethan Nwaneri flew to Germany on Tuesday morning and completed a season-long loan to Borussia Dortmund . He remains under contract at Arsenal until 2030, and the deal carries a recall option. The reasoning is straightforward and slightly sad. The arrival of Eberechi Eze pushed him down a pecking order that already contained Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Mikel Merino . Club and player agreed he needed regular football. His January loan to Marseille was undone almost immediately when Roberto De Zerbi was dismissed shortly after he arrived. Dortmund is a better bet: they have an excellent record with young attackers, and they moved after losing Giannis Konstantelias to an ACL injury. A neat detail: Nwaneri scored against Dortmund in Arsenal 's 3-2 pre-season defeat, which is reported to have sharpened their interest. Certainty tier: official. This has been the most aggressive summer Arsenal 's women's team has had in years, and it needed to be. Renee Slegers won the WSL last season with 51 points from 22 games, lost one match all campaign, and won the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup by beating Corinthians 3-2 in February. She is dropping between the centre-backs in build-up with Kim Little ahead of her as a shield, a 3-1-6 shape that takes progression duties off Little and Mariona and adds a genuine long diagonal passer. Labor Day lands on Monday September 7. Before it, the Dons play twice at Negoesco and Bay FC host Kansas City under lights in San Jose. After it, the calendar barely pauses. September is the month the city stops pretending it is summer and gets on with it. Twelve pianos go into the Botanical Garden for eleven days from September 10. The San Francisco Opera plays a free afternoon on the grass on September 13. Grant Avenue closes for the Autumn Moon Festival, Haight Street closes for its street fair, and Folsom Street closes for a fair that needs no introduction. The sport is unusually good right now. The Valkyries have clinched a playoff spot at 28-11 and close the regular season with two home nights at Chase Center. The Giants have not, and their final homestand against the Dodgers is the last baseball at Oracle until spring. The Earthquakes take their annual trip to Levi's Stadium on September 19. Then the window closes on the best free weekend of the year. Hardly Strictly Bluegrass runs October 2 to 4 in Golden Gate Park, and the night before it, the Masonic hosts a one-off tribute to Steve Earle with Emmylou Harris, Jackson Browne and Gillian Welch. Plan the first weekend of October now. The weekend read The National Weather Service has San Francisco holding steady in the mid-60s all week: partly sunny and 65 on Monday, up to 67 on Tuesday, and mostly sunny and 66 by Friday. The only wet note in the forecast is a slight chance of showers on Friday night. Saturday September 5 comes back mostly sunny and 67, which is close to ideal for the first Saturday of a long weekend. Sunday September 6 sits past the current forecast horizon, so treat it as unknown rather than assured. For Candlestick Point, Mount Diablo or anything in Golden Gate Park, the risk this week is wind and afternoon fog rather than rain. The act-now clock Now Portola passes are on sale for September 26 and 27. Two-day general admission starts at $399.95 and single days at $269.95, both direct from the festival with no added fees. Last chance Sunday September 27 is the Giants' final home game of 2026. There is no baseball at Oracle Park after that until spring. Pick of the Month Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Friday October 2 to Sunday October 4, 2026 · Hellman Hollow, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco · Free. No tickets, no wristbands, no queue. The defensible reason is the simplest one available: it is the largest free music festival in the country, it is in our park, and it is free because a San Francisco financier endowed it to stay that way in perpetuity. Warren Hellman died in 2011. The festival has not charged a cent since, and roughly 750,000 people turn up across the three days. The 2026 bill has now had three announcement rounds. Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, My Morning Jacket, Alison Krauss, Sierra Hull, Old Crow Medicine Show, Hiss Golden Messenger, Kathleen Edwards, Yasmin Williams with William Tyler, AJ Lee and Blue Summit, El Khat and Tyler Ballgame are all confirmed, with more still to come. What tips it from very good to unmissable this year is the night before. On Thursday October 1 the Masonic hosts An Evening Honoring Steve Earle, with Emmylou Harris, Jackson Browne, Hot Tuna, Gillian Welch and David Rawlings, Molly Tuttle, Buddy Miller, Larry Campbell and Teresa Williams and others, benefiting Sweetwater Spectrum. That lineup will not assemble again. Practical advice: do not drive. The N Judah, the 5 Fulton and the 7 all serve the park and all of them will be full. Go in on foot from the east end, bring a layer for when the fog comes in around four, and wear boots if there has been rain, because Hellman Hollow turns to mud faster than you would think. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and weighed Edition No. 1 · Wednesday, August 26, 2026 Deadline week In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Six days left, and the money has not stopped moving The summer window shuts on Tuesday. A World Cup pushed every European calendar back, so for the first time in years the most expensive week of the football year is being played out with the league tables already on the wall. T he transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1, at 23:00 in England and just before midnight on the continent. Major League Soccer follows a day later, on September 2. That is the ordinary rhythm of a European summer. What is not ordinary is where the season sits when the whistle goes on it. The World Cup finished on July 19 at MetLife Stadium, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time through Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, with Enzo Fernandez and Leandro Paredes both sent off. Every domestic calendar in Europe slid back to accommodate it. The Premier League did not start until August 22. The Bundesliga has not started at all: matchday one is Friday. So clubs are now conducting the single most consequential week of their financial year with points already on the board and, in several cases, with a crisis already in the building. The Deadline Board Ten deals that could still land before Tuesday, and how far each has actually travelled. Omar Marmoush Man City to Tottenham Medical Liam Delap Chelsea to Nottingham Forest Medical El Hadji Malick Diouf West Ham to Brentford Medical Bradley Barcola PSG to Liverpool Advanced talks Nicolas Jackson Chelsea to Aston Villa Advanced talks Moise Kean Fiorentina to Como Terms agreed, fee open Ollie Watkins Aston Villa to Al-Hilal Four bids rejected Rafael Leao Milan to Aston Villa Talks, no fee agreed Enzo Fernandez Chelsea to Man City No formal bid yet Julian Alvarez Atletico Madrid, exit sought Club refusing to sell Status as reported on the morning of August 26. Sourcing for each item appears in the write-ups below. One morning, one teenager Consider Wednesday morning as a single data point. Manchester City confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi , 18, from Lille . Sky Sports reported the structure as £81.3m guaranteed with £4.3m in add-ons, a total of roughly £86m; Lille announced it in euros at £100m equivalent, or a shade under. Whichever currency you prefer, it is the most expensive teenager in Premier League history, comfortably past the £58.9m Manchester United paid for Leny Yoro in 2024. Lille, for their part, called it the largest sale a Ligue 1 club has ever made to a foreign buyer, beating the €80m Nicolas Pepe fetched in 2018. Bouaddi is worth pausing on. He made his European debut at 16 years and three days, a competition record, and became the youngest player of the century in Ligue 1 at 16 years and 20 days. He had 96 senior appearances for Lille before his 19th birthday and started five of Morocco's six matches at the World Cup. In his farewell message he wrote that Lille is “where I grew up, where I learned, and where I experienced my first emotions at the highest level.” City are buying a succession plan, not a squad player. They need one. This is the first City summer without Pep Guardiola , who was replaced on June 29 by Enzo Maresca on a three-year deal. Since then City have sold Rodri to Barcelona for €76.5m, Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah , Savio to Tottenham for £85m and let Bernardo Silva and John Stones go for nothing. Marmoush is at a medical at Spurs, Nico Gonzalez is expected at Newcastle , and Jack Grealish is still unresolved. Money in the other direction has gone on youth: £116m to Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson , now £86m to Lille for a teenager. Maresca was asked on Sunday whether more was coming. “We will see, it's eight days to go,” he said. “For sure something is going to happen.” “I would give that an 85 to 90 per cent chance. I think that's gonna happen. I don't think Liverpool would've come this far to walk away from it.” David Ornstein on Bradley Barcola, The Athletic FC Podcast, August 25 Selling as a strategy The second thing this window has confirmed is that selling well is now a strategy rather than an admission of defeat. Chelsea are the purest expression of it. On Tuesday they agreed to send Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest for £45m rising to £50m, a Forest club record, with the medical set for Wednesday. Delap scored three goals in 47 Chelsea appearances. Chelsea paid Ipswich Town £30m for him a year ago. That is a profit of roughly £20m on a player who did not work out, and it is not an accident. In the same seven days Chelsea loaned Benoit Badiashile to Napoli with a purchase option, sold Omari Kellyman to Strasbourg for around €6m, and moved close to selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa . Santi Aouna of Foot Mercato reported on Wednesday that the clubs are near an agreement but that Jackson has not yet approved it. Meanwhile Chelsea are the ones saying no: Manchester City want Enzo Fernandez , valued at roughly £120m, and as of Tuesday had not submitted a formal offer. Xabi Alonso , four days into his Chelsea tenure, was careful about it. “My wish is that we know what will happen for the future,” he said, “but we will see this week.” Newcastle have run the same play at a larger scale, banking more than £240m in sales including Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m, then spending it across five signings. Tottenham have gone past £300m under Roberto De Zerbi . And on the opening Saturday Tottenham lost 3-0 at Brentford , their joint-heaviest opening-day defeat in Premier League history, conceding 5.63 expected goals. De Zerbi did not hide behind the scoreline. “Our physical condition was not at the right level for all players,” he said, “because many came later after the World Cup.” Spending is not the same as a team, and this summer has left almost nobody time to build one. There is a counterweight, and it is Italy. Juventus lost Dusan Vlahovic for nothing this month when his contract expired and he signed for Besiktas . Asked about the market after his side's opening win at Frosinone , Luciano Spalletti shrugged: “potremmo anche rimanere cosi,” we could even stay as we are. He also conceded that without Champions League football, everyone is available. Calcio e Finanza marked the season's start with a blunt accounting: Serie A's domestic television deal is worth about €900m a season against a €1.2bn target, and of the dozen or so clubs on earth who can spend €100m on a single player, not one of them is Italian. The players stop waiting Which brings us to the third and least comfortable feature of the week: the players have stopped waiting politely. Moise Kean arrived late at Fiorentina's training ground on Wednesday, refused to train with the squad and was fined. Julian Alvarez did not turn up to Atletico Madrid training at all, the club citing indisposition, three days after being whistled by his own supporters. Rafael Leao is training away from the Milan group despite being fit. Ousmane Dembele has been given a week off by PSG that RMC's Daniel Riolo flatly called a punishment. Ollie Watkins has turned down a new Villa contract and made clear he would take the Saudi offer. Five clubs, five different countries, one common cause: a window this short, arriving this late, hands leverage to whoever is willing to make a scene. Six days remain. The tell to watch is not the biggest name but the first domino: if Chelsea blink on Enzo Fernandez, City will have spent north of £200m in a fortnight and Chelsea will have another nine-figure sum to reinvest in January. If they hold, this becomes a window remembered for teenagers rather than superstars. Either way, Tuesday night will be busy. Signed and Sealed The five biggest fees officially confirmed between August 19 and August 26, in millions of pounds. Ayyoub Bouaddi Lille to Man City 86 Savio Man City to Tottenham 85 Carlos Baleba Brighton to Man Utd 70 Liam Delap Chelsea to Nottingham Forest 50 Curtis Jones Liverpool to Inter 30 Guaranteed fees as reported, rounded, add-ons excluded except where a maximum has been agreed. Delap is £45m rising to £50m. Bouaddi's total includes £4.3m of add-ons on an £81.3m base. Secondary Feature Nine new managers, and a record that had stood for eighty years Almost half the Premier League changed its head coach this summer. Opta had to go back to 1946 to find anything comparable. Nine of the twenty Premier League clubs began the season with a manager taking charge of his first league game for them. Opta's line, carried by Sky Sports, is that this is the most in an English top-flight season since 1946-47. Serie A very nearly matched it: nine of that league's twenty benches also changed hands, four of them going to men who had never managed in Italy before. The English list reads like a reshuffle of the entire coaching class. Enzo Maresca left Chelsea for Manchester City to replace Pep Guardiola . Xabi Alonso took the Chelsea job Maresca vacated. Andoni Iraola left Bournemouth for Liverpool in succession to Arne Slot , and Marco Rose took the Bournemouth job. Matthias Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle on August 5, the latest appointment of the nine. Oliver Glasner moved from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest , with Pierre Sage taking over at Selhurst Park. Alvaro Arbeloa has Fulham after Marco Silva 's departure on June 2, and Gary O'Neil has promoted Ipswich Town . Opening weekend split them neatly. Maresca won on debut, and did it by playing a centre-back in midfield: Marc Guehi scored the 85th-minute equaliser against Bournemouth before Josko Gvardiol won it in stoppage time. “I know Marc from Palace and I always thought he could play as a midfielder because he is very good,” Maresca said. Alonso won too, 3-2 at Fulham , though his goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was at fault for both home goals. “It's a process. It's day one,” Alonso offered. The others got a harder education. Iraola needed a penalty deep into stoppage time from Dominik Szoboszlai to draw 2-2 at Newcastle, where Jaissle, twenty days into the job, had led 2-1. “Hard luck, I would say,” Jaissle said. “I'm really, really happy with the performance after such a short amount of time.” Glasner lost at home to Leeds United to an 88th-minute Anton Stach free-kick, then lost to Leeds again three days later in the Carabao Cup, the only Premier League club knocked out in round two. Sage lost at Everton . Rose lost at City. Arbeloa lost and sounded delighted anyway: “If we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.” Only O'Neil, among the newcomers at a promoted club, took three points, courtesy of a 90th-minute Jack Clarke winner against Sunderland . The structural point underneath the churn is that all nine are managing squads they did not assemble, in a window that does not shut until Tuesday, having had a pre-season shortened at both ends by a World Cup. De Zerbi named three of his own players as physically unready after the Brentford defeat. Maurizio Sarri , one of Serie A's new arrivals at Atalanta , made the same complaint in gentler language: “De Ketelaere arrived on August 4, and the new signings arrived recently too.” Judgements formed in the next three weeks will be formed on incomplete evidence. They will be formed anyway. Transfer News Tottenham have spent past £300m. On Saturday they were beaten 3-0 by Brentford. Savio arrived for a Manchester City club-record sale, Marmoush is at a medical, and the squad that took the field on opening day conceded four first-half goals' worth of chances. Tottenham confirmed the signing of Savio on Monday: £75m plus £10m in add-ons, of which around £5m is effectively guaranteed. At £85m it is the largest fee Manchester City have ever received for a player, past the £82m Julian Alvarez brought from Atletico. Omar Marmoush , 27, is following him, on loan with a £60m obligation to buy, with a medical booked as of Wednesday morning per PA and Sky. City will recoup roughly the £59m they paid Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025. Those two follow Sandro Tonali from Newcastle at a club-record fee, Mateus Fernandes from West Ham at £85m, Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton at £52m, and free transfers for Andy Robertson , Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka . On the reported Tonali figure the sources diverge, Sky carrying £100m and Football365 £92.5m, so treat the exact number with care. The direction of travel is not in doubt. Against all that, Saturday at the Gtech was chastening. Brentford's 3-0 was their largest top-flight win and Tottenham's joint-heaviest opening-day defeat, matching a 3-0 at Manchester United in 2011-12. Archie Gray , at 20 years and 163 days, became the club's youngest Premier League captain, breaking Harry Kane 's record. Spurs are still trying to sell. Lucas Bergvall has submitted a transfer request with Newcastle's £46m bid rejected and Spurs holding out for close to £60m, and David Ornstein reports the move now looks unlikely. Pape Matar Sarr and Richarlison are both available, the latter at £35m, which Everton consider too much. Manchester United paid £70m for Carlos Baleba, then lost at Hull Michael Carrick has his midfielder. He says he still needs a left-back, and he is running out of days to find one. Manchester United completed the signing of Carlos Baleba , 22, from Brighton on Tuesday for £65m guaranteed plus £5m in add-ons, on a five-year deal with a further year's option. There is a footnote worth noting: Lille , who sold Baleba to Brighton in 2023, collect roughly €10m from a resale clause that sporting director Olivier Letang inserted at the time. Lille have therefore banked around €110m in a single week from two players they no longer own. Carrick is not finished. “We want more, we need more,” he told Sky Sports. Left-back is the stated priority. United enquired about Lewis Hall and Newcastle refused to sell; Antonee Robinson of Fulham is under consideration. Harry Amass is expected to leave before September 1. No forward is expected, because Marcus Rashford has returned from Barcelona and made his first competitive United appearance in 618 days as a substitute at Hull. That appearance came in a 2-0 defeat at newly promoted Hull City , Semi Ajayi heading in on 17 minutes and Nobel Mendy scoring on his Premier League debut on 38. “We are bitterly disappointed with the result today,” Carrick said. “But it won't knock us.” His captain was less diplomatic. “Same mistakes as we did last season,” Bruno Fernandes said. “Every away game we give too much of the ball to them.” Serie A's late window is being run by the players Moise Kean refused to train. Rafael Leao is working alone. Christopher Nkunku went home to Leipzig. Italy's deadline week has turned personal. Moise Kean , 26, wants to join Como . Como have bid €35m plus €5m in bonuses and asked for an answer inside 48 hours. Personal terms of around €5m a year, roughly matching what he earns now, are understood to be agreed. On Wednesday, La Nazione reported, Kean arrived late at the Viola Park, declined to train with the group, left before his teammates and did a solo session. He was fined and threatened with further sanctions. Fiorentina 's position, stated publicly, is that the club “is solid, it has no need to sell any player.” Director Fabio Paratici set the conditions plainly: “Our players are for sale only if they ask, if a suitable offer arrives, and if we find an equal or better replacement.” At Milan , Rafael Leao is training separately from the squad with no injury to explain it. Corriere dello Sport reports he is outside Ruben Amorim 's project and that Aston Villa are pushing, with Milan asking €50m to €60m and Villa negotiating below it. Galatasaray are also involved. Leao is said to have turned down a large Al-Hilal proposal, preferring to stay in Europe. Amorim would not be drawn: “Right now the good of the team matters far more to us.” Milan did move one attacker on. Christopher Nkunku , 28, returned to RB Leipzig on loan with a purchase option on August 25, back at the club where he scored 126 direct goal involvements in 172 games and won two DFB-Pokals. “When the opportunity to join RB Leipzig came up, I wanted to seize it,” he said. “I'm top fit and eager to help the team immediately.” Elsewhere: Atalanta have had two bids for Bologna 's Jonathan Rowe rejected, the second worth €35m plus bonuses, which would be a club-record signing if it landed; Franck Kessie is in advanced talks with Juventus, who hold his preference, though Roma met his agent on Tuesday to try to intervene; and Napoli have offered €15m to €16m for Chelsea's Marc Guiu against a £25m equivalent asking price. Atletico Madrid say Julian Alvarez is not for sale. Julian Alvarez did not come to training. Whistled by his own supporters on Sunday, absent on Wednesday, and holding an understanding with Barcelona that his club will not honour. The sequence matters. On Sunday Julian Alvarez came off the bench in Atletico Madrid 's 2-2 draw with Villarreal , his first appearance at the Metropolitano in more than three months, and was whistled by sections of his own crowd. At full time he walked down the tunnel rather than join the squad in saluting the supporters. On Wednesday morning he did not appear at training. The club's stated reason was indisposition. Infobae and El Espanol both reported it as an escalation rather than an illness. The underlying position is that Alvarez has had an understanding with Barcelona since May and that Atletico will not sell to a domestic rival. Matteo Moretto of Relevo, speaking on August 21, said Barcelona now regard the deal as “basically impossible” and that the club's plan is a cheaper attacker of similar profile with a view to revisiting Alvarez in a year. A Premier League bid, from Arsenal , has been reported at up to €150m; the player is said to be reluctant to return to England. His release clause is €500m. Atletico's public line has not moved: he is not being sold. Atletico have otherwise had an eventful summer under new ownership. Apollo Sports Capital completed a majority takeover in March, taking 55 per cent at a valuation of €2.5bn including debt, adding a €100m capital increase for the Ciudad del Deporte project and expanding the board from five members to eleven. Enrique Cerezo and Miguel Angel Gil Marin remain in place through June 2029 under a lock-up, and David Villa has joined the board. On the pitch, Cristian Romero arrived from Tottenham for around €40m and Diego Simeone , whose contract runs to June 2027, has four points from two matches.
