Around the Leagues England: Premier League One round played, and it was a strange one. Two of the three promoted clubs won: Hull City beat Manchester United 2-0 in front of 24,470 at the MKM Stadium in their first top-flight game since 2017, and Ipswich Town beat Sunderland 2-1 through Emersonn and a 90th-minute Jack Clarke strike. Coventry City , back in the top division after 25 years under Frank Lampard , lost 3-0 away. The heaviest defeat of the weekend went to a club that finished fourth last season: Aston Villa lost 4-0 at Brighton , conceding all four inside the first half and losing Joao Gomes to a red card on 40 minutes for kicking out at Georginio Rutter . He faces a three-match ban. Opta noted that only one other side in Premier League history has conceded four, taken a red card and scored an own goal in a single first half: Southampton, in the 9-0 against Manchester United in February 2021. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in 79 seconds for Brighton and has four goals in his last four home league games, one more than in the previous 26 at the Amex. Lewis Dunk made his 300th Premier League appearance for the club, the first player to reach it. Elsewhere Manchester City beat Bournemouth 2-1 with late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol , both created by Rayan Cherki ; Everton won their first opening weekend in five years, 2-0 over Crystal Palace ; and Chelsea won 3-2 at Fulham , Joao Pedro scoring after 31 seconds and Morgan Rogers marking his debut. The week's refereeing row came at St James' Park, where Stuart Attwell gave a stoppage-time penalty for Lewis Hall 's challenge on Victor Munoz and VAR confirmed it. The Premier League's Match Centre published its reasoning verbatim: Hall “doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact.” Newcastle, 2-1 up, drew 2-2. Off the pitch Off the pitch, two structural stories. First, Profit and Sustainability Rules are gone. From this season clubs are governed by a Squad Cost Ratio capping on-pitch spending, wages, head-coach salary, agent fees and transfer amortisation, at 85 per cent of football revenue, with a Red Threshold at 115 per cent. Breaches between the two trigger financial levies; above the Red Threshold the penalty is a six-point deduction rising by a point for every £6.5m of overspend. A separate Sustainability and Systemic Resilience regime adds working capital, liquidity and positive equity tests. Second, Liverpool 's owners FSG sold a minority stake in mid-August to a consortium led by Amit Bhatia and including Jeff Bezos , reported at around 38 per cent on a valuation near $7bn with an option to take control at roughly $8bn within twelve months. FSG's statement was categorical: it “continues to retain majority ownership and operational control.” Sky reported the investment brings no separate transfer budget. Also of note: the Women's Super League expands from 12 clubs to 14 this season, starting September 4, with Sky showing 163 matches live. Spain: La Liga Spain's opening rounds have been played out of order. Matchday one was spread from August 15 to August 27 because clubs with World Cup semi-finalists were given extra rest, so several sides have played matchday two before matchday one. The consequence is a table that will look nothing like itself by Friday. It is also, briefly, a table topped by Sevilla , who have six points from two and are top of La Liga for the first time in 189 matchdays, since the second round of 2021-22. Matias Almeyda 's side beat Rayo Vallecano 2-1 with a 97th-minute penalty, then won 3-1 at San Mames against a ten-man Athletic Club , who are bottom with nothing. That Athletic red card produced the week's cleanest institutional story. On the debut edition of the referees' committee's new review programme, the CTA ruled that Cesar Soto Grado 's 11th-minute dismissal of Yuri Berchiche was a “clear and obvious error” and that VAR should have intervened. The committee's reasoning was that Sevilla's Miguel Sierra pushed the ball away from himself, so there was no genuine goalscoring opportunity. The correct decision was a free kick and no card. Four other reviewed decisions from the round were upheld. Mourinho, and a Madrid without limits Real Madrid are being managed by Jose Mourinho , appointed on June 11 on a contract to June 2029. He won his league return 2-1 at Espanyol through a 90th-minute goal from Carlos Espi , a 21-year-old debutant signed from Levante who now has 11 goals in 14 games. Madrid's summer has been extraordinary in scale: Yan Diomande arrived from RB Leipzig for €125m, the largest fee in the club's history, alongside Marc Cucurella , Denzel Dumfries , and free transfers for Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva . Vinicius Junior renewed to June 2032 on August 6. Mourinho has also imposed a set of dressing-room rules, per AS: prescribed meals, latecomers training alone in the gym rather than being fined, and all rehabilitation done in-house at Valdebebas. On the market he was dismissive on Tuesday: “For me it is closed, but with the market open.” Barcelona , the defending champions, opened with a 5-0 win at Elche : Raphinha two goals and an assist, Fermin Lopez two, Karim Adeyemi scoring on debut and Anthony Gordon assisting twice off the bench on his. The registration crisis that has defined recent Barcelona Augusts did not materialise; Rodri , Adeyemi and Gordon were all registered on August 21 with the club operating under the 1:1 rule after shedding payroll. The Gamper Trophy was staged at the rebuilt Spotify Camp Nou on August 19, and the league opener against Athletic on Thursday is at the stadium too. What Barcelona do not have is a recognised centre-forward. Matteo Moretto's summary of the shortlist was withering: “I don't think it will be Tresoldi, I don't think it will be Gyokeres, I don't think it will be the names that have come out.” The surprise signing he teased turned out to be a goalkeeper, Dominik Livakovic , on a small fee from Fenerbahce . Two more. Rayo Vallecano are homeless in their 50th-anniversary season: Vallecas has failed safety clearance, so they played Alaves at Butarque in Leganes in front of 4,280 people, the smallest crowd of the round, and Getafe have refused them the Coliseum for September 5. And Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , now 37, has signed for promoted Deportivo La Coruna from Marseille and scored twice in his first two games. Germany: Bundesliga Germany has not kicked off. Matchday one is Friday, Bayern Munich against VfB Stuttgart , the latest start in years and another consequence of the World Cup. What Germany has had is a Supercup and a cup round, and both were instructive. Bayern beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 at Signal Iduna Park on August 22 in front of 81,365. The goals came from Nathaniel Brown , a left-back signed from Eintracht Frankfurt who was fielded at number ten and scored on his competitive debut, and Michael Olise in first-half stoppage time. Fabio Silva pulled one back on 75 minutes; Ramy Bensebaini was sent off on 90 and has since been given a two-match cup suspension. Vincent Kompany on Brown: “Sometimes the full-backs' spaces are similar to those of a number ten. He is unbelievably good between the spaces.” It was a fitting start to a week in which Bayern also extended Max Eberl and Jan-Christian Dreesen to June 2029, sold Joao Palhinha permanently to Benfica , and watched Harry Kane collect Germany's Footballer of the Year award, with 272 of 659 votes, days after picking up the European Golden Shoe for 36 league goals. Kompany was named Coach of the Year for last season's double. The DFB-Pokal first round produced a record haul of goals and two proper shocks, both against clubs relegated from the second tier rather than the first: fifth-tier SSV Jeddeloh II beat Heidenheim 5-2, and Rot-Weiss Essen knocked out St Pauli 2-0. Eintracht Frankfurt won 11-0 at SC St Tonis, the biggest cup win in the club's history. Hamburger SV won 3-0 at SC Verl, where Louis Lemke , aged 16 years, 10 months and 16 days, became the youngest goalscorer in HSV history. And at Halle, Edin Dzeko , 40, scored twice for promoted Schalke 04 , roughly fifteen years and eight months after his previous appearance in German top-flight football. “My plan from the very beginning was to come back,” he said. “I really only wanted to keep playing for Schalke.” The week's saddest news came on August 23, when Klaus-Michael Kuhne died aged 89. The logistics billionaire was the second-largest shareholder in HSV's football company, financed the buy-back of the stadium naming rights that restored the Volksparkstadion name, and was for a decade the single most-cited figure in Germany's argument about outside investment in football. He last attended a match in 2015. What happens to his holding is, at the time of writing, unreported. Italy: Serie A Serie A began on August 22 and the opening round belonged to one player. Donyell Malen scored a hat-trick inside 68 minutes as Roma beat Fiorentina 4-0, taking three shots on target and scoring all three, with 11 touches in the opposition box. All three were laid on by Paulo Dybala . Gian Piero Gasperini , who has heard a decade of jokes about Dybala's fragility, took the opportunity: “Paulo is extraordinary, world-class. He could have played extra time too, never mind silk muscles.” Malen now has 17 goals in Europe's top five leagues in the calendar year 2026, level with Kane, albeit in more appearances. Nine of the twenty benches changed over the summer. Ruben Amorim took Milan and won 2-1 at Torino , with 18-year-old Alphadjo Cisse scoring on his Serie A debut. Massimiliano Allegri took Napoli and won 2-0 at Genoa , where the game's flashpoint arrived: Kevin De Bruyne 's 82nd-minute opener came after contact with Genoa's Johan Vasquez that referee Marco Di Bello waved away and VAR did not review. Daniele De Rossi called it “one of the ugliest episodes of my career.” The refereeing body, led by Daniele Orsato , backed Di Bello while conceding that giving a foul would not have been a serious error. The disciplinary fallout landed on Genoa: director Diego Javier Lopez was banned until September 8 for entering the pitch and obstructing the referee. Reigning champions Inter beat Monza 4-1, Pio Esposito scoring with a backheel. Maurizio Sarri won on his Atalanta debut, Gennaro Gattuso won on his Lazio debut through Davide Frattesi , who had trained with his new teammates six times. Juventus won 1-0 at Frosinone through a Bremer header and then lost Kenan Yildiz : a foot injury, examined at J Medical, with Gazzetta and ANSA both reporting a suspected fracture, possible surgery and up to two months out. As of Monday the results were still pending. Fiorentina, meanwhile, are in open crisis after one match, with the Florence press putting Fabio Grosso on trial for his team selection and Franco Mastantuono , on loan from Real Madrid, throwing something to the ground when substituted. France: Ligue 1 France opened on August 22 with an 18-club division containing two newcomers, Troyes and Le Mans , the latter back after 16 years. Marseille lead on goal difference after beating Strasbourg 4-0; Lens , the reigning Coupe de France holders, put five past Auxerre . Champions Paris Saint-Germain , chasing a sixth consecutive title, drew 2-2 at Rennes . That draw produced the French story of the week. Luis Enrique withdrew both Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at half-time. On Tuesday PSG announced Dembele would miss Friday's trip to Lille, stating that “in agreement with the coach and the sporting management, Ousmane Dembele will have a period of rest over the coming days,” and insisting it was unrelated to the substitution. The 2025 Ballon d'Or winner has three appearances and 120 minutes this season. RMC's Daniel Riolo was unconvinced: “Are we talking about a week's rest, or can we say things clearly and call it a heavy punishment?” Lille's summer needs no further introduction after Bouaddi, but the club has also brought in Dilane Bakwa on a straight season loan from Nottingham Forest with no option. Lyon spent Wednesday night trying to reach the Champions League league phase for the first time in six years, hosting Fenerbahce at the Groupama Stadium after a 1-1 first leg; qualification is worth roughly €25m to a club still under financial restriction. The tie kicked off as this edition went to press. Lyon also deactivated 437 tickets identified in illegal resale to keep visiting supporters out of home sections. The larger French story is money. Ligue 1+, the league's own channel, carries every match but is running well below revenue expectations, and the LFP may open a new tender as early as October. The league lost €78.5m a year when beIN Sports dropped its Saturday package and received an €85m settlement when DAZN exited early. Olivier Bramly of LFP Media has held talks with Apple, Netflix, Amazon and Paramount, and Canal+, which had walked away from French football, has re-established contact: Bramly met chief executive Maxime Saada recently. A regulatory change now allows the rights to be sold as a single package rather than split into lots. They beat Columbus Crew 3-2 on Saturday with stoppage-time goals from Reed Baker-Whiting and Andy Najar . In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps lead on 40 points from 20 with a game in hand on almost everyone, and hammered FC Dallas 5-0. Thomas Muller is at the heart of it. Lionel Messi , 39, is second in the East with Inter Miami on 39 points and has 14 goals and nine assists in the regular season. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest North London · Est. 1886 · Free of Social Media The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, Every Tuesday No. 2 · Edition of Tuesday, August 25, 2026 · Champions of England In This Edition The Lead Transfer News The Squad Hale End Arsenal Women Gunners Abroad Numbers of the Week In Brief What to Watch The Lead Six Days to Remake a Forward Line Arsenal have won their first two matches of the title defence by an aggregate of 6-0 and have not conceded a goal. Underneath that placid surface, the champions are dismantling and rebuilding their attack with less than a week of the window left, and the outcome rests on two men who have not yet decided anything. T here is a particular kind of quiet that settles over a club that has just won the league. Arsenal have spent this month enjoying it. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on August 16, a match settled inside 24 seconds by Riccardo Calafiori and finished off by Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard . Five days later they opened the Premier League season at the Emirates by beating newly promoted Coventry City 3-0 on a Friday night, and the visitors did not register a single tackle in the first half. Two matches, six goals, none conceded, and a manager who described the evening as having "a lot to like" about it. And yet the most consequential Arsenal story of the past seven days did not happen on a pitch. It happened on the phone lines between north London, Riyadh and Madrid, and it concerns the shape of the attack that Mikel Arteta will take into a Champions League campaign that begins in a fortnight. The Premier League window closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. That leaves six days for a set of decisions that will define the season more than any of the five signings already made. The Two Undecided Men The first is Gabriel Martinelli . David Ornstein of The Athletic reported on August 23 that Arsenal have placed a valuation of around 70 million euros, roughly 60 million pounds, on the Brazilian, and that the player is open to a move to the Middle East. Al Hilal have been circling for a fortnight. Sky Sports reported on Monday that the two clubs are closing on an agreement, with a sell-on clause understood to be part of the structure, and that the decision now belongs to the player himself. Martinelli turned down an approach from Galatasaray last week. He has been left out of both matchday squads so far this season. Whichever figure the deal eventually lands on, it will comfortably break Arsenal's record for a player sale. The second is the man Arsenal would like to sign with the proceeds, and here the picture is genuinely unresolved. Fabrizio Romano said on Tuesday that Arsenal remain attentive to Julian Alvarez , that the club has an internal feeling it could reach agreement with Atletico Madrid on the financial terms, and that Arsenal will not lodge a formal bid until the striker signals he actually wants to come. That last clause is the whole story. Alvarez has made no secret of preferring Barcelona , a move Spanish reporting describes as financially close to fiction, and the Argentine press is split on whether Atletico are desperate to sell or determined to keep him and rehabilitate him in front of a crowd that whistled him. Arsenal are not, on the current evidence, prepared to spend anything close to 150 million on a player who regards them as a fallback. This is a more disciplined position than Arsenal have historically taken in the last week of a window, and it is worth pausing on. Andrea Berta , in his second summer as sporting director, has run a window of unusual decisiveness. Piero Hincapie made permanent from Bayer Leverkusen for a reported 34.5 million in June, Illan Meslier taken on a free from Leeds United in July, Christos Tzolis bought from Club Brugge for a reported 34 million as the designated replacement for Leandro Trossard , Bruno Guimaraes prised out of Newcastle United for a reported 75 million, and then Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on the eve of the season for 51 million plus 4 million in add-ons. That is roughly 198.5 million pounds of gross spending before deadline week has even started. "He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment." Ian Wright, on Gabriel Martinelli What the Money Has Not Settled What that spending has not yet bought is a resolution to the question Arsenal have been circling for two years. Havertz started the opener and scored, having also scored in Cardiff, which left Viktor Gyokeres on the bench and unused. The Swede scored 14 Premier League goals and 21 in all competitions in his first season, numbers that would flatter most centre-forwards and which somehow still left the debate open. Arteta's public position is that the two are complementary rather than competing. His team sheets over the past ten days suggest something slightly firmer than that. Meanwhile the club is quietly working the other end of the ledger. Ethan Nwaneri , back from a difficult half-season on loan at Marseille , is the subject of loan interest from Newcastle United and others, with Arsenal understood to prefer a temporary move to a sale. Gabriel Jesus has one year left and has been linked with a Premier League exit. Fabio Vieira , Reiss Nelson and Kepa Arrizabalaga are all names the club would move on if the right offer arrives. There is more traffic to come through the gates at London Colney in the next six days than there has been all summer. The context that makes it urgent is Europe. Arsenal lost the Champions League final in Budapest on May 30, drawing 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain after Havertz had scored inside six minutes, and going out 4-3 on penalties after Eberechi Eze missed and David Raya saved from Nuno Mendes . Arsenal had four shots that night to PSG's eighteen. That is the reason a club that has just won its first title in 22 years spent the summer buying a 75 million midfielder and a 55 million centre-back rather than resting on it. The league is being defended. Europe is being attacked. Both plans need a front line that is finished, and as of Tuesday lunchtime, it is not. Konsa Goes Home on Monday Night Arsenal's first road test of the season is at Villa Park, four days after signing Villa's best defender. It is also a meeting between a side who have not conceded and a side who shipped four in ninety minutes. The fixture computer has an unkind sense of humour. On Monday, August 31, at 8pm UK time, which is midday Pacific, Arsenal travel to Villa Park with Ezri Konsa likely to make his debut against the club he served for seven years and left ten days earlier. He missed the Coventry match because he only completed his medical and signed that morning. Aston Villa arrive in a considerably worse state than anyone expected. They were beaten 4-0 at Brighton on the opening weekend, sit twentieth on goal difference, lost their best centre-back to the champions, and will be without Joao Gomes through an automatic suspension after a red card for violent conduct in that Brighton defeat. Reporting in the West Midlands has Villa chasing Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez to plug the hole Konsa left. For Arsenal the selection questions are more interesting than the opposition. Bruno Guimaraes missed the opener with a muscle problem picked up in the Community Shield, variously reported as thigh and groin tightness, and Arteta's assessment was pointedly relaxed: "We expect that not to be weeks at all." If the Brazilian is fit, Arteta must decide whether to break up a midfield that functioned beautifully at the Emirates, with Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly behind Martin Odegaard . Lewis-Skelly, playing in central midfield rather than at left-back, had 94 touches at 95 per cent passing accuracy. At the back, Cristhian Mosquera partnered Gabriel Magalhaes in the absence of William Saliba and did so without alarm. Konsa's arrival gives Arteta a genuine alternative there and, usefully, a second option at right-back where Ben White has started both matches and provided an assist on Friday. Villa Park in late August, against a wounded and short-handed home side, is exactly the kind of fixture the champions dropped points in three seasons running before last year. That is what makes it worth watching rather than merely worth winning. Transfer News Martinelli and the Record That Is About to Fall Status: advanced talks between clubs. Player decision pending. Seven years after arriving from Ituano as a teenager nobody outside Brazil had heard of, Gabriel Martinelli is on the edge of leaving Arsenal for Saudi Arabia. The reporting has moved quickly and in one direction. David Ornstein established the frame on August 23: Arsenal value the winger at around 70 million euros, roughly 60 million pounds, and Martinelli is open to the move. Sky Sports followed on Monday with news that Al Hilal and Arsenal are close to agreement, with a sell-on clause of about 20 per cent of future profit expected in the structure. Fee figures reported elsewhere this week have ranged from a 47 million pound opening bid up to a 55 million pound near-complete deal in the Daily Mail. Readers should treat any single number as provisional until the club confirms one. What is not in dispute is the direction of travel: Martinelli has been omitted from both matchday squads this season, he rejected a Galatasaray approach reported at around 38 million pounds, and the decision now sits with him rather than with either club. It is a strange way for a significant Arsenal career to end. Martinelli was part of the squad that won the title last season, though he managed only one league goal in it, and James McNicholas of The Athletic has reported that the club never explicitly told him he was for sale even as it worked to find him a destination. Ian Wright , never a man to leave a Hale End-adjacent grievance unspoken, said this week that Martinelli deserves better treatment than he has received. The financial logic is harder to argue with. Arsenal's previous record sale has stood since 2017. Selling a 25-year-old with reportedly one year left on his contract, for a fee in this range, to fund a marquee replacement, is precisely the sort of trade the club has spent a decade being told it should make. This is the thread that will decide whether Arsenal's window is remembered as good or as great, and it is also the one where readers should be most careful about what they believe. Here is what can be stood up. Fabrizio Romano reported on Tuesday that Arsenal remain attentive to Julian Alvarez , believe they could reach a financial agreement with Atletico Madrid , and will only make an official approach once the player indicates he wants to join. Atletico's asking price has been reported at around 150 million. Beyond that, the Spanish and Argentine reporting diverges almost completely. Infobae, drawing on El Chiringuito and the English press, described Atletico as desperate to sell but unwilling to sell to Barcelona , and reported that Arteta has set one condition: the player must be genuinely committed to the move rather than treating Arsenal as a consolation. La Nacion, on the same days, reported almost the opposite, that Atletico refuse to negotiate below the release clause, that Arsenal and Atletico "never found common ground," and that Alvarez himself has reservations about returning to England after his time at Manchester City . Both cannot be right. What both agree on is that Alvarez's preference is Barcelona, that Barcelona cannot afford it, and that the clock runs out on September 1. The Daily Mirror reported Arteta is prepared to sanction a push of around 130 million pounds with the same caveat about commitment attached. Treat all of it as live and unresolved. The logic on Arsenal's side is straightforward. Nwaneri is homegrown, which makes him valuable both for squad registration and, in accounting terms, as pure profit if ever sold. Selling him at 19 after one difficult loan would be the sort of decision clubs regret for a decade. Two pre-season wins in four days suggest the idea is taking. Arsenal beat Manchester City 2-1 in a behind-closed-doors friendly at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on August 20. Stina Blackstenius headed them in front from a corner, Lauren Hemp equalised with a curled finish, and then Selina Cerci released Lisa Baum to win it late. Three days later, in front of a crowd at Meadow Park, they beat Paris FC 1-0 with Olivia Smith cutting inside and finishing in the 91st minute. Georgia Stanway was excellent in both, Geraldine Reuteler impressed in a 30-minute debut cameo, and Alessia Russo had a goal ruled out for offside after coming on at half-time. Smilla Holmberg went off at the break with a knock. Baum is the story worth telling properly. She is 19, arrived from RB Leipzig in July with Barcelona , Manchester United and Bayern Munich all reported to have wanted her, and has now scored in pre-season against the reigning WSL champions. She is also the clearest expression of what Slegers has been building. Arsenal drew six league games last season and lost the title to Manchester City largely because they could not turn control into goals. The recruitment answer has been three Bundesliga forwards ( Baum , Cerci from Hoffenheim and Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt ) chosen for their ability to create a shot from nothing in tight spaces. The two headline arrivals are Georgia Stanway , back in England from Bayern Munich , and Ona Batlle , signed on a free from Barcelona on July 10. Stanway's early public framing of the move has been notable in itself: she has described Arsenal as "setting the standard with women's football" and said the club is "more than just a football club." Two goalkeepers, Isabella Damm from Brondby and Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , have also arrived this month. The outgoing traffic has been just as heavy and considerably more emotional. Beth Mead , Katie McCabe , Victoria Pelova , Laia Codina and Manuela Zinsberger have all left, with Mead joining Manchester City . Matchday 1 has been split: five matches went ahead between 15 and 17 August, while the openers of clubs with players who reached the World Cup semi-finals or beyond were deferred to between 19 and 27 August, an agreement between LaLiga, the RFEF and the players' union to reduce injury risk. Espanyol lead the table on goals scored after a 3-0 win over Levante , Roberto Fernandez scoring twice inside 40 minutes. Alaves beat Getafe 3-0 and Deportivo marked their return to the top flight after eight years with a 1-1 draw against Elche in which Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored on debut. Atletico Madrid host Malaga as this edition goes out. Two rows are already running. The opening night produced an immediate refereeing controversy at Sevilla , where Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea awarded a penalty, saw it overturned by VAR, then gave another in the seventh minute of stoppage time that El Debate and others reported the replays did not support. Sevilla won 2-1. Rayo Vallecano 's Alvaro Garcia said afterwards: "Three penalties. The match was even, but too much of a leading role for the person who should not be a lead character." Separately, Celta against Osasuna was postponed on 13 August because of a problem with the Balaidos turf , identified in Spanish reporting as a fungus. Osasuna issued a statement expressing "absolute disagreement" with the new date of 27 August, saying both clubs had agreed the September international break would work and that the team most harmed by the postponement is once again the team most harmed by the fix. Meanwhile Real Madrid open their season at Espanyol on Saturday under Jose Mourinho , their third head coach in eight months, after beating Schalke 3-0 in Gelsenkirchen to finish pre-season unbeaten. Bundesliga Germany starts last, on 28 August, but Saturday brings the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup at Signal Iduna Park, where Borussia Dortmund host Bayern Munich as last season's runners-up. Bayern arrive as champions of a league they won on 19 April with four games to spare while scoring a record 122 goals, and with Harry Kane collecting the European Golden Shoe in Munich on 19 August for 36 Bundesliga goals, ahead of Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe . Bayern beat RB Leipzig 3-1 and Heidenheim 4-2 in friendlies, with Kane and Michael Olise returning as substitutes after extended post-World Cup breaks. Below Bayern the picture is uneven. Eintracht Frankfurt lost 7-0 at Brentford on 15 August in their final friendly, captain Robin Koch going off injured at half time; the club's own report called it an expensive education. RB Leipzig lost their record signing Yan Diomande to Real Madrid for a reported €140m including bonuses and their replacement target Moreira to Milan, and Martin Demichelis said publicly that his sporting director "has work to do." Sebastian Hoeness of Stuttgart , contracted to 2028, acknowledged on 19 August that clubs including Manchester City and Milan have made enquiries about him, saying it would "not now be surprising if there were perhaps one or two clubs that made an enquiry about me," as reported by sport.de on 19 August. And the Bundeskartellamt delivered its final assessment on the 50+1 rule on 12 August, accepting the rule's aims while ruling that enforcement must be consistent and naming Leverkusen , Wolfsburg , RB Leipzig and Hannover 96 as needing to change. That is currently single-sourced in English and the authority's own document is worth reading before anyone declares 50+1 saved. Serie A Italy kicks off on Saturday and has already produced its first disaster. Lazio , beaten finalists in last season's Coppa Italia, went out of this season's competition at the first hurdle, losing 2-0 at home to Serie B side Mantova in Gennaro Gattuso 's competitive debut, Ruocco scoring on 75 minutes and Cajazzo in stoppage time. Gattuso was without six players through injury or fatigue. "It's a devastating blow," he said, per ANSA . "We must apologise and move forward with focus and unity rather than seeking excuses." Il Messaggero and Leggo both marked him four out of ten for a nightmare debut. In the same round Palermo knocked out Lecce 2-0, Pisa went through on penalties against Empoli , and of the Serie A clubs playing on 17 August only Sassuolo won. The league also arrives with a new refereeing regime. On 18 August the AIA held an online meeting with all 20 clubs, run by technical director Domenico Messina and the new CAN designator Daniele Orsato , whose predecessor Gianluca Rocchi self-suspended in late April while under investigation for sporting fraud over allegedly steered appointments. Calcio e Finanza set out the changes , which broadly mirror England's: VAR confined to clear and obvious error, a one-minute exile for treated players, a visible five-second count on restarts, and a strengthened captain protocol. "The legacy of the World Cup is that we saw how the central figure was the referee," Orsato said. Not everyone is charmed by the calendar: Maurizio Sarri , now at Atalanta , called the transfer window dates "madness" and said that discussing the market endlessly is "an insult to my profession," per Tuttosport . Ligue 1 France produced the result of the week. RC Lens beat Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on 16 August to win the Trophee des Champions for the first time in the club's history, Florian Thauvin scoring on 32 minutes and Lens then playing roughly 47 minutes of normal time with ten men after Kyllian Antonio was sent off. Nuno Mendes was dismissed late for PSG, who had 69 per cent of the ball and 22 shots to Lens's eight. Goalkeeper Robin Risser made six saves. Zinedine Zidane , confirmed as France head coach on 28 July, watched from the stand. Lens head coach Dino Toppmoller 's dressing-room speech, published the next day by RMC, is the quote of the French week: "Lens is this: we fear no one. We said it before the match, we can beat everyone here." Luis Enrique 's verdict, on PSG's own site, was one line: "I'm pleased with what I saw, but frustrated." Four days earlier PSG had won a second consecutive UEFA Super Cup, beating Aston Villa 2-1 in Salzburg, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue scoring and Villa's 17-year-old Brian Madjo becoming the youngest player to start and score in the fixture, which was refereed by Omar Artan of Somalia, the first non-European to take a Super Cup. Elsewhere Monaco and Paul Pogba ended their partnership by mutual consent on 19 August , the club saying "the objectives initially set were only partially achieved" and Pogba replying that he would "always be grateful." Nice signed the 37-year-old Axel Witsel on a free from Girona on 18 August as emergency cover after a serious knee injury to Laurent Abergel . And the league itself changes shape commercially: with beIN Sports declining to renew, Ligue 1+ becomes the sole broadcaster of every match, with the subscription rising to €19.99. The season also has zero midweek matchdays, a deliberate scheduling choice. Major League Soccer America is the only league of the six in the thick of it, and Nashville SC have taken it over. They sit on 43 points from 19 matches with a goal difference of plus 24 and only 15 conceded, five clear of Inter Miami , and they demolished them 4-1 on 15 August, Hany Mukhtar scoring twice in the second half after goalkeeper Brian Schwake saved a first-half Lionel Messi penalty. Miami's fortnight has been grim: they went out of the Leagues Cup in the league phase on 12 August, losing 3-2 at home to Club Leon with three points from three matches, their worst campaign of the Messi era. Messi came on at half time to a standing ovation, days after the death of his father and long-time agent Jorge Messi at 68. "For people to understand what Leo Messi is, I think it was proven today," Leon coach Javier Gandolfi said. "He's a competitive animal, a player who, in my opinion, is the best in history." In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps lead on 37 points from 18 with the best goal difference in the league, and clinched a record ninth Cascadia Cup by winning 2-0 at Seattle Sounders on 17 August, Rayan Elloumi and Thomas Muller scoring in front of 30,026. Seattle are in freefall, that defeat extending a league losing run to seven, with Jesus Ferreira going off injured after 36 minutes and Brian Schmetzer conceding his team managed only "30 to 35 good minutes." Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the Golden Boot race on 14 goals. Chicago Fire have won five straight in all competitions for the first time since 2000. And at Orlando City , Antoine Griezmann has two goals, one assist and 14 chances created in his first six appearances since arriving from Atletico, team-mate Griffin Dorsey telling MLSsoccer that "as much as he's a star, it's very easy to be in a room with Grizi and feel like he's just another human being." Numbers of the Week 76.5m euros The total value of Rodri's move from Manchester City to Barcelona, per ESPN. Sky reported the fee as £65.4m. 10 of 20 new benches Premier League clubs starting the season with a manager they did not have a year ago. 43 points Nashville SC's total from 19 MLS matches, five clear at the top and only 15 goals conceded. 36 goals Harry Kane's Bundesliga tally last season, enough for the European Golden Shoe, presented in Munich on 19 August. In Brief Vinicius Junior has extended at Real Madrid to 30 June 2032, the club confirming the deal on 6 August and closing a saga that had run for the better part of two years. Borussia Dortmund signed Joey Veerman from PSV on 18 August after activating a €21.5m release clause. Managing director Lars Ricken said the club had "deliberately focused our transfer activities this summer on the central midfield." Niclas Fullkrug has returned to Werder Bremen on loan, taking a pay cut. Nico Elvedi left Borussia Monchengladbach for Leeds United for a reported €10m after 11 years. Atalanta sold Matteo Ruggeri to Aston Villa permanently on 19 August, fee undisclosed, and Parma sold goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to Villa the same day, Sky Sports reporting £29.9m. Alexia Putellas has left Barcelona after 14 years for London City Lionesses , part of a women's-team exodus that also includes Mapi Leon , Salma Paralluelo , now at Olympique Lyonnais , and Ona Batlle . k: Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against Coventry on Friday, three days after a 3-0 Community Shield win and with the centre-back department still unfixed.
x: North London Since 1886 The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every week, all of it. Edition No. 1 Tuesday, August 18, 2026 The Lead Champions Again, and Already One Defender Short Arsenal open the defence of a first league title in twenty-two years on Friday night against Coventry City. The Community Shield said one thing about this squad. The treatment room says another. T wenty-five seconds. That is how long Arsenal waited to score the first goal of their post-championship life. Myles Lewis-Skelly slid a ball into the space that Manchester City had not yet decided to defend, and Riccardo Calafiori arrived at the end of it. By the time the Principality Stadium had settled into its seats on Sunday afternoon the Community Shield was already tilting. It finished 3-0. It could reasonably have finished by more. That is the version of this football club the rest of the league will be looking at on Friday evening, when Coventry City arrive at the Emirates for the curtain-raiser of the 2026-27 season. It is not the whole picture. The whole picture includes a centre-half who cannot play, a right-sided defender who cannot play, and a sporting director with under a fortnight to do something about both. The injury that shapes everything William Saliba came off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final in July and has not been right since. Arsenal confirmed on July 23 that specialist reviews had found a back injury requiring "a period of rehabilitation," and that he would be out for an extended spell. Surgery was considered and rejected, which is the good news: the operation would have cost four to five months. The BBC's Sami Mokbel has since put the realistic floor at two to three months, pointing at the home fixture with Leeds United on October 10 as a plausible re-entry point. Jurrien Timber , who had a small procedure on a stubborn groin problem, is further along but not close. Mikel Arteta said on August 10 that there were still "a few weeks to go." Key Facts / Arsenal v Coventry City Kickoff Friday, August 21, 12:00pm Pacific (8:00pm BST), Emirates Stadium Occasion Matchweek 1. Arsenal open a season as reigning champions for the first time since 2004-05. The visitors Coventry won the Championship by 11 points under Frank Lampard. First top-flight season in 25 years. Head to head Arsenal have won the last five meetings, aggregate 16-2. They last met in the FA Cup in 2014. Unavailable Saliba (back), Timber (groin). Ben White is fit and started the Shield. Losing Saliba is not a squad-depth inconvenience. It is a structural one. Sky Sports noted alongside the club's July statement that Arsenal 's win rate falls from 68 per cent to 50 per cent in matches he does not start. The reason is visible in the way Arteta asks his team to play. The high line that lets Arsenal compress the pitch and win the ball 60 yards from their own goal is underwritten by a defender who can recover 40 metres in a straight line without panicking. Take him out and either the line drops, which costs territory, or it does not, which costs goals. On Sunday the answer was Cristhian Mosquera alongside Gabriel Magalhaes , with Ben White at right-back and Calafiori at left, and it worked well enough that the question got quieter for ninety minutes. Manchester City , under Enzo Maresca for the first time in a showpiece, never really got Erling Haaland into the game. Jeremy Doku was doubled up on the touchline every time he took possession. David Raya made the two saves that mattered. But a Community Shield in the third week of August is not a Tuesday in Naples in November, and Arteta knows the difference. Asked afterwards about the window, he did not bother with the usual manager's shrug. "We know there are certain areas that through injuries we are weaker and we need to strengthen. We're trying to do that and we've been trying to do that for weeks." Mikel Arteta, August 17 Selection, and too many good players The selection questions for Friday sit further forward. Kai Havertz scored the second goal on Sunday and started ahead of Viktor Gyokeres , who came off the bench, and a real debate has opened about which of them leads the line in the games that decide seasons. Gyokeres was Arsenal 's leading league scorer last season with 14: a respectable debut return for a 55-million-pound striker, and a slightly underwhelming one for a player who arrived from Sporting CP with a reputation as an unstoppable force. Havertz offers the link play that makes Martin Odegaard 's job easier, and Odegaard was the best player on the pitch in Cardiff. There is also the matter of who plays on the right. Bukayo Saka went to the World Cup, played in England's bronze-medal match against France on July 18, and returned late; he was a substitute on Sunday. Noni Madueke started in his place and kept it through most of the game. Arteta has more players than shirts, which is the position every champion wants to be in and the position that creates a specific problem. Gabriel Jesus , Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri were all left out of the Shield squad entirely: all three fit, all three now the subject of transfer conversations. Do not dismiss the visitors Coventry City should not be treated as a formality even though the bookmakers treat them as one. Frank Lampard 's side won the Championship by eleven points, which is not a play-off scramble but a procession. They have spent the summer sensibly: Carl Rushworth made permanent in goal after his loan from Brighton , six new arrivals in all, Gustavo Hamer and Taiwo Awoniyi to carry the attack. They beat Monaco 2-0 and Espanyol 3-1 in pre-season. A newly promoted team playing its first top-flight match in twenty-five years, away, in front of the champions' crowd, under lights, is a team with nothing to lose and a manager who will have spent a fortnight thinking about nothing else. The larger frame is what makes Friday interesting rather than routine. Arsenal have not defended a Premier League title since 2004, and the last time they tried they were coming off an unbeaten season and still finished second. The 2025-26 team won it by seven points with the best defence in the division, and it has been strengthened rather than dismantled: Bruno Guimaraes for 75 million, Christos Tzolis for 34, Piero Hincapie made permanent. What has not been solved, three days before kickoff, is the one thing that broke on its own. The Title Defence Tracker The Premier League has not kicked off. The baseline Arsenal are defending, from 2025-26: 85 Points, 1st +44 Goal diff 27 Conceded 19 Clean sheets Record 26-7-5 from 38, seven points clear of Manchester City . First title since 2003-04, ending a 22-year wait, and Arsenal's 14th English championship. Clinched on May 19 when City drew at Bournemouth. Last Season's Scorers Viktor Gyokeres, Premier League goals 14 Arsenal goals from corners, an all-time record 18 Erling Haaland, Golden Boot winner 27 The 75-Million-Pound Rewiring of the Arsenal Midfield Bruno Guimaraes played 45 minutes in Cardiff. It was enough to see what Arteta has bought, and what it does to everybody else. The signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United on August 9, for a fee reported at 75 million pounds on a four-year deal with a further year at the club's option, was the most expensive piece of business Arsenal have done this summer and the least obviously necessary. This was a squad that already contained Declan Rice , Martin Zubimendi , Mikel Merino and Odegaard . Adding a 28-year-old Brazilian international to that group looks, on a team sheet, like hoarding. Watch the Community Shield and it looks like something else. Guimaraes started in a three with Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard , which is not the shape anybody predicted, and the effect was to give Arsenal a midfielder who breaks lines with a pass rather than with a carry. Rice destroys and drives. Zubimendi circulates. Guimaraes plays the ball that skips a phase. Against a City side pressing in a mid-block, that was the difference between working the ball around the outside and getting through the middle of it. He was withdrawn at half-time for Rice , which reads less like a hook than like a manager who signed a player nine days ago and is not going to break him in week one. The knock-on effects are real. Lewis-Skelly , nineteen, started in midfield rather than at left-back and produced the pass for the opening goal. Zubimendi , a World Cup winner five weeks ago, came off the bench. Merino did not get on. That is why the outgoing side of this window has become as consequential as the incoming one. Transfer News Thirteen Days to Find a Centre-Half Konsa, Quansah, Kounde, Pubill. Four names, four different problems, and a deadline that does not move. The furthest advanced of the four is Ezri Konsa , and "furthest advanced" is doing heavy lifting in that sentence. Arsenal have made at least two approaches to Aston Villa for the England defender, with reported figures in the 30 to 45 million range. Villa have valued him at 60 million and not blinked. As of Monday the second proposal had fallen short and the two clubs were not close. Certainty: bid made, fee not agreed . The alternative that emerged over the weekend is Jarell Quansah , the 23-year-old former Liverpool defender now at Bayer Leverkusen . ESPN reported on August 16 that Arsenal had opened talks and that Leverkusen want somewhere around 50 million euros. This is the deal that makes the most institutional sense: a Premier League-schooled defender still on the right side of 24, at a club Arsenal have just done business with over Hincapie , at a price that does not require selling anybody. Certainty: early talks . The glamour option is Jules Kounde . Catalan outlets including Mundo Deportivo and SPORT reported in the middle of last week that Arsenal were prepared to pay a substantial fee for the Barcelona defender, with Liverpool also circling. Treat this one with care. It is sourced entirely to the selling market, no bid has been confirmed, and Barcelona 's financial calendar has a way of generating stories about players they might sell. Certainty: concrete interest, single market, unconfirmed . The fourth is already dead. Arsenal made contact with Atletico Madrid about Marc Pubill , and Fabrizio Romano and Jorge Garcia Hernandez of AS both reported around August 13 and 14 that Atletico had declared the defender non-transferable, pointing at a release clause of 500 million euros by way of punctuation. Certainty: rejected . Read those four together and a pattern emerges. Andrea Berta is not shopping for a squad player. He is shopping for someone who can start thirty games at the heart of a title defence and then hand the shirt back when Saliba returns. That is a strange and expensive brief, and it explains why the club has been willing to look at four different leagues rather than settle for the obvious. It also explains Arteta 's unusually direct language on Sunday. Managers do not normally say they are weaker. Ins & Outs / Summer 2026 Confirmed and official. The window closes in the first week of September. Red is money leaving Arsenal, navy is money arriving. Bruno Guimaraes £75m Piero Hincapie £34.5m Christos Tzolis £34m Jakub Kiwior up to £22.4m Leandro Trossard £15.3m Christian Norgaard £7m Karl Hein £2.6m Nwaneri at the Crossroads Four clubs, two countries, and a buy-back clause. The most delicate decision of Arsenal's summer involves a player who is not going to start. He was fit. He had trained. He had played through pre-season. And on Sunday, Ethan Nwaneri was not in the Community Shield squad at all, which is the loudest thing Arteta has said about him all summer. The manager's public phrasing was more diplomatic. Nwaneri , he said, "needs consistent minutes at this stage of his career." The nineteen-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Marseille , a move that went wrong for reasons largely outside his control. Roberto De Zerbi , the coach who wanted him, left shortly after he arrived, and under Habib Beye he managed a little over 400 minutes across nine appearances, with two goals. He came back to a club that had just won the league and then added Tzolis and Guimaraes on top of a forward line that already had Saka , Madueke , Eberechi Eze and Martinelli in it. The most concrete reporting so far comes from Italy. Carlo Pellegatti has described RB Leipzig as being in advanced talks, with the German club prepared to offer between 35 and 40 million euros for a permanent transfer, and Arsenal exploring a buy-back clause valued at 55 to 60 million. Leipzig expect funds from an outgoing sale of their own and have capped individual spending at 45 million this summer, which makes the arithmetic plausible. AC Milan made an enquiry in late July and have been linked with a loan. Borussia Dortmund , Fulham and Galatasaray have all been mentioned. Certainty: exit expected, structure undecided . The complication is that Nwaneri is contracted to 2030, so Arsenal face no pressure at all. Selling a Hale End graduate who broke the Premier League's youngest-player record is the kind of decision that gets re-litigated for a decade if it goes wrong. A loan protects the asset and solves nothing. A sale with a buy-back solves the minutes problem and transfers the risk to whether the buy-back price stays sane. Somebody at London Colney has to pick one within a fortnight. The Turkish Channel Galatasaray bid for Martinelli and were turned down. What else was on the table in that conversation is the more interesting story. David Ornstein reported on August 14 that Galatasaray had bid 45 million euros, around 38.4 million pounds, for Gabriel Martinelli , and that the Brazilian had declined the move. Arsenal are understood to be open to selling him at the right number, but to a club in one of Europe's leading leagues rather than to Turkey, and Martinelli 's own preference appears to run the same way. He scored eleven goals in 53 appearances last season and was left out of the Shield squad. Certainty: bid made, declined by player . The detail worth filing away came from the BBC's Sami Mokbel , also on August 14. In the course of those talks, the future of Victor Osimhen is understood to have been discussed as well. Berta and his assistant Maurizio Michele have long-standing relationships in Turkey, and Berta 's brief this summer explicitly includes making Arsenal active sellers rather than only buyers. Nothing about this constitutes a pursuit of Osimhen . It does tell you that the channel between the two clubs is open in both directions, which is worth remembering if a striker becomes available in the last week of the window. Certainty: single-source, exploratory, no bid . The Rumour Mill The smaller threads, the ones still simmering, and where each of them honestly sits. Pedro Neto The noisiest name of the past week and the least likely to move. Chelsea are willing to sell, but the asking price has travelled from around 70 million on August 10, per Simon Phillips , to close to 100 million by Monday, and Arsenal are in a queue with Manchester City and Tottenham . Given that Tzolis arrived in July and produced six assists and a goal in six pre-season matches, spending nine figures on another wide forward would be a strange use of the remaining budget. Certainty: interest, no bid . Nico Williams Berta held discussions over the Athletic Club winger, whose release clause sits at around 90 million euros, after moves for other wide targets fell away earlier in the summer. Reported by Graeme Bailey on August 6 and quiet since. Certainty: interest, dormant . Gabriel Jesus In talks with Napoli at agent level, per Fabrizio Romano on August 7 and 8. His new representative also represents the Napoli coach, which is how these conversations tend to start. Arsenal want a permanent sale in the region of 20 million rather than a loan, and Napoli must resolve Romelu Lukaku 's future first. Certainty: agent-level talks . Martin Zubimendi Interest from Real Madrid surfaced through Spanish reporting and football.london's Tom Canton on August 10, with a figure around 90 million euros attached. Arsenal have no intention of selling and Madrid are reported to be internally divided on whether to pursue it. Certainty: rumour . Myles Lewis-Skelly Chelsea made a second formal enquiry, reported by Sky Sports on August 12, with Manchester United also long-term admirers. The teenager has signed a new five-year contract and Arsenal have no interest in selling to a domestic rival. Arteta 's response was the only correct one: "if there is speculation about our players, it's a good sign." Certainty: enquiry rebuffed . Salma Paralluelo On the women's side, the forward is a free agent following her release by Barcelona , with Arsenal named alongside Chelsea and OL Lyonnes among interested parties. Nothing has been confirmed by any of the three. Certainty: unconfirmed link . The Squad What Cardiff Told Us, and What It Did Not Ninety minutes against Manchester City is a poor sample and a good sign. Reading it honestly. Arteta sent out Raya behind White , Mosquera , Gabriel and Calafiori , a midfield of Guimaraes , Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard , and a front line of Madueke , Havertz and Tzolis . Read that back and note how many players you would call automatic starters are missing from it: Saka , Rice , Zubimendi , Gyokeres , Eze . All five were on the bench. All five came on or could have. The press, and the corner The pressing was the most striking feature. Arsenal scored inside half a minute because they were already hunting the ball when City tried to play out, and they never really stopped. This is the pattern that produced 27 goals conceded and 19 clean sheets last season, and it survived the loss of the defender who anchors it, at least for one afternoon. Set pieces remain the club's most distinctive weapon and the one most likely to suffer if the personnel change. Arsenal scored 18 goals from corners in 2025-26, an all-time Premier League single-season record, beating a mark that had stood for 32 years. More than 40 per cent of their league goals arrived from dead-ball situations. That routine depends heavily on aerial threat from centre-backs. It is another quiet argument for signing a defender who can head a ball, not just defend a counter. The armband The captaincy was settled without drama. Odegaard retained the armband after a vote of players and staff that Arteta described as unanimous "by a big, big 100 miles," and then won man of the match in the Shield. He has held the role since 2022, but the manner of the confirmation matters in a dressing room about to shed several senior names. Availability / Men's First Team William Saliba , back. Injured on World Cup duty with France, surgery ruled out in favour of rehabilitation. Arsenal said on July 23 he would miss an extended period. The BBC's estimate is a minimum of two to three months, pointing at October. Jurrien Timber , groin. Underwent a small procedure and is doing individual pitch work. Arteta said on August 10 there were still "a few weeks to go," with a late-September return the realistic target. Ben White , knee. Fully recovered from surgery, back in training since late July, started the Community Shield at right-back. Louie Copley , knee. The under-21 defender suffered a season-ending anterior cruciate ligament injury in the pre-season friendly against Real Betis. Form and the number nine On individual form, the debate that will not go away is Havertz against Gyokeres . Havertz started in Cardiff and scored. Gyokeres came off the bench. The case for the German is the one Arteta has always made, that a centre-forward in this system is a connector as much as a finisher, and Havertz 's passing numbers are considerably better. The case for the Swede is that 14 league goals in a first season in England, at a club that scored 71, is a platform rather than a ceiling. Expect them to share it, and expect the question again in November. The one to watch quietly is Tzolis . Six assists and a goal in six pre-season appearances, then the header that set up Havertz for the second in the Shield, and a body of work at Club Brugge that reads 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. At 34 million pounds, in a market where Chelsea want three times that for Pedro Neto , he already looks like the shrewdest thing Berta has done. Hale End A New Academy, Top to Bottom Mertesacker gone, De Maesschalck in, and a new under-21 head coach appointed yesterday. The pathway that produced Saka and Lewis-Skelly has new management. The most recent piece of news here is the freshest thing in this edition. On Monday, Arsenal confirmed David Horseman as the new under-21 head coach, filling the vacancy created when Max Porter left for Stoke City . It completes a summer of change. Per Mertesacker stepped down as academy manager after eight years, a decision confirmed in January and effective at the end of last season, and has since taken a senior role with the German federation. His replacement started on August 1 with a new job title. Pascal De Maesschalck arrives as Academy Director, rather than academy manager, from a technical director role at Strasbourg and with previous academy stints at Monaco and Club Brugge . Berta cited his "outstanding track record in youth development." He inherits a department with an outstanding recent record for producing first-team players, a rather less outstanding one in the youth leagues themselves, and the perennial problem of holding on to the best fifteen-year-olds in London. The season starts now Competitive football is only now beginning. The under-21s open their EFL Trophy campaign today away at Barnet , in a group that also contains Leyton Orient and AFC Wimbledon , and start their Premier League 2 season at home to Crystal Palace on Saturday. That competition has been restructured again: 31 teams across three tiers, 20 league games each, top 16 into the play-offs. The under-18s started their season on August 15 away at West Bromwich Albion . The names to know, according to Jeorge Bird 's pre-season review published on August 13, are Marli Salmon and Theo Julienne . Salmon , a centre-back who turns 17 later this month, was the second-youngest Englishman ever to appear in the Champions League last season, at 16 years and 103 days. Julienne was described as the biggest winner of pre-season and played 62 minutes at right-back in the first-team friendly against Como at the Emirates on August 12, alongside Josh Ogunnaike , who signed his first professional contract on July 17. And then there is Max Dowman , who is the reason the rest of English football keeps checking the Hale End team sheets. He does not turn 16 until December and is already the youngest player and youngest goalscorer in Premier League history, at 16 years and 73 days for the latter. He scored, assisted and was named man of the match in the pre-season win over Girona on August 1, and he was on the bench in Cardiff on Sunday. He has signed scholarship terms; a professional contract follows when he turns 17. Nine first-year scholars were confirmed for 2026-27, among them Emerson Nwaneri , a midfielder and the younger brother of Ethan , who scored a hat-trick against Chelsea at under-16 level. The one bad piece of academy news is Louie Copley 's cruciate injury, which ends his season before it starts. Loan Watch Unusually thin this year. Two names, both this week. Charles Sagoe Jr , 21, at Kalmar FF in Sweden until January. Scored and assisted against Mjallby, scored again at IFK Goteborg on August 9, then started and played 73 minutes in a 4-0 defeat to Hammarby on Sunday. Ismeal Kabia , 20, joined St Mirren on loan until May 2027 on Saturday and made his debut a day later, playing 59 minutes in a 5-1 Scottish League Cup defeat. Manager Craig McLeish said the club had beaten off competition from Britain and Europe to get him. Arsenal Women Seven In, Six Out, and Three Weeks to Build a Team Renee Slegers has rebuilt half a squad in a summer. La Manga produced a defeat, a first goal for a new signing, and a very welcome sight at centre-back. The most significant thing that happened to Arsenal Women last week was not the result. It was Leah Williamson heading in an equaliser from an Olivia Smith corner in the 46th minute against AC Milan in La Manga on August 13. The England captain spent much of last season managing recurring knee, hamstring and calf problems, and missed the June World Cup qualifiers with a hamstring picked up in rehabilitation. Seeing her rise for a set piece at competitive tempo is the best piece of news of the women's pre-season. The match itself finished 3-2 to Milan , and it ended the Spanish training camp on a sour note. Thea Kyvag put the Italians ahead on 25 minutes after a defensive mix-up, Williamson levelled straight after the break, and Sara Stokic restored the lead around the 70th. Selina Cerci , one of seven summer arrivals, scored her first Arsenal goal with a strike from outside the area before Monica Renzotti won it in stoppage time. New goalkeeper Isabella Damm , signed from Brondby in July, made a smart double save. The rebuild, in full Seven players in, all but one on free transfers: Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona on a four-year deal with an option, Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Cerci from Hoffenheim , and goalkeepers Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid and Damm from Brondby . The exception is Lisa Baum , 19, signed from RB Leipzig for a reported 600,000 euros, understood to be a record fee for a German women's league transfer. The departures cut deeper than the arrivals suggest. Katie McCabe left for Chelsea after ten years and the captaincy. Beth Mead went to Manchester City on a three-year deal. Laia Codina joined West Ham and Victoria Pelova crossed north London to Tottenham . Manuela Zinsberger went to Borussia Dortmund and Rosa Kafaji to London City Lionesses . That is a captain, a European Championship winner and a first-choice goalkeeper out of one dressing room in a single window. What they are rebuilding from Arsenal finished second in the Women's Super League last season, four points behind Manchester City , who won their first title in a decade and ended Chelsea 's six-year run. Second place was secured on the final day with a 3-1 win at Liverpool , Alessia Russo scoring twice. In Europe, the defending champions finished third in the league phase, beat Chelsea 3-2 on aggregate in the quarter-finals and lost the semi-final 4-3 on aggregate to OL Lyonnes . They did add a trophy: the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup, won 3-2 after extra time against Corinthians at the Emirates on February 1, with goals from Olivia Smith , Lotte Wubben-Moy and Caitlin Foord . Slegers herself is secure, having signed an extension understood to run to the summer of 2029. Behind her, set-piece coach Chris Bradley left after two seasons and was replaced on July 31 by Nikita Runnacles , a former Ipswich Town goalkeeper and Brighton assistant, who will also help with goalkeeper coaching. The Season Ahead / Arsenal Women The league. The WSL expands to 14 clubs and 26 matches and begins on September 4. Arsenal open away at Brighton on the 6th. The venue. All thirteen home league fixtures will be played at the Emirates for a second consecutive season, confirmed in May. The audience. Nearly 500,000 tickets sold across all competitions last term, an average league attendance of 34,677, and 17,000 season-ticket holders. Europe. The Women's Champions League draw is on September 4 and Arsenal are in pot one. Gunners Abroad The World Cup Bill Comes Due There is no international break in August. There is, however, a squad still absorbing the cost of a tournament three Arsenal players won. The 2026-27 calendar has no August window, with the next international break falling in September in an extended format. So there are no Arsenal internationals to report on this week. The European calendar is equally quiet: the UEFA Super Cup was played in Salzburg on August 12 between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa , with no Arsenal involvement. What is still shaping the season is the summer that has just finished. Spain won the World Cup on July 19, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time, and three Arsenal players were world champions: David Raya , Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino . A day earlier, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka had played in England's extraordinary 6-4 win over France in the third-place match, a game in which William Saliba lined up on the losing side. The consequences are visible in every team sheet. Raya , Zubimendi and Merino did not return to training until around August 10. Saka and Rice came back late enough that both began the Community Shield on the bench. And Saliba came back with an injury that will cost him the first two months of the title defence. Players from nations eliminated earlier, among them Kai Havertz with Germany, Viktor Gyokeres with Sweden, Piero Hincapie with Ecuador and Gabriel and Martinelli with Brazil, were back in mid to late July and are correspondingly further ahead. Numbers of the Week 25 seconds Time elapsed before Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring in the Community Shield, from a Myles Lewis-Skelly pass. £65m Annual value of the extended Emirates partnership announced on August 6, up from £45m, rising to £75m a year from 2028-29 and running to 2033. 18 Goals Arsenal scored from corners in 2025-26, an all-time Premier League single-season record, beating a mark that had stood for 32 years. 34,677 Arsenal Women's average WSL attendance across nine home league matches at the Emirates last season. All thirteen will be played there in 2026-27. In Brief CHAMPIONS LEAGUE DRAW. Arsenal are in pot one for the 2026-27 league phase, drawn on Thursday, August 27. Matchday one falls between September 8 and 10. Pot one also contains Paris Saint-Germain, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Barcelona, Inter and Atletico Madrid. Liverpool and Manchester City are seeded there as well, but English clubs cannot be drawn against each other. PFA AWARDS. Three Arsenal players are shortlisted for the PFA Players' Player of the Year, announced on August 25: Gabriel Magalhaes, David Raya and Declan Rice. Raya has already collected the Premier League Golden Glove for a third consecutive season, with 19 clean sheets. THE EMIRATES QUESTION. Arsenal have engaged the architects Populous, who designed the current stadium, to study expansion options. Reporting through the spring suggested anything from an additional 5,000 hospitality seats to a full redevelopment towards 80,000. No planning application has been submitted and executives are said to feel no pressure to decide. SHIRT SPONSOR. From 2027-28 the front of the shirt will read simply "Emirates," dropping the "Fly Better" tagline. The new agreement covers the men's, women's and academy teams, training kit and stadium naming rights, and was negotiated by chief commercial officer Juliet Slot, who leaves the club later this year. THE ACCOUNTS. Arsenal's most recently published figures, for the year to May 2025 and released in March, showed record revenue of around £690m against a pre-tax loss of roughly £1m, with a wage bill of £346.8m at just over 50 per cent of turnover. The title and the run to the Champions League final should push the next set higher: the European campaign alone was worth about £123m in UEFA prize money. PRE-SEASON, FOR THE RECORD. Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 and MK Dons, drew 1-1 with Como at the Emirates and won the shoot-out 4-3, and lost to Real Betis 3-1 and Borussia Dortmund 3-2. Then they beat Manchester City 3-0 at Cardiff.
